527	
528	> Portable loopback-proxy helpers. Honors `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` (+ optional `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` for split Clash `socks-port:` configs); otherwise prefers an active Clash config (`mixed-port:` or `port:`/`socks-port:` from `~/.config/clash/config.yaml` or `~/Library/Application Support/clash/config.yaml`) before falling back to probing ports 7890/7891/1087/8118/8080 with `nc -z -w1`. Detection is cached per shell; `proxy-off` and `proxy-refresh` clear that cache before the next lookup. Set `$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1` to auto-export env vars on shell startup. Full guide: [docs/tools/web-reader.md](../tools/web-reader.md). See also: [docs/tools/containers.md](../tools/containers.md) for how `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` feeds the chezmoi-managed `~/.docker/config.json` `proxies.default` block.

```text
1	# Zsh Completions Best Practices
2	
3	How zsh tab completions are organized in this dotfiles project.
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	```
8	compinit runs once (inside oh-my-zsh.sh)
9	        │
10	        ├── ~/.zfunc/                          ← user-generated completions (NOT tracked by chezmoi)
11	        ├── ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/       ← community completions (184 files, cloned by ansible)
12	        │     └── zsh-completions/src/
13	        ├── ~/.docker/completions/             ← Docker-shipped completions
14	        ├── $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/        ← Homebrew-managed completions (via `brew completions link`)
15	        │     └── site-functions/
16	        └── $ZSH/completions/                  ← oh-my-zsh built-in completions
17	```
18	
19	All `fpath` additions are in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` **before** `source "$ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh"`, so `compinit` runs exactly once and picks up everything.
20	
21	## Completion Categories
22	
23	Tools fall into four categories:
24	
25	### A. Self-generating (`tool completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tool`)
26	
27	Most modern CLI tools can output their own completion script. Run once after install, re-run after version upgrades.
28	
29	| Tool | Command |
30	|------|---------|
31	| `uv` | `uv generate-shell-completion zsh` |
32	| `mise` | `mise completion zsh` |
33	| `chezmoi` | `chezmoi completion zsh` |
34	| `just` | `just --completions zsh` |
35	| `bat` | `bat --completion zsh` |
36	| `delta` | `delta --generate-completion zsh` |
37	| `starship` | `starship completions zsh` |
38	| `rg` | `rg --generate complete-zsh` |
39	| `fd` | `fd --gen-completions zsh` |
40	| `zellij` | `zellij setup --generate-completion zsh` |
41	| `sesh` | `sesh completion zsh` |
42	| `pueue` | `pueue completions zsh` |
43	| `docker` | `docker completion zsh` |
44	| `gh` | `gh completion -s zsh` |
45	| `opencode` | `opencode completion zsh` |
46	| `bw` | `bw completion --shell zsh` |
47	
48	**Usage pattern:**
49	
50	```bash
51	# Generate once (or after upgrade)
52	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc
53	uv generate-shell-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_uv
54	mise completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_mise
55	```
56	
57	### B. Pre-bundled (no action needed)
58	
59	Completions ship with the package or via the `zsh-completions` community plugin.
60	
61	| Tool | Source |
62	|------|--------|
63	| `eza` | Homebrew formula installs `_eza` into site-functions |
64	| `git` | oh-my-zsh `git` plugin |
65	| `yazi` | Ships `_yazi` in release assets (also in zsh-completions) |
66	| `lazygit` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
67	| `btop` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
68	| Many others | `zsh-completions` plugin covers 184 tools |
69	
70	### C. Eval/source at startup (shell integration)
71	
72	These tools inject completions as part of broader shell integration. Already handled in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`.
73	
74	| Tool | Where | How |
75	|------|-------|-----|
76	| `fzf` | `tools/10_fzf.zsh` | `source <(fzf --zsh)` |
77	| `zoxide` | `tools/20_zoxide.zsh` | `eval "$(zoxide init zsh)"` |
78	| `thefuck` | `tools/25_thefuck.zsh` | `eval $(thefuck --alias)` |
79	| `direnv` | `tools/30_direnv.zsh` | `eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"` |
80	| `marimo` | `tools/29_marimo.zsh` | `eval "$(_MARIMO_COMPLETE=zsh_source marimo)"` |
81	
82	### D. No completion support
83	
84	`claude`, `gemini`, `btop`, `lazygit` -- no generation command available.
85	
86	### E. Python tools via `shtab` / `tyro`
87	
88	Python CLI frameworks can generate completions:
89	
90	- **[tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/)**: `python my_cli.py --tyro-write-completion zsh ~/.zfunc/_my_cli`
91	- **[shtab](https://github.com/iterative/shtab)**: `shtab --shell=zsh my_module.parser > ~/.zfunc/_my_tool`
92	- **argcomplete**: `register-python-argcomplete tool_name` (uses eval, category C)
93	- **click** (used by mlflow, litellm, etc.): `_TOOL_COMPLETE=zsh_source tool > ~/.zfunc/_tool`
94	
95	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
96	
97	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
98	
99	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
100	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
101	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
102	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
103	
104	### What we DO track
105	
106	- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
107	- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
108	- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
109	- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`
110	
111	## Generating Completions After Fresh Install
112	
113	After `chezmoi apply` on a new machine, most completions already work via `zsh-completions` plugin and Homebrew site-functions. For tools you want **richer/newer completions**, generate them into `~/.zfunc/`:
114	
115	```bash
116	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc
117	
118	# Core tools (always installed)
119	chezmoi completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_chezmoi
120	mise completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_mise
121	uv generate-shell-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_uv
122	just --completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_just
123	starship completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_starship
124	
125	# Dev tools (if installed)
126	command -v gh    && gh completion -s zsh > ~/.zfunc/_gh
127	command -v docker && docker completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_docker
128	command -v rg    && rg --generate complete-zsh > ~/.zfunc/_rg
129	command -v fd    && fd --gen-completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_fd
130	command -v bat   && bat --completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_bat
131	command -v delta && delta --generate-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_delta
132	command -v zellij && zellij setup --generate-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_zellij
133	command -v sesh  && sesh completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_sesh
134	command -v pueue && pueue completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_pueue
135	
136	# Coding agents (if installed)
137	command -v opencode && opencode completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_opencode
138	command -v bw    && bw completion --shell zsh > ~/.zfunc/_bw
139	
140	# Force rebuild completion cache
141	rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit
142	```
143	
144	> **Tip:** You can save this as a script in `~/.local/bin/` or add it to `~/.zshrc.adhoc` as a function.
145	
146	## Priority / Override Order
147	
148	When the same `_tool` file exists in multiple fpath directories, the **first match wins**:
149	
150	```
151	1. ~/.zfunc/                                    (highest - your overrides)
152	2. ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/
153	3. ~/.docker/completions/
154	4. $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/   (Homebrew-managed)
155	5. /usr/share/zsh/*/functions/                  (system, lowest)
156	```
157	
158	Current `dot_zshrc.tmpl` order:
159	
160	```zsh
161	fpath+=~/.zfunc                     # appended (lowest of custom)
162	fpath=(zsh-completions/src $fpath)  # prepended (higher than ~/.zfunc)
163	fpath=(~/.docker/completions $fpath) # prepended (highest of custom)
164	```
165	
166	If you want `~/.zfunc/` to override community completions, change to prepend:
167	
168	```zsh
169	fpath=(~/.zfunc $fpath)  # prepend instead of append
170	```
171	
172	## FAQ
173	
174	**Q: Should I generate completions for tools that `zsh-completions` already covers?**
175	A: Only if you want the latest version. The community plugin may lag behind. For fast-moving tools (uv, mise), generating your own is worthwhile.
176	
177	**Q: A completion file throws errors after I uninstall a tool. What do I do?**
178	A: Remove the file: `rm ~/.zfunc/_toolname`. Stale `_tool` files in fpath are harmless (silently ignored) unless they have syntax errors.
179	
180	**Q: How do I debug completion issues?**
181	A: Run `echo $fpath | tr ' ' '\n'` to see all fpath entries. Use `which _toolname` to see which completion file is being used. Force rebuild with `rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit`.
182
```
</details></tool-use>

 `./docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md`

```text
1	# Linux GUI Apps — packaging mechanisms, this repo's strategy, and how to add a new one
2	
3	Ubuntu has **five** packaging mechanisms for desktop apps. They differ in
4	*where binaries land*, *whether anything keeps them current*, and *how
5	desktop integration (icon, `.desktop`, MIME handlers) gets wired up*.
6	
7	This doc:
8	
9	1. lays out the five mechanisms and the trade-off matrix,
10	2. inventories every GUI app this repo's `gui_apps_linux` ansible role
11	   knows about (plus the snaps you probably installed via Ubuntu App
12	   Center), so you can tell at a glance which path each app is on,
13	3. gives a decision tree for adding a *new* app to the role.
14	
15	## TL;DR — five mechanisms, one trade-off matrix
16	
17	| Mechanism | Auto-update? | Install scope | Desktop integration | Sandbox |
18	|---|---|---|---|---|
19	| **`.deb` w/ apt-source postinst** | ✅ via `apt upgrade` | system-wide (`/usr/share/...`) | ✅ baked in | ❌ |
20	| **`.deb` w/o apt-source postinst** | ❌ manual re-deploy | system-wide | ✅ baked in | ❌ |
21	| **Snap** (Ubuntu App Center) | ✅ `snapd` background daemon | `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` | ✅ baked in | ✅ confined |
22	| **Flatpak** (Flathub) | ✅ `flatpak update` | per-user `~/.var/app/...` | ✅ baked in | ✅ confined |
23	| **AppImage + AppImageLauncher** | ❌ re-download | per-user `~/Applications/` | ✅ via AIL daemon | ❌ |
24	| Cargo / from source | ❌ via `cargo install --force` | per-user `~/.cargo/bin/` | ❌ manual `.desktop` | ❌ |
25	| Tarball / `.tar.xz` | ❌ pure manual | per-user (anywhere) | ❌ manual | ❌ |
26	
27	The **green-checkmark `.deb` row is the gold standard** when upstream
28	provides it. Snap and Flatpak are the auto-update fallbacks for vendors
29	who don't ship `.deb` (or who want sandboxing). AppImage is the
30	last-mile bridge for everyone else.
31	
32	## Priority order on Ubuntu
33	
34	The matrix above is *what each mechanism does*. The list below is *which
35	to pick when you have a choice* — the explicit ordering this repo
36	follows when a vendor ships in multiple formats:
37	
38	1. **`.deb` w/ auto apt-source** — `apt upgrade` keeps it current with zero
39	   sandbox overhead and native startup speed. The right answer for
40	   hot-path apps (editors, terminals, browsers, daily-driver tools).
41	   Examples: Cursor, VSCode, Chrome, Signal, 1Password, Slack.
42	2. **Flatpak (Flathub)** — clean sandbox, cross-distro friendly, faster
43	   to launch than Snap, auto-update via `flatpak update`. Right when
44	   `.deb` is missing or vendor only publishes on Flathub. Default
45	   recommendation for community-packaged apps that need confinement.
46	3. **Snap** — set-and-forget auto-refresh via `snapd` (4×/day, no user
47	   action). Acceptable for non-hot-path apps where the extra ~1-3s
48	   startup penalty is invisible (password manager, music player).
49	   Avoid for hot-path apps; the daily startup cost adds up.
50	4. **AppImage + AppImageLauncher** — when 1-3 are unavailable. No
51	   auto-update unless the bundle ships `.zsync` AND AppImageLauncher's
52	   update check is configured. Re-running our ansible task is the
53	   typical refresh path.
54	5. **Cargo / from-source / tarball** — last resort. Manual everything,
55	   no apt/snap/flatpak update path. Only when upstream really only
56	   ships source.
57	
58	> **Why not "always Snap"?** Snap looks similar to Homebrew Cask on
59	> macOS but the comparison is misleading. Snap apps live in
60	> `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` mounted as squashfs and bring up an AppArmor
61	> sandbox on every launch — Firefox snap takes ~2-3s to boot on SSD
62	> versus ~0.3s for the `.deb`. The sandbox also breaks subtle workflows
63	> by default (snap Bitwarden can't read `~/.ssh` without `snap connect
64	> bitwarden:password-manager-service`; many snaps can't see external
65	> drives). For occasional-use apps these costs are invisible; for
66	> daily drivers (browser, IDE, terminal) they're a real annoyance.
67	> Snap is *fine* — it's just not the universal answer macOS users
68	> sometimes assume from their Cask experience. Pick by row 1-3 above.
69	
70	## Inventory of GUI apps on this machine

75	|---|---|---|---|---|

95	> **Clash for Windows is dead.** The original developer (Fndroid)
96	> publicly stopped maintenance in **2023-11** and the GitHub repo is
97	> archived. No new releases, no CVE patches. Migrate to one of the
98	> maintained forks:
99	>
100	> - [Clash Verge Rev](https://github.com/clash-verge-rev/clash-verge-rev) — active fork, ships .deb + AppImage
101	> - [Clash Nyanpasu](https://github.com/libnyanpasu/clash-nyanpasu) — Tauri-based GUI, AppImage + .deb
102	> - [Mihomo Party](https://github.com/mihomo-party-org/mihomo-party) — successor of CFW UX, AppImage + .deb
103	>
104	> All three publish `.deb` packages — drop the new app into `gui_apps_linux`
105	> following the [`.deb` pattern](#concrete-patterns) below and delete
106	> `~/Documents/ClashForWindows/` after the new one is wired up.
107	
108	## Why `.deb` auto-update works (the apt-source postinst trick)
109	
110	When `dpkg -i cursor_<v>_amd64.deb` runs, Cursor's package contains a
111	`DEBIAN/postinst` script that, on success, writes:
112	
113	- `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/cursor.sources` — pointing at `https://downloads.cursor.com/aptrepo`
114	- `/usr/share/keyrings/anysphere.gpg` — the signing key
115	
116	After that, `apt update` pulls Cursor's release index alongside Ubuntu's
117	own, and `apt upgrade cursor` (or generic `apt upgrade` / `just upgrade-system`)
118	treats it like any other apt package. The user never needs to revisit
119	cursor.com.
120	
121	You can verify this for any installed `.deb`:
122	
123	```sh
124	dpkg -L cursor | grep -E 'sources|keyring'
125	# /etc/apt/sources.list.d/cursor.sources
126	# /usr/share/keyrings/anysphere.gpg
127	```
128	
129	VSCode, Chrome, Signal, 1Password, Slack, Microsoft Edge, Brave all
130	follow this pattern. **Discord does not** — see the next section.
131	
132	## Discord auto-update — why the screenshot keeps appearing
133	
134	Discord's `.deb` does **not** ship a postinst that adds an apt source:
135	
136	```sh
137	dpkg -L discord | grep -E 'sources|keyring'
138	# (empty)
139	```
140	
141	So `apt upgrade` is never aware of new Discord releases. Discord's
142	in-app updater detects the version mismatch, but on Linux it can't
143	actually invoke `dpkg` (no root) — so it pops the *"Must be your lucky
144	day, there's a new update!"* modal with a "Download" button that just
145	opens the vendor download page. You then have to manually `dpkg -i` the
146	new `.deb`.
147	
148	Three ways out:
149	
150	1. **Re-run the ansible task on demand**: `chezmoi apply` (the role
151	   re-fetches the latest `.deb` URL via Discord's API every apply).
152	   This is what we do for Cursor too, so it's consistent.
153	2. **Switch to Flatpak**: `flatpak install flathub com.discordapp.Discord`.
154	   Flatpak auto-updates via `flatpak update`. Loses some native
155	   integration (notifications via XDG portal, screen-share via
156	   PipeWire) but the upgrade story is clean.
157	3. **Switch to Vesktop / WebCord** (community Discord clients with
158	   self-update). Drift from official Discord; not recommended unless
159	   you're already running modded Discord.
160	
161	**This repo's default is option 2 (Flatpak)** — controlled by the
162	`discordChannel` chezmoi prompt (`flatpak | deb | none`, default `flatpak`).
163	The role's flatpak path:
164	
165	1. apt-installs the `flatpak` package if missing (one-time, with sudo)
166	2. adds the Flathub remote at user scope (no sudo)
167	3. installs `com.discordapp.Discord` at user scope (no sudo)
168	
169	To switch from `.deb` to `flatpak` on an existing machine: set
170	`discordChannel = "flatpak"` in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` and run
171	`chezmoi apply --tags gui_apps`. The two installs can coexist briefly
172	(different `.desktop` entries); once you've validated the Flatpak version,
173	`sudo apt remove discord` to clean up the old `.deb`.
174	
175	## Snap (Ubuntu App Center) — what's actually happening
176	
177	The Ubuntu App Center is a GTK frontend for `snapd` — Canonical's
178	universal package manager that ships `.snap` archives from the Snap
179	Store. When you install **Bitwarden** or **Spotify** from App Center:
180	
181	- The `.snap` file is extracted to `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` (versioned,
182	  read-only)
183	- A symlink `/snap/<app>/current` always points at the active rev
184	- A wrapper script at `/snap/bin/<app>` is what `$PATH` actually picks up
185	- A user-systemd service `snapd.refresh.service` checks for updates
186	  ~4× per day and applies them in the background
187	- Desktop integration (`/var/lib/snapd/desktop/applications/<app>.desktop`)
188	  is auto-generated; the snap-store daemon updates these on refresh
189	
190	This means **Bitwarden Desktop and Spotify will keep themselves up to
191	date with no manual action** — the same way `apt upgrade` doesn't run
192	automatically but apt-source `.deb`s are kept current via your existing
193	`just upgrade-system` cadence, snaps are kept current via `snapd`'s
194	*always-on* refresh daemon. Different paradigm, same end result.
195	
196	To inspect: `snap list`, `snap info <app>`, `snap refresh --list`
197	(pending updates), `snap refresh <app>` (force-refresh now), `snap
198	revert <app>` (rollback to previous rev — neat property of the
199	versioned `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` layout).
200	
201	> Caveat: snaps run in a confinement sandbox, which can break power-user
202	> workflows (no access to `~/.ssh` by default for example). Most desktop
203	> apps work fine; CLI tools sometimes don't. Prefer `.deb` or apt
204	> when both options exist.
205	
206	## AppImage + AppImageLauncher — the catch-all
207	
208	When upstream ships only an AppImage (Zen Browser, Cursor's old AppImage,
209	many indie tools), our convention is:
210	
211	1. **Stable filename**: drop the file at `~/Applications/<app>.AppImage`
212	   (no version or hash in the name). Re-runs of the ansible task just
213	   overwrite it. Files like `zen-x86_64_fe71259e...AppImage` (old hash
214	   suffix in filename) are the wrong shape — they accumulate forever.
215	2. **Executable bit**: `mode: '0755'` in the ansible task.
216	3. **AppImageLauncher integration**: `appimagelauncherd.service` (user
217	   systemd unit, set up by our role) watches `~/Applications/`. New
218	   AppImages trigger a first-run modal: *"Integrate or Run once?"* —
219	   integrating extracts the icon, generates a `.desktop` entry under
220	   `~/.local/share/applications/`, and (optionally) moves the file to
221	   AppImageLauncher's canonical location.
222	
223	For our managed AppImages we usually skip the modal by writing the
224	`.desktop` entry ourselves in the same ansible task — see Zen Browser.
225	For AppImages you drop manually (Frpc Desktop), let the modal handle it.
226	
227	To check the daemon: `systemctl --user status appimagelauncherd`.
228	Manual integration: `ail-cli integrate ~/Applications/foo.AppImage`.
229	
230	## Adding a new GUI app to `gui_apps_linux`
231	
232	```
233	Does upstream publish a .deb?
234	├─ YES → Does the .deb add an apt source (check `dpkg -L <pkg> | grep sources` after install)?
235	│        ├─ YES → use the .deb. Ansible installs once, apt keeps current. ★ best path
236	│        └─ NO  → use the .deb anyway, BUT add a refresh hook to
237	│                 `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` so `just upgrade-system`
238	│                 re-fetches latest. (Discord pattern.)
239	│
240	├─ NO ── Does upstream publish on Snap or Flatpak with FIRST-PARTY support?
241	│        ├─ Official Snap → use snap (community.general.snap module).
242	│        │                 Cleanest auto-update on Ubuntu, but confined.
243	│        ├─ Official Flathub → use flatpak (community.general.flatpak module).
244	│        │                    Cross-distro friendly, also confined.
245	│        └─ Community-only → skip; AppImage probably more reliable.
246	│
247	└─ Only AppImage / tarball?
248	   ├─ AppImage → drop in ~/Applications/ as <app>.AppImage. AIL integrates.
249	   └─ tarball  → ~/Applications/<app>/ + wrapper script + manual .desktop.
250	                 ⚠️ Last resort — no auto-update path, manual everything.
251	```
252	
253	### Concrete patterns
254	
255	**`.deb` pattern** — see "Install Cursor via .deb" in
256	[`gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml).
257	Two-step:
258	
259	1. `ansible.builtin.uri` — fetch vendor's API to resolve the latest
260	   `.deb` URL (return JSON, parse `debUrl` or similar field).
261	2. `ansible.builtin.get_url` — download the `.deb`, with `force: true`
262	   (overwrite stale files from prior apply) and `until: cursor_dl is
263	   succeeded` + `retries: 4` + `delay: 5` (GFW-region CDN drops).
264	3. `ansible.builtin.apt: deb=<path>` — install. Postinst handles apt
265	   source if vendor ships one.
266	4. Wrap the whole block in `rescue:` that prints a manual-fallback URL.
267	
268	**AppImage pattern** — see "Install Zen Browser AppImage" in the same
269	file. Three-step:
270	
271	1. `ansible.builtin.uri` — GitHub releases API (or vendor equivalent)
272	   to resolve the asset URL.
273	2. `selectattr('name', 'match', '^<prefix>-<arch>\\.AppImage$')` filter
274	   to pick the right asset for `target_architecture` (already normalized
275	   to `x86_64` / `aarch64` by the `Set target_architecture from dpkg` task
276	   in [`linux.yml`](../../dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml)).
277	3. `ansible.builtin.get_url` to `~/Applications/<app>.AppImage` with
278	   `mode: '0755'` and a stable filename.
279	4. Write a `.desktop` entry under `~/.local/share/applications/` using
280	   `ansible.builtin.copy` with a `content:` literal — the file gets
281	   merged into the system menu via `update-desktop-database`.
282	
283	**Snap pattern** — none yet in this repo. Template:
284	
285	```yaml
286	- name: Install Bitwarden Desktop via Snap
287	  community.general.snap:
288	    name: bitwarden
289	    state: present
290	    classic: false   # most apps are confined; set true only when vendor docs say so
291	  become: true
292	```
293	
294	**Flatpak pattern** — none yet. Template:
295	
296	```yaml
297	- name: Install Discord via Flatpak (instead of .deb)
298	  community.general.flatpak:
299	    name: com.discordapp.Discord
300	    state: present
301	    remote: flathub  # add `community.general.flatpak_remote` first if missing
302	    method: user     # per-user install; `system` requires root
303	```
304	
305	Always add a `rescue:` block that points the user at the manual
306	fallback URL (cursor.com / discord.com / GitHub release page) so a
307	failed automated install isn't a dead end.
308	
309	## Cross-references
310

312	- [`docs/this_repo/upgrades.md`](../this_repo/upgrades.md) — the install-vs-upgrade split: why `chezmoi apply` doesn't bump versions, what `just upgrade-*` covers, where each package manager fits in.
313	- [`dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) — the actual ansible role, with the patterns you'd copy when adding a new app.

1	# Development Workflow — "Only type where you're going"
2	
3	The end-to-end flow for picking up a project, jumping between worktrees, and
4	running parallel AI coding agents — without memorising helper function names.
5	
6	This doc is the **index**. For deep dives see
7	[`docs/tools/sesh.md`](../tools/sesh.md) (picker, layouts, sesh config),
8	[`docs/tools/worktrunk.md`](../tools/worktrunk.md) (worktrees, parallel agents,
9	hooks), and [`docs/tools/tmux/`](../tools/tmux/) (panes, popup menu, theme).
10	
11	---
12	
13	## TL;DR — one key per intent
14	
15	| Intent | Key | Where the key lives |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| Switch project / open a new one | `Alt+S` (outside tmux) or `prefix+g` (inside) | `smart-picker.sh` |
18	| Switch branch within current project | inside the picker → `Ctrl+W` worktrees | `smart-picker.sh` |
19	| Spin up a new parallel branch + agent | `wt cc <branch> -- '<prompt>'` | [`worktrunk.md`](../tools/worktrunk.md#per-worktree-claude--opencode) |
20	| Peek at sibling worktree (no session swap) | `wtcd` (fzf-tmux picker) | [`worktrunk.md`](../tools/worktrunk.md#the-wtcd-rationale) |
21	| Refresh coding-agent layout on current repo | `scode` (manual override) | [`sesh.md`](../tools/sesh.md) |
22	
23	Everything else is explained by these five rows.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## The one keystroke
28	
29	- **Outside tmux** (plain zsh prompt): `Alt+S`
30	- **Inside tmux**: `prefix + g`
31	
32	Both open the same fzf popup. Same hotkeys, same behaviour, same dispatch
33	logic. The only difference is that outside-tmux spawns a fresh tmux client,
34	inside-tmux uses `switch-client` — handled by `sesh connect` and
35	`_sesh_attach_or_switch` transparently.
36	
37	### Filter modes inside the picker
38	
39	```
40	 ^a all         sesh list --icons
41	 ^t tmux        active tmux sessions only
42	 ^g configs     configured sesh sessions (from sesh.toml)
43	 ^x zoxide      zoxide frecency dirs  ← "type where I've been before"
44	 ^w worktrees   worktrees of the current repo  ← the worktrunk combo
45	 ^f find        fd walk from $HOME (depth 2)  ← when zoxide doesn't know yet
46	 ^d kill        kill the session under cursor, reload list
47	```
48	
49	Hit the hotkey → the list reloads with that source. Type to fuzzy-filter.
50	Enter to dispatch.
51	
52	### What happens on Enter — smart dispatch
53	
54	The picker doesn't ask "which layout?" — it decides based on what you picked.
55	
56	| Selection shape | Dispatch |
57	|---|---|
58	| Existing tmux session name | `sesh connect <name>` → switch/attach |
59	| Path inside a git repo (`.git` dir exists) | `scode -p <path>` → **coding-agent layout** (nvim 75% + agent 25% + btop window) |
60	| Path *not* inside a git repo | `sesh connect <path>` → plain session (wildcard patterns in `sesh.toml` still win if the path matches one) |
61	| Configured sesh session name | `sesh connect <name>` → honours `startup_command` |
62	
63	The rule in one sentence: **git repo = scode layout; everything else =
64	sesh's default**. No second menu, no remembering which helper to type.
65	
66	### When to override the smart rule
67	
68	The picker is opinionated. If you want something else, skip the picker and
69	call the helper directly — all four remain available:
70	
71	- `shere` — plain shell at `$PWD`, no editor, no git requirement
72	- `sroot` — honours `sesh.toml` wildcards and `default_session.startup_command`
73	- `scode` — coding-agent layout (requires git repo)
74	- `svibe` — parametric multi-agent layout (requires git repo)
75	
76	See [`docs/tools/sesh.md`](../tools/sesh.md) for the full helper spec.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## Sesh + worktrunk — three orthogonal axes
81	
82	Stolen from [`docs/tools/worktrunk.md`](../tools/worktrunk.md#mental-model)
83	because it's the mental model that makes the whole flow click:
84	
85	| Axis | Tool | Granularity | What the picker shows |
86	|---|---|---|---|
87	| **Project** | `sesh` | One per repo | `^t` + `^g` + `^x` filters |
88	| **Branch** | `wt` (worktrunk) | One per parallel task in a project | `^w` filter |
89	| **Pane** | `tmux` | Editor / agent / logs / git | — (the layout inside the session) |
90	
91	Picker = axes 1 and 2 in one popup. Worktrunk's own `wt switch` / `wtcd` /
92	`wt cc` still exist — reach for them when you want to *create* a worktree
93	or *run hooks*. The picker is for *jumping* to one that exists.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## Decision tree — which tool for which moment
98	
99	```
100	Am I starting from scratch (no session for this project yet)?
101	├── Project I use often           → Alt+S / prefix+g, type name, hit Enter
102	├── Project I haven't used before → Alt+S / prefix+g → ^f (find) → pick → Enter
103	└── Brand new empty dir           → cd there → shere (skips git check)
104	
105	Am I already in a session for this project?
106	├── Want to jump to a sibling worktree  → Alt+S / prefix+g → ^w → pick
107	├── Want to just peek at one (no swap)  → wtcd
108	├── Want to spin up a fresh branch + Claude agent → wt cc <branch> -- '<prompt>'
109	└── Want to see all worktrees' agent progress     → wt list
110	
111	Am I wrapping up?
112	├── Branch ready to merge       → wt merge main
113	├── Branch rejected / scratch   → wt remove
114	└── Session no longer needed    → Alt+S / prefix+g → ^t → ^d to kill
115	```
116	
117	---
118	
119	## Why this reduces memorisation burden
120	
121	Before: four helper functions (`shere` / `sroot` / `scode` / `svibe`), three
122	worktrunk commands (`wt switch` / `wt cc` / `wtcd`), and a sesh picker that
123	created *wrong* layouts for zoxide-picked repos. Seven names to remember,
124	plus the wrong default.
125	
126	After: two keys (`Alt+S` and `prefix+g` — same behaviour either way) cover
127	every "I want to go somewhere" case. The picker auto-picks the coding-agent
128	layout for git repos so you never have to type `scode` for the common case.
129	`wt cc` / `wtcd` / `wt merge` are still the right tools for *creating* and
130	*cleaning up* — but for *navigating*, one key is enough.
131	
132	---
133	
134	## Gotchas
135	
136	- **The picker's `^w` only lists worktrees of the current directory's repo.**
137	  Outside any repo it returns an empty list. This is deliberate for the MVP;
138	  cross-project worktree enumeration would need a known-projects list and
139	  doesn't earn its complexity yet.
140	- **Smart dispatch uses `.git` directory existence.** A non-git dir that
141	  happens to match a sesh wildcard (e.g. `/Volumes/Data/Program/foo/bar`
142	  which has no `.git`) will get the wildcard's layout, *not* scode. If you
143	  want scode, call `scode -p <path>` directly.
144	- **`scode` is called via `zsh -ic` from the bash picker script.** Means a
145	  fresh zsh sources your zshrc once per picker-enter. Fast enough
146	  (~50–150ms) but not instant. If you see lag, it's the zshrc, not sesh.
147	- **Outside tmux**, picking anything replaces your current shell with
148	  `tmux attach-session`. Ctrl-B d to get back. No way around this — tmux's
149	  own design.

# 基礎架構與虛擬化參考

!!! note "Terminology rule (zh-TW pages)"
    技術名詞首次出現以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現，例：依賴注入
    (dependency injection)。**不自創翻譯**——若無公認譯名直接保留英文
    （如 `embedding`、`tokenizer`）。代碼、API 名、CLI flag、套件名、檔名一律不翻。

虛擬化 (virtualization)、共享儲存 (shared storage)、多使用者運算排程，以及共享家目錄身分驗證 (shared-home identity) 等模式的參考筆記。**僅為文件** —— 此資料夾內容皆不會由 chezmoi 安裝。這是「當你已經不再只用筆電」之後的知識庫。

## 此資料夾涵蓋（與不涵蓋）的範圍

| 範圍 | 在此資料夾？ | 由 chezmoi 安裝？ |
|-------|-----------------|-----------------------|
| 裸機虛擬化作業系統 (Proxmox / ESXi / XCP-ng) | 是（參考） | 否 —— 這些是主機作業系統，不是應用程式 |
| 桌面 VM 管理工具 (OrbStack、UTM、VirtualBox、Fusion) | 是（參考） | 僅 OrbStack，透過 [dot_ansible/roles/docker/tasks/main.yml](../../dot_ansible/roles/docker/tasks/main.yml) |
| 叢集共享儲存 (CephFS、BeeGFS、Lustre、NFS) | 是（參考） | 否 —— 多節點叢集議題 |
| 多使用者運算排程 (SLURM、K8s、Nomad) | 是（參考） | 否 —— 叢集營運議題 |
| 身分驗證與共享家目錄 (FreeIPA、LDAP、SSSD) | 是（參考） | 否 —— 組織專屬 |
| 個人開發筆電工具（編輯器、CLI、dotfiles） | 否 —— 請見 [docs/tools/](../tools/) | 是 —— 本 repo 的主要目的 |

如果你想知道「我要怎麼在 MacBook 上跑一個 VM？」 —— 答案是 OrbStack（已預裝），請見 [virtualization.md](virtualization.md#desktop-vm-managers)。如果你問的是「我們團隊要怎麼建立一個共用運算叢集？」 —— 此資料夾勾勒出大致的版圖，但實際建置是另一個獨立的營運專案。

## 決策樹

\```mermaid
flowchart TD
    startNode["我需要某處的運算或儲存資源"] --> q1{規模}
    q1 -->|筆電上的單一 VM| laptop["virtualization.md#desktop-vm-managers"]
    q1 -->|幾台伺服器 / 家用實驗室| hypervisor["virtualization.md#type-1-bare-metal-hypervisors"]
    q1 -->|多使用者叢集| cluster{要解決什麼問題？}
    cluster -->|跨節點共享檔案| storage["shared-storage.md"]
    cluster -->|將工作排程到節點| sched["compute-scheduling.md"]
    cluster -->|單一登入 + 各處同一 UID| identity["shared-home-identity.md"]
\```

## 內容

| 文件 | 涵蓋內容 |
|-----|----------------|
| [virtualization.md](virtualization.md) | 桌面 VM 管理工具 (OrbStack、UTM、VirtualBox、Fusion、Lima、libvirt)、type-1 hypervisor (Proxmox VE、ESXi、XCP-ng、Harvester、Nutanix)、K8s 原生 VM (KubeVirt)。包含明確的 OrbStack 與 Proxmox 對照。 |
| [shared-storage.md](shared-storage.md) | CephFS、BeeGFS、Lustre、GlusterFS、MooseFS / SeaweedFS / JuiceFS、NFSv4、Samba。依工作負載分類的決策矩陣與 client 端掛載範例。 |
| [compute-scheduling.md](compute-scheduling.md) | SLURM、Kubernetes + Kueue/Volcano、Nomad、HTCondor、OpenPBS、YARN、Mesos、Ray/Dask、OpenStack Nova、Proxmox HA。涵蓋多使用者 CPU/GPU/VM 配置。 |
| [shared-home-identity.md](shared-home-identity.md) | FreeIPA、389ds、OpenLDAP、Samba AD、SSSD、autofs 家目錄掛載、UID/GID 慣例。「所有人的 `$HOME` 都放在 NAS 上」這個經典模式。 |

## 各層如何組合

典型的多使用者 Linux 運算叢集大致堆疊如下：

\```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph compute["運算層"]
        scheduler["排程器 (SLURM / K8s / Nomad)"]
        nodes["Worker 節點"]
        scheduler --> nodes
    end
    subgraph storage["儲存層"]
        cephbeegfs["共享 FS (CephFS / BeeGFS / NFS)"]
    end
    subgraph identity["身分驗證層"]
        ipa["FreeIPA / LDAP + Kerberos"]
        sssd["每個節點上的 SSSD"]
    end
    subgraph virt["虛擬化層（選用）"]
        hyp["Proxmox / ESXi / KVM"]
        vms["承載 worker 節點的 VM"]
        hyp --> vms
    end
    vms -.-> nodes
    nodes -->|掛載 /home, /scratch| cephbeegfs
    nodes -->|認證| sssd
    sssd -->|LDAP/KRB| ipa
\```

依規模獨立挑選每一層：

- **單一使用者筆電**：只有「運算層」（直接用你的筆電，或許搭配 OrbStack 開些用完即丟的 VM）
- **小型團隊（5-20 人）**：加上 NFS + FreeIPA。排程器選用。
- **HPC / ML 研究實驗室（50+ 人）**：加上 Proxmox 或裸機 + BeeGFS/Lustre + SLURM + FreeIPA
- **現代雲原生 (cloud-native)**：以 Kubernetes 取代 SLURM、以 CephFS + CSI 取代 NFS、保留 FreeIPA 處理 SSH/sudo 身分

## 本 repo 內相關文件

- [docs/tools/containers.md](../tools/containers.md) —— 容器執行階段 (container runtime)（Docker / OrbStack / Podman）營運筆記
- [docs/tools/container-config-map.md](../tools/container-config-map.md) —— 「哪個工具讀哪份 Docker 設定檔」對照表
- [docs/tools/infrastructure-as-code.md](../tools/infrastructure-as-code.md) —— 用 Azure CLI / Terraform / OpenTofu 來佈建本資料夾所討論的基礎架構
- [docs/tools/networking.md](../tools/networking.md) —— 網路 CLI 工具

1	# Repo architecture & install flow
2	
3	How `chezmoi apply` deploys configs and triggers ansible / brew on this machine.
4	
5	## Layout
6	
7	```
8	chezmoi repo/
9	├── dot_* files               → ~/.* (config files)
10	├── dot_ansible/              → ~/.ansible/ (ansible playbooks)
11	├── run_once_before_*.tmpl    → bootstrap (runs once)
12	└── run_onchange_after_*.tmpl → ansible (runs on changes)
13	```
14	
15	## Install order
16	
17	1. **Bootstrap** (`run_once_before`) — installs Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, ansible, mise.
18	2. **`chezmoi apply`** — deploys config files + ansible playbooks.
19	3. **Ansible** (`run_onchange_after`) — runs on fresh install + when roles change.
20	4. **Brew bundle** (`run_onchange_after`) — installs GUI apps when enabled.
21	
22	## Auto-run scripts
23	
24	| Script | Behavior |
25	|--------|----------|
26	| `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` | Installs Homebrew (macOS and Linux), uv, mise, ansible |
27	| `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` | Runs ansible with all tags |
28	| `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl` | Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps`, or on macOS if `installAiDesktopApps`) |
29	
30	The onchange script includes SHA256 hashes of all role files. It runs on **fresh install** (no previous hash state) and on **updates** (any role's `tasks/main.yml` or `defaults/main.yml` changes).
31	
32	To force re-run all scripts:
33	
34	```bash
35	chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=scriptState
36	chezmoi apply
37	```
38	
39	See [sudo-session.md](sudo-session.md) for the shared sudo cache used by all three run-scripts.
40	
41	## Externals (`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`)
42	
43	Upstream git repos / single-file downloads that used to be cloned by Ansible are declared in `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` at the repo root. chezmoi fetches them during `chezmoi apply` and re-pulls weekly (`refreshPeriod = "168h"`):
44	
45	- oh-my-zsh core + 4 custom plugins (`zsh-autosuggestions`, `zsh-syntax-highlighting`, `zsh-completions`, `zsh-vi-mode`)
46	- TPM (tmux plugin manager, `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm`)
47	- fzf git source (Linux only, `~/.fzf`; apt version lacks `--zsh`)
48	- toolkami.rb (`~/.local/share/toolkami/toolkami.rb`)
49	
50	```bash
51	chezmoi apply                          # normal: pull if older than 168h
52	chezmoi apply --refresh-externals      # force: pull every external now
53	```
54	
55	Ansible retains only the post-clone steps externals can't do:
56	
57	- `zsh` role — install `zsh` package + change login shell.
58	- `devtools` role — run `tpm/bin/install_plugins` once (sentinel: `~/.tmux/plugins/.ansible-installed`).
59	- `lazyvim_deps` role — run `~/.fzf/install --bin` (idempotent via `creates:`).
60	
61	**When to add an entry here vs Ansible**: use `.chezmoiexternal` when the content is a plain clone / single file and the only conditional is `.chezmoi.os`. Keep things in Ansible when they need arch / `noRoot` / `armv7l` logic, dynamic version paths, or `become: true`. Full schema notes: [chezmoi-prefixes.md → Companion file: `.chezmoiexternal.<format>`](../tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md#companion-file-chezmoiexternalformat).
62	
63	## Ansible vs Homebrew
64	
65	**Primary tool: Ansible** — manages CLI tools and system dependencies cross-platform.
66	
67	| Tool | Role | When to Use |
68	|------|------|-------------|
69	| **Ansible** | CLI tools, system packages | Always (apt/brew formulas) |
70	| **Brewfile** | macOS GUI apps (casks), App Store | Optional (opt-in) |
71	| **Linuxbrew** | Linux packages not in apt | Always installed on Linux |
72	
73	Bootstrap installs Homebrew on both macOS and Linux. Ansible roles use `community.general.homebrew` for macOS formulas. Brewfile manages casks (GUI apps) and mas (App Store) separately. On Linux, Ansible uses apt; Linuxbrew is available for newer packages.
74	
75	Deeper comparison of Linux package sources (apt / snap / Linuxbrew / GitHub binaries) and the policy ansible roles follow: [docs/linux-package-sources.md](../linux-package-sources.md).
76	
77	## Ansible usage
78	
79	Ansible playbooks run automatically via `chezmoi apply` when playbook files change. For manual runs, use `~/.ansible/`:
80	
81	```bash
82	cd ~/.ansible
83	
84	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml                    # Full setup (macOS)
85	ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml                    # Full setup (Linux)
86	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --tags "neovim"    # Specific tags only
87	ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml --skip-tags "sudo" # Skip sudo tasks
88	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --check            # Dry run
89	```
90	
91	After modifying playbooks/roles, syntax check:
92	
93	```bash
94	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/base.yml
95	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/macos.yml
96	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml
97	```
98	
99	Or use `just ansible-syntax-check`.

146	## No-root mode (Linux)
147	
148	For Linux servers without sudo/root access, enable `noRoot = true` during `chezmoi init`:
149	
150	```bash
151	chezmoi init --force  # Answer "y" to "No sudo/root access" prompt
152	```
153	
154	This skips all tasks tagged with `[sudo]` (apt packages, system-level installations). Tools with user-level fallbacks are automatically installed to `~/.local/bin`.
155	
156	**User-level tools** (installed automatically without sudo):
157	
158	- **GitHub binaries**: neovim, ripgrep, fd, jq, just, bat, bats, eza, delta, yazi, superfile, zellij, btop, gitleaks, lazygit, fzf, sesh, taplo, television
159	- **tmux-appimage** (x86_64 only): extracted AppImage → `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/squashfs-root`, shim at `~/.local/bin/tmux`. Runs only when system `tmux` is older than 3.3.
160	- **mise**: Node.js, Rust runtime management
161	- **Installers**: zoxide, starship, thefuck, tldr
162	- **cargo tools**: pueue
163	- **uv tools**: `pre-commit` (pinned to `--python 3.13`, see [docs/tools/pre-commit.md](../tools/pre-commit.md)), mlflow, sqlit-tui, tmuxp
164	- **llm tools**: ollama, litellm, llmfit, models
165	- **npm tools**: Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Bitwarden CLI
166	
167	**What you won't get without root**: zsh (needs `/etc/shells`), htop, direnv (apt only), Docker, Ollama service, system fonts, ruby + gem tools, build-essential / git / curl / wget / tree (assumed pre-installed).
168	
169	**Tip**: ask sysadmin to run `sudo apt install git curl wget zsh tmux htop direnv build-essential tree`.
170	
171	## ARM / Raspberry Pi support
172	
173	Raspberry Pi 5 (64-bit OS only) works with the `ubuntu_server` profile and gets full tool support. Raspberry Pi 4 may run 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS (armhf userland) with a 64-bit kernel (`arm_64bit=1` default), which causes `uname -m` to report `aarch64` while userland is 32-bit.
174	
175	**How it's handled:**
176	
177	- **Bootstrap** detects userland architecture via `dpkg --print-architecture`; skips Linuxbrew on armhf (Homebrew requires amd64 or arm64 userland).
178	- **Ansible playbooks** (`linux.yml`) override `ansible_architecture` in `pre_tasks` to match real userland (e.g. `armv7l` instead of `aarch64`), so roles download correct binaries.
179	- **Tool availability on armhf**: apt packages work fine; GitHub release downloads are skipped for tools without armv7l builds.
180	
181	**Tools with armv7l/armhf releases** (work on RPi 4 32-bit): ripgrep, fd, jq, glow, rclone, direnv, gitleaks, trippy, speedtest, bats.
182	
183	**Tools skipped on armv7l** (no 32-bit ARM release): neovim (GitHub tarball), lazygit, eza, git-delta, yazi, superfile, zellij, sesh, taplo, television, duckdb, doggo, gping, bandwhich, SpecStory, CodexBar, Claude Code (install.sh ships arm64/amd64 only).
184	
185	**Skipped via mise on armv7l**: bun, ruby; node pinned to `node@20` (last LTS with armv7l tarball). npm-based tools install via `mise exec -- npm`. tree-sitter-cli skipped (cargo build needs libclang, takes 15+ min on RPi 4).
186	
187	**Recommendation**: use 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS for full tool compatibility.
188	
189	## Brewfile (GUI apps, opt-in)
190	
191	GUI applications managed via Homebrew Brewfile in `~/.config/homebrew/`. Installation is **opt-in** (disabled by default): enable via `chezmoi init --force` and set `installBrewApps = true`. On macOS, AI desktop apps are a separate opt-in via `installAiDesktopApps = true`.
192	
193	```
194	~/.config/homebrew/
195	├── Brewfile          # Shared: taps, CLI formulas, mas
196	├── Brewfile.darwin   # macOS: casks (GUI apps), mas entries
197	└── Brewfile.linux    # Linux: linuxbrew-specific (minimal)
198	```
199	
200	```bash
201	chezmoi edit ~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin       # Edit
202	brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile        # Apply manually
203	brew bundle check --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin  # Check
204	chezmoi apply                                         # Or trigger via run_onchange
205	```
206	
207	**Categories (darwin)**: terminals & editors (alacritty, iterm2, warp, cmux, cursor, vscode), AI & coding (claude, chatgpt, opencode-desktop, antigravity, codex-app on Apple Silicon, ollama-app gated on `installAiDesktopApps` + `installLlmTools`), system utilities (aerospace, alt-tab, raycast, jordanbaird-ice), communication (discord, telegram, wechat, tencent-meeting), browsers (arc, google-chrome, tor-browser), productivity (obsidian, google-drive, grammarly-desktop), gaming (steam, minecraft, battle-net — skipped if `WORK_MACHINE` env set), finance (binance, tradingview), network (tailscale, openvpn-connect, clash-verge-rev), Mac App Store (LINE, Keynote, Numbers, Pages).
208	
209	**Conditional sections** (Brewfiles are chezmoi templates):
210	
211	- Gaming apps: skipped if `WORK_MACHINE` is set.
212	- Chinese apps (baidunetdisk): only included if `useChineseMirror` is true.
213	- mas apps: requires signing in to App Store.app first.
214
```

```text
1	# `bootstrap.sh` — first-touch entry for a new machine
2	
3	The repo's one-liner installer:
4	
5	```bash
6	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | bash
7	```
8	
9	does just three things (the script itself is ~75 lines, mostly logging):
10	
11	1. **Install [`uv`](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv)** if missing (Astral's
12	   installer → `~/.local/bin/uv`).
13	2. **Reattach stdin to `/dev/tty`** so [`questionary`](https://github.com/tmbo/questionary)
14	   prompts inside `dotfiles_init.py` can read keystrokes (otherwise the curl
15	   pipe would steal stdin and the wrapper would silently fall back to
16	   non-interactive stubs).
17	3. **`exec uv run --script <URL>`** — fetches
18	   [`scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`](../../scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py)
19	   over HTTPS, resolves its PEP 723 inline deps (`questionary`, `rich`, `tyro`)
20	   into an ephemeral venv, runs it. No global pip install, no `pyproject.toml`.
21	
22	`bootstrap.sh` is in [`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiignore.tmpl) — `chezmoi
23	apply` does **not** deploy it to `$HOME/bootstrap.sh`.
24	
25	## "It's been 5 minutes and there's no output — is it stuck?"
26	
27	Most likely the wrapper is downloading something silently. Three layers can
28	each take 30 s – several minutes on a slow / throttled network with **zero
29	visible output**:
30	
31	| Layer | What's happening | How to confirm |
32	|---|---|---|
33	| `curl https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh \| sh` | Downloading the `uv` binary tarball from GitHub Releases | `pgrep -af 'uv\|curl\|install.sh'` |
34	| `uv run --script <URL>` (deps stage) | Resolving + downloading `questionary`/`rich`/`tyro` wheels from PyPI; building any sdists | `lsof -p $(pgrep -f dotfiles_init) -i \| head` |
35	| `chezmoi init` (after prompts) | `git clone` the dotfiles repo (~MBs of submodules, agent skills, etc.) over HTTPS / SSH | `pgrep -af 'git\|chezmoi'` |
36	
37	### Diagnose without killing the run
38	
39	In **another shell** on the same machine:
40	
41	```bash
42	# 1) see the full process tree under bootstrap
43	echo "=== process tree ==="
44	pgrep -af 'bootstrap|dotfiles_init|uv|chezmoi|ansible|brew|apt|git'
45	
46	# 2) what is the leaf doing right now?
47	LEAF=$(pgrep -f 'dotfiles_init|chezmoi|ansible' | tail -1)
48	[ -n "$LEAF" ] && {
49	  ps -p "$LEAF" -o pid,ppid,etime,stat,command
50	  lsof -p "$LEAF" 2>/dev/null -i | head -10        # network sockets
51	  lsof -p "$LEAF" 2>/dev/null -p "$LEAF" | grep REG | tail -10  # files being read
52	}
53	
54	# 3) which remote is slow?
55	for url in https://astral.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com \
56	           https://pypi.org https://github.com https://get.chezmoi.io; do
57	  printf '%-40s ' "$url"
58	  curl -fsS --max-time 5 -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code}  %{time_total}s\n' "$url" \
59	    || echo 'TIMEOUT/FAIL'
60	done
61	```
62	
63	Common patterns:
64	
65	- **`curl` to `astral.sh` taking >30 s** → GFW; set `https_proxy` (see below).
66	- **`uv` process exists but has no TCP socket** → resolver is CPU-bound on a
67	  big sdist build (rare for these three deps; usually means a transitive
68	  pulled in something heavy). Wait it out or run with `DOTFILES_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE=1`.
69	- **`git-remote-https` / `git-remote-ssh` child** → `chezmoi init` is cloning;
70	  GFW slowness is normal here.
71	- **Python process in `select()` with no children** → it's waiting for
72	  keyboard input. The TTY reattach failed; kill and re-run from a real
73	  terminal (not over a non-PTY SSH session).
74	
75	### Verbose mode
76	
77	Re-run with progress output everywhere:
78	
79	```bash
80	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh \
81	  | DOTFILES_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE=1 bash
82	```
83	
84	That sets `set -x` in `bootstrap.sh`, prints timestamped stage logs, and adds
85	`uv run --verbose` so you see every wheel download / venv operation.
86	
87	## Skipping `bootstrap.sh` entirely (recommended on slow networks)
88	
89	Once you've cloned the repo locally, you don't need the curl-piped bootstrap
90	at all — call the wrapper script directly via the `just` recipe:
91	
92	```bash
93	git clone https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles ~/.local/share/chezmoi
94	cd ~/.local/share/chezmoi
95	
96	just bootstrap-local                 # interactive (same as bootstrap.sh)
97	just bootstrap-local-verbose         # shows uv resolver progress
98	
99	# Pass through args after `--`:
100	just bootstrap-local -- --yes --bundle minimal     # non-interactive
101	just bootstrap-local -- doctor                     # schema parity check
102	just bootstrap-local -- list-bundles               # see all bundles
103	```
104	
105	Advantages:
106	
107	- **No `raw.githubusercontent.com` round-trip** for the wrapper script (only
108	  the deps still need PyPI, and PyPI is mirrorable; see below).
109	- **No `/dev/tty` re-exec gymnastics** — you're already in a real shell.
110	- **You can `git pull` and re-run** to test wrapper changes without re-running
111	  the curl pipeline.
112	- **You can `git checkout <branch>`** and run a feature branch's wrapper
113	  before merging.
114	
115	The only thing `bootstrap.sh` does that `just bootstrap-local` doesn't is
116	auto-installing `uv`. If `uv` is missing on the new host, install it once:
117	
118	```bash
119	curl -fsSL https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
120	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
121	```
122	
123	then `just bootstrap-local`.
124	
125	## Behind GFW / corporate proxy
126	
127	Three layers each need separate proxy/mirror config. The cheapest setup is a
128	local SOCKS/HTTP proxy (clash, v2ray, etc.) listening on `127.0.0.1:7890`:
129	
130	```bash
131	# (1) shell layer — curl, git, uv installer
132	export https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:7890
133	export http_proxy=$https_proxy
134	export all_proxy=socks5://127.0.0.1:7890
135	export no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1
136	
137	# (2) git layer — chezmoi init clones via git
138	git config --global http.https://github.com.proxy "$https_proxy"
139	# (or globally: git config --global http.proxy "$https_proxy")
140	
141	# (3) uv / PyPI layer — switch index instead of routing through proxy
142	export UV_INDEX_URL=https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple
143	# Tencent / Aliyun mirrors also work:
144	#   https://mirrors.cloud.tencent.com/pypi/simple
145	#   https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/
146	```
147	
148	If `raw.githubusercontent.com` itself is the bottleneck (the very first
149	`curl` in the bootstrap pipeline), point at a mirror:
150	
151	```bash
152	# ghproxy.com proxies *.githubusercontent.com transparently
153	export DOTFILES_RAW_URL="https://ghproxy.com/https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles"
154	export DOTFILES_REF=main
155	
156	curl -fsSL "${DOTFILES_RAW_URL}/${DOTFILES_REF}/bootstrap.sh" | bash
157	```
158	
159	`bootstrap.sh` itself respects `DOTFILES_RAW_URL` / `DOTFILES_REF` when
160	constructing the inner script URL, so the inner `uv run --script` will also
161	go through the mirror.
162	
163	> **Caveat — jsdelivr / cdn.statically.io** style CDNs use a different URL
164	> scheme (`/gh/owner/repo@ref/path`) and will not work as a drop-in
165	> `DOTFILES_RAW_URL`. Stick with `ghproxy.com`-style transparent proxies, or
166	> just clone locally and use `just bootstrap-local`.
167	
168	## What the inner `dotfiles_init.py` does
169	
170	See `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` (~836 lines) — it pre-flights chezmoi /
171	git / SSH, presents grouped feature-flag prompts via `questionary`, and
172	shells out to `chezmoi init <repo> --apply --promptString …`. Subcommands:
173	
174	- `init` (default) — the interactive flow.
175	- `doctor` — greps `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` + `Dockerfile` and verifies every
176	  prompt key is mirrored in the script's `PROMPTS` tuple. CI-friendly; exits
177	  non-zero on drift. See [AGENTS.md → Dockerfile + dotfiles_init wrapper](../../AGENTS.md).
178	- `list-bundles` — show the pre-canned feature-flag bundles
179	  (`personal-mac` / `work-mac` / `server-linux` / `minimal`).
180	
181	## Related
182	
183	- [`scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`](../../scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py) — the wrapper.
184	- [`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`](../../.chezmoi.toml.tmpl) — the prompt definitions chezmoi sees.
185	- [`Dockerfile`](../../Dockerfile) — the third file that must stay in sync (CHEZMOI_* build args).
186	- [docs/this_repo/initial_setup/](initial_setup/) — narrative walk-through of a fresh-machine install.
187	- [docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md](fleet-apply.md) — once one machine is up, push to a fleet from there.
188
```

```text
1	# Ansible Customization Guide
2	
3	This document explains how to customize the ansible setup for your dotfiles.
4	
5	## Directory Structure
6	
7	After `chezmoi apply`, ansible files are deployed to `~/.ansible/`:
8	
9	```
10	~/.ansible/
11	├── ansible.cfg            # Ansible configuration (sets roles_path, inventory)
12	├── inventories/
13	│   └── localhost.ini      # Local inventory
14	├── playbooks/
15	│   ├── base.yml           # Cross-platform essentials
16	│   ├── linux.yml          # Linux-specific setup
17	│   └── macos.yml          # macOS-specific setup
18	└── roles/
19	    ├── base/              # git, curl, ripgrep, fd, etc.
20	    ├── homebrew/          # macOS Homebrew installation
21	    ├── neovim/            # Neovim with version check
22	    └── lazyvim_deps/      # fzf, lazygit, tree-sitter-cli
23	```
24	
25	## Prerequisites
26	
27	Install ansible and required collections:
28	
29	```bash
30	# Install ansible with uv
31	uv tool install ansible-core
32	
33	# Install community.general collection (for homebrew module)
34	ansible-galaxy collection install community.general
35	```
36	
37	## Running Playbooks
38	
39	Run from `~/.ansible/` directory (ansible.cfg sets inventory and roles_path automatically):
40	
41	### Full Setup
42	
43	```bash
44	cd ~/.ansible
45	
46	# macOS
47	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml
48	
49	# Linux
50	ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml
51	```
52	
53	### Specific Tags
54	
55	```bash
56	cd ~/.ansible
57	
58	# Only install neovim
59	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --tags neovim
60	
61	# Install neovim and its dependencies
62	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --tags "neovim,lazyvim_deps"
63	```
64	
65	### Skip Tags
66	
67	```bash
68	# Skip tasks requiring sudo (for non-admin users)
69	ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml --skip-tags sudo
70	```
71	
72	### Dry Run
73	
74	```bash
75	# Check what would change without applying
76	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --check
77	
78	# Verbose output
79	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --check -v
80	```
81	
82	## Available Tags
83	
84	| Tag | Description | Requires Sudo |
85	|-----|-------------|---------------|
86	| `base` | Essential tools (git, curl, ripgrep, fd, jq) | Linux only |
87	| `homebrew` | macOS Homebrew installation | No |
88	| `neovim` | Neovim installation with version check | Linux only |
89	| `lazyvim_deps` | LazyVim dependencies | Linux only |
90	| `networking_tools` | Networking CLI tools (nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy, etc.) | Linux only (partial) |
91	| `sudo` | All tasks requiring elevated privileges | Yes |
92	
93	## Adding New Roles
94	
95	1. Create role directory structure:
96	
97	```bash
98	mkdir -p ~/.ansible/roles/myrole/tasks
99	mkdir -p ~/.ansible/roles/myrole/defaults  # optional
100	```
101	
102	2. Create tasks file `~/.ansible/roles/myrole/tasks/main.yml`:
103	
104	```yaml
105	---
106	- name: Install my package (macOS)
107	  when: ansible_os_family == "Darwin"
108	  community.general.homebrew:
109	    name: mypackage
110	    state: present
111	
112	- name: Install my package (Debian/Ubuntu)
113	  when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"
114	  become: true
115	  tags: [sudo]
116	  ansible.builtin.apt:
117	    name: mypackage
118	    state: present
119	```
120	
121	3. Add role to playbook:
122	
123	```yaml
124	# In ~/.ansible/playbooks/macos.yml or linux.yml
125	roles:
126	  - role: myrole
127	    tags: [myrole]
128	```
129	
130	## Syncing Changes Back to Chezmoi
131	
132	After experimenting with changes in `~/.ansible/`, add them back to chezmoi:
133	
134	```bash
135	# Copy modified files back to chezmoi source
136	cp ~/.ansible/roles/myrole/tasks/main.yml ~/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/myrole/tasks/main.yml
137	
138	# Or use chezmoi re-add
139	chezmoi re-add ~/.ansible/roles/myrole/tasks/main.yml
140	```
141	
142	## OS Detection
143	
144	Ansible facts used for OS detection:
145	
146	| Fact | macOS | Ubuntu/Debian |
147	|------|-------|---------------|
148	| `ansible_os_family` | Darwin | Debian |
149	| `ansible_distribution` | MacOSX | Ubuntu |
150	| `ansible_pkg_mgr` | homebrew | apt |
151	
152	Example conditional:
153	
154	```yaml
155	- name: macOS only task
156	  when: ansible_os_family == "Darwin"
157	  # ...
158	
159	- name: Ubuntu only task
160	  when: ansible_distribution == "Ubuntu"
161	  # ...
162	```
163	
164	## Sudo Handling
165	
166	### Linux
167	
168	Most package installations require sudo. Tasks are tagged with `sudo`:
169	
170	```yaml
171	- name: Install package
172	  become: true
173	  tags: [sudo]
174	  ansible.builtin.apt:
175	    name: mypackage
176	```
177	
178	Skip these with `--skip-tags sudo` if you don't have sudo access.
179	
180	### macOS
181	
182	Homebrew runs as user, no sudo needed. The only exception is system-level changes.
183	
184	## Troubleshooting
185	
186	### Syntax Check
187	
188	```bash
189	ansible-playbook --syntax-check ~/.ansible/playbooks/base.yml
190	```
191	
192	### Verbose Output
193	
194	```bash
195	ansible-playbook ... -vvv
196	```
197	
198	### List Tasks
199	
200	```bash
201	ansible-playbook ... --list-tasks
202	```
203	
204	### List Tags
205	
206	```bash
207	ansible-playbook ... --list-tags
208	```
209	
210	### Common Failures
211	
212	#### `GLIBC_2.XX not found` when running an installed CLI (Ubuntu 22.04 / older distros)
213	
214	**Symptom** — a CLI installed by the ansible roles fails at startup:
215	
216	```
217	tv: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.39' not found (required by tv)
218	```
219	
220	**Root cause** — the `.tar.gz` or `.deb` published under the tool's
221	`unknown-linux-gnu` target was built on a CI image (Ubuntu 24.04 / Debian 13)
222	whose glibc is newer than what the host distro ships. Ubuntu 22.04 LTS is
223	stuck on **glibc 2.35**, so any binary needing glibc ≥ 2.36 will fail to
224	start.
225	
226	**Fix (already applied in this repo as of the Jammy hardening patch):** the
227	ansible roles now prefer musl assets over gnu assets, and fall back to
228	Linuxbrew (or skip-with-warning) when no safe musl asset exists. See
229	[docs/linux-package-sources.md → GitHub binary asset selection policy](../linux-package-sources.md#github-binary-asset-selection-policy)
230	for the full policy.
231	
232	**If you still see the error on a box provisioned by this repo**, one of
233	these applies:
234	
235	1. **A stale gnu binary is still on PATH from a previous apply.** The new
236	   role only downloads musl / brew when the `command -v <tool>` check
237	   fails — so an old broken binary short-circuits the install. Remove it and
238	   re-run `chezmoi apply`:
239	
240	   ```bash
241	   rm -f ~/.local/bin/tv /usr/local/bin/tv   # or whichever tool
242	   chezmoi apply
243	   ```
244	
245	2. **The tool has no upstream musl asset and Linuxbrew isn't installed.**
246	   Affected tools as of this writing: `tv` (all arches), `git-delta` (arm64
247	   only), `eza` (arm64 only). The role prints an explicit debug message
248	   telling you to install Linuxbrew. On Debian/Ubuntu:
249	
250	   ```bash
251	   /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
252	   eval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
253	   chezmoi apply     # re-runs the role, brew-install branch taken this time
254	   ```
255	
256	3. **A new tool was added to a role using `unknown-linux-gnu` again.** When
257	   adding a role that downloads a Rust/Go binary, prefer the musl asset and
258	   fall back to brew-or-skip per the policy linked above. Pattern examples:
259	   `ripgrep` / `bat` / `fd` / `zellij` / `tailspin` / `lnav` / `trippy`.
260	
261	#### `eza` install fails on some hosts with broken third-party apt repo
262	
263	See the comment on the `Add eza repository` task in
264	`dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — the `deb.gierens.de` repo
265	occasionally ships an expired GPG signature. The role tolerates this and
266	falls through to the GitHub-release fallback, so no manual fix is usually
267	needed. If the fallback also fails, remove the broken repo file:
268	
269	```bash
270	sudo rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/gierens.list /etc/apt/keyrings/gierens.gpg
271	sudo apt update
272	chezmoi apply     # re-runs the role; GitHub-release fallback picks it up
273	```
274	
275	## LazyVim Requirements
276	
277	LazyVim needs:
278	
279	- Neovim >= 0.11.2
280	- ripgrep (for telescope live grep)
281	- fd (for telescope file finder)
282	- Node.js (for LSP servers)
283	- tree-sitter-cli (for syntax highlighting)
284	- lazygit (optional, for git integration)
285	- fzf (optional, for fuzzy finding)
286	
287	All are installed by the `base`, `neovim`, and `lazyvim_deps` roles.
288
```

```md
# Zsh 補全最佳實踐

本 dotfiles 專案中 zsh 自動補全 (tab completion) 的組織方式。

!!! note "Terminology rule (zh-TW pages)"
    技術名詞首次出現以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現，例：依賴注入
    (dependency injection)。**不自創翻譯**——若無公認譯名直接保留英文
    （如 `embedding`、`tokenizer`）。代碼、API 名、CLI flag、套件名、檔名一律不翻。

## 架構 (Architecture)

\```
compinit runs once (inside oh-my-zsh.sh)
        │
        ├── ~/.zfunc/                          ← user-generated completions (NOT tracked by chezmoi)
        ├── ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/       ← community completions (184 files, cloned by ansible)
        │     └── zsh-completions/src/
        ├── ~/.docker/completions/             ← Docker-shipped completions
        ├── $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/        ← Homebrew-managed completions (via `brew completions link`)
        │     └── site-functions/
        └── $ZSH/completions/                  ← oh-my-zsh built-in completions
\```

所有 `fpath` 的新增都在 `dot_zshrc.tmpl` 中、且**位於** `source "$ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh"` 之**前**，因此 `compinit` 只會執行一次並載入所有項目。

## 補全分類 (Completion Categories)

工具可分為四大類：

### A. 自我產生 (`tool completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tool`)

大多數現代 CLI 工具能夠輸出自己的補全腳本 (script)。安裝後執行一次，版本升級後重新執行。

| Tool | Command |
|------|---------|
| `uv` | `uv generate-shell-completion zsh` |
| `mise` | `mise completion zsh` |
| `chezmoi` | `chezmoi completion zsh` |
| `just` | `just --completions zsh` |
| `bat` | `bat --completion zsh` |
| `delta` | `delta --generate-completion zsh` |
| `starship` | `starship completions zsh` |
| `rg` | `rg --generate complete-zsh` |
| `fd` | `fd --gen-completions zsh` |
| `zellij` | `zellij setup --generate-completion zsh` |
| `sesh` | `sesh completion zsh` |
| `pueue` | `pueue completions zsh` |
| `docker` | `docker completion zsh` |
| `gh` | `gh completion -s zsh` |
| `opencode` | `opencode completion zsh` |
| `bw` | `bw completion --shell zsh` |

**使用模式：**

\```bash
# 產生一次（或升級後）
mkdir -p ~/.zfunc
uv generate-shell-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_uv
mise completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_mise
\```

### B. 預先打包 (無需動作)

補全隨套件 (package) 一起出貨，或經由 `zsh-completions` 社群外掛 (plugin) 提供。

| Tool | Source |
|------|--------|
| `eza` | Homebrew formula 將 `_eza` 安裝到 site-functions |
| `git` | oh-my-zsh `git` plugin |
| `yazi` | release 資產中包含 `_yazi`（zsh-completions 也有） |
| `lazygit` | 不支援補全；不需要（TUI app） |
| `btop` | 不支援補全；不需要（TUI app） |
| 其他眾多工具 | `zsh-completions` plugin 涵蓋 184 個工具 |

### C. 啟動時 eval/source（shell 整合）

這些工具在更廣泛的 shell 整合中注入補全。已在 `dot_config/zsh/tools/` 中處理。

| Tool | Where | How |
|------|-------|-----|
| `fzf` | `tools/10_fzf.zsh` | `source <(fzf --zsh)` |
| `zoxide` | `tools/20_zoxide.zsh` | `eval "$(zoxide init zsh)"` |
| `thefuck` | `tools/25_thefuck.zsh` | `eval $(thefuck --alias)` |
| `direnv` | `tools/30_direnv.zsh` | `eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"` |
| `marimo` | `tools/29_marimo.zsh` | `eval "$(_MARIMO_COMPLETE=zsh_source marimo)"` |

### D. 不支援補全

`claude`、`gemini`、`btop`、`lazygit` —— 沒有可用的產生命令。

### E. 透過 `shtab` / `tyro` 的 Python 工具

Python CLI 框架 (framework) 可以產生補全：

- **[tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/)**：`python my_cli.py --tyro-write-completion zsh ~/.zfunc/_my_cli`
- **[shtab](https://github.com/iterative/shtab)**：`shtab --shell=zsh my_module.parser > ~/.zfunc/_my_tool`
- **argcomplete**：`register-python-argcomplete tool_name`（使用 eval，屬於 C 類）
- **click**（mlflow、litellm 等使用）：`_TOOL_COMPLETE=zsh_source tool > ~/.zfunc/_tool`

## 為何 `~/.zfunc/` **不**由 chezmoi 追蹤

**決定：`~/.zfunc/` 不納入版本控制。** 理由：

1. **補全與工具版本相依。** 由 `uv 0.6` 產生的補全腳本可能不符合 `uv 0.7`。追蹤過時檔案會造成隱微的損壞。
2. **不是所有使用者都安裝相同工具。** 若沒安裝 pueue，`_pueue` 補全檔案毫無用處（且會丟出警告）。
3. **重新產生很簡單。** 每個工具只需要一行命令。
4. **Brew 安裝的工具自動管理其補全**，透過 site-functions。在 `~/.zfunc/` 中重複會造成衝突。

### 我們**有**追蹤的內容

- `dot_zshrc.tmpl` 中的 `fpath+=~/.zfunc`（確保此目錄在搜尋路徑中）
- 由 ansible 複製 (clone) 的 `zsh-completions` 外掛（社群補全）
- `~/.docker/completions` 的 fpath 條目
- `dot_config/zsh/tools/` 中工具特定的 `eval`/`source` 整合

## 全新安裝後產生補全

在新機器上執行 `chezmoi apply` 後，多數補全已可透過 `zsh-completions` 外掛和 Homebrew site-functions 運作。對於想要**更豐富/更新版補全**的工具，可將其產生到 `~/.zfunc/`：

\```bash
mkdir -p ~/.zfunc

# 核心工具（永遠安裝）
chezmoi completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_chezmoi
mise completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_mise
uv generate-shell-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_uv
just --completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_just
starship completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_starship

# 開發工具（若已安裝）
command -v gh    && gh completion -s zsh > ~/.zfunc/_gh
command -v docker && docker completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_docker
command -v rg    && rg --generate complete-zsh > ~/.zfunc/_rg
command -v fd    && fd --gen-completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_fd
command -v bat   && bat --completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_bat
command -v delta && delta --generate-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_delta
command -v zellij && zellij setup --generate-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_zellij
command -v sesh  && sesh completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_sesh
command -v pueue && pueue completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_pueue

# Coding agents（若已安裝）
command -v opencode && opencode completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_opencode
command -v bw    && bw completion --shell zsh > ~/.zfunc/_bw

# 強制重建補全快取
rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit
\```

> **小提示：** 你可以將其儲存為 `~/.local/bin/` 中的腳本，或將其作為函式 (function) 加入 `~/.zshrc.adhoc`。

## 優先順序 / 覆寫順序

當同一個 `_tool` 檔案存在於多個 fpath 目錄中時，**第一個符合者勝出**：

\```
1. ~/.zfunc/                                    (最高 - 你的覆寫)
2. ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/
3. ~/.docker/completions/
4. $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/   (Homebrew-managed)
5. /usr/share/zsh/*/functions/                  (system, lowest)
\```

目前 `dot_zshrc.tmpl` 的順序：

\```zsh
fpath+=~/.zfunc                     # appended (lowest of custom)
fpath=(zsh-completions/src $fpath)  # prepended (higher than ~/.zfunc)
fpath=(~/.docker/completions $fpath) # prepended (highest of custom)
\```

若你希望 `~/.zfunc/` 覆寫社群補全，改為前置 (prepend)：

\```zsh
fpath=(~/.zfunc $fpath)  # prepend instead of append
\```

## FAQ

**Q：對於 `zsh-completions` 已涵蓋的工具，我還應該產生補全嗎？**
A：只有當你想要最新版本時。社群外掛可能落後。對於快速演進的工具（uv、mise），自行產生是值得的。

**Q：解除安裝某工具後，補全檔案丟出錯誤，該怎麼辦？**
A：移除該檔案：`rm ~/.zfunc/_toolname`。fpath 中過時的 `_tool` 檔案除非有語法錯誤，否則無害（會被靜默忽略）。

**Q：我該如何除錯補全問題？**
A：執行 `echo $fpath | tr ' ' '\n'` 查看所有 fpath 條目。使用 `which _toolname` 查看正在使用哪個補全檔案。透過 `rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit` 強制重建。

# 基礎架構與虛擬化參考

!!! note "Terminology rule (zh-TW pages)"
    技術名詞首次出現以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現，例：依賴注入

虛擬化 (virtualization)、共享儲存 (shared storage)、多使用者運算排程，以及共享家目錄身分驗證 (shared-home identity) 等模式的參考筆記。**僅為文件** —— 此資料夾內的內容皆不會由 chezmoi 安裝。這是「當你已經不再只用筆電」之後的知識庫。

## 此資料夾涵蓋（與不涵蓋）的範圍

| 範圍 | 在此資料夾？ | 由 chezmoi 安裝？ |
|-------|-----------------|-----------------------|
| 裸機 hypervisor 作業系統 (Proxmox / ESXi / XCP-ng) | 是（參考） | 否 —— 這些是主機作業系統，不是應用程式 |
| 桌面 VM 管理工具 (OrbStack、UTM、VirtualBox、Fusion) | 是（參考） | 僅 OrbStack，透過 [dot_ansible/roles/docker/tasks/main.yml](../../dot_ansible/roles/docker/tasks/main.yml) |
| 叢集共享儲存 (CephFS、BeeGFS、Lustre、NFS) | 是（參考） | 否 —— 多節點叢集議題 |
| 多使用者運算排程 (SLURM、K8s、Nomad) | 是（參考） | 否 —— 叢集營運議題 |
| 身分驗證與共享家目錄 (FreeIPA、LDAP、SSSD) | 是（參考） | 否 —— 組織專屬 |
| 個人開發筆電工具（編輯器、CLI、dotfiles） | 否 —— 請見 [docs/tools/](../tools/) | 是 —— 本 repo 的主要目的 |

如果你想知道「我要怎麼在 MacBook 上跑一個 VM？」 —— 答案是 OrbStack（已預裝），請見 [virtualization.md](virtualization.md#desktop-vm-managers)。如果你問的是「我們團隊要怎麼建立一個共用運算叢集？」 —— 此資料夾勾勒出大致的版圖，但實際建置是另一個獨立的營運專案。

## 決策樹

\```mermaid
flowchart TD
    startNode["我需要某處的運算或儲存資源"] --> q1{規模}
    q1 -->|筆電上的單一 VM| laptop["virtualization.md#desktop-vm-managers"]
    q1 -->|幾台伺服器 / 家用實驗室| hypervisor["virtualization.md#type-1-bare-metal-hypervisors"]
    q1 -->|多使用者叢集| cluster{要解決什麼問題？}
    cluster -->|跨節點共享檔案| storage["shared-storage.md"]
    cluster -->|將工作排程到節點| sched["compute-scheduling.md"]

\```

## 內容

| 文件 | 涵蓋內容 |
|-----|----------------|
| [virtualization.md](virtualization.md) | 桌面 VM 管理工具 (OrbStack、UTM、VirtualBox、Fusion、Lima、libvirt)、type-1 hypervisor (Proxmox VE、ESXi、XCP-ng、Harvester、Nutanix)、K8s 原生 VM (KubeVirt)。包含明確的 OrbStack 與 Proxmox 對照。 |
| [shared-storage.md](shared-storage.md) | CephFS、BeeGFS、Lustre、GlusterFS、MooseFS / SeaweedFS / JuiceFS、NFSv4、Samba。依工作負載分類的決策矩陣與 client 端掛載範例。 |
| [compute-scheduling.md](compute-scheduling.md) | SLURM、Kubernetes + Kueue/Volcano、Nomad、HTCondor、OpenPBS、YARN、Mesos、Ray/Dask、OpenStack Nova、Proxmox HA。涵蓋多使用者 CPU/GPU/VM 配置。 |
| [shared-home-identity.md](shared-home-identity.md) | FreeIPA、389ds、OpenLDAP、Samba AD、SSSD、autofs 家目錄掛載、UID/GID 慣例。「所有人的 `$HOME` 都放在 NAS 上」這個經典模式。 |

## 各層如何組合

典型的多使用者 Linux 運算叢集大致堆疊如下：

\```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph compute["運算層"]
        scheduler["排程器 (SLURM / K8s / Nomad)"]
        nodes["Worker 節點"]
        scheduler --> nodes
    end
    subgraph storage["儲存層"]
        cephbeegfs["共享 FS (CephFS / BeeGFS / NFS)"]
    end
    subgraph identity["身分驗證層"]
        ipa["FreeIPA / LDAP + Kerberos"]
        sssd["每個節點上的 SSSD"]
    end
    subgraph virt["虛擬化層（選用）"]
        hyp["Proxmox / ESXi / KVM"]
        vms["承載 worker 節點的 VM"]
        hyp --> vms
    end
    vms -.-> nodes
    nodes -->|掛載 /home, /scratch| cephbeegfs
    nodes -->|認證| sssd
    sssd -->|LDAP/KRB| ipa
\```

依規模獨立挑選每一層：

- **單一使用者筆電**：只有「運算層」（直接用你的筆電，或許搭配 OrbStack 開些用完即丟的 VM）
- **小型團隊（5-20 人）**：加上 NFS + FreeIPA。排程器選用。
- **HPC / ML 研究實驗室（50+ 人）**：加上 Proxmox 或裸機 + BeeGFS/Lustre + SLURM + FreeIPA
- **現代雲原生 (cloud-native)**：以 Kubernetes 取代 SLURM、以 CephFS + CSI 取代 NFS、保留 FreeIPA 處理 SSH/sudo 身分
