1	# Upgrades — Explicit, Opt-in Tool Refresh
2	
3	> How to actually move installed tools forward on a machine managed by this repo, and why `chezmoi apply` deliberately will *not* do that for you.
4	
5	## Why install and upgrade are split
6	
7	`chezmoi apply` (and the ansible phase it triggers) is **install-only by design**. Ansible roles use `state: present` + `creates:` so that running `chezmoi apply` on a running box is idempotent and never silently bumps every tool to whatever happens to be latest that day. This matters because:
8	
9	- **Predictability** — rerunning apply after editing one role file shouldn't ripple-upgrade unrelated tools.
10	- **Offline / flaky network** — install-only can be satisfied by what's already on disk; `--upgrade` workflows always hit the network.
11	- **Review friction** — you *want* to see "chezmoi says 10 casks would move; proceed?" as a separate decision from "apply my dotfile changes".
12	
13	The explicit upgrade path lives in [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](../../scripts/upgrade_tools.sh), exposed via `just upgrade-*` recipes in [`justfile`](../../justfile). It is the **only** thing that intentionally moves tools forward on this repo's flow.
14	
15	Two side-effects worth knowing about:
16	
17	- `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` entries have `refreshPeriod = "168h"` — chezmoi itself will re-fetch those weekly on apply. That's a bounded "nudge", not an upgrade mechanism for installed binaries.
18	- Homebrew casks that carry a `homebrew_cask` entry with `state: present` freeze to that version until a Brewfile hash change forces a re-bundle with `--no-upgrade`. Still install-only; `upgrade-brew` is what actually bumps them.
19	
20	## Entry points
21	
22	```bash
23	just upgrade-all          # externals → brew → mise → uv → npm → cargo → dotnet → gem → flatpak → warp → agents → plugins
24	just upgrade-dry-run      # same, but commands are printed, not executed
25	just upgrade-<category>   # run one category in isolation
26	```
27	
28	Or use the script directly when you want the flags:
29	
30	```bash
31	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh                           # same as 'all'
32	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh brew uv                   # two categories
33	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --only brew,mise          # same, via --only
34	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --skip agents,plugins     # all, minus those
35	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --dry-run all             # preview
36	./scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --help
37	```
38	
39	The script runs categories in the canonical `ALL_CATEGORIES` order regardless of CLI arg order — dependencies between categories are real (see [§ Run order](#run-order)).
40	
41	## Category matrix
42	
43	| Category | What actually happens |
44	| --- | --- |
45	| `externals` | `chezmoi upgrade` (the chezmoi binary itself) + `chezmoi apply --refresh-externals` (force-refresh the 168h externals: oh-my-zsh, TPM, toolkami.rb, fzf). First because a chezmoi version bump may change how later steps behave. |
46	| `brew` | `brew update` → `brew upgrade` → `brew upgrade --cask --greedy` → `brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile` *without* `--no-upgrade` → `Brewfile.{darwin,linux}` → `brew cleanup`. macOS pre-warms the shared sudo session via [`scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`](../../scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) so cask pkg installers that shell out to `sudo /usr/sbin/installer` find a live ticket. |
47	| `mise` | `mise self-update --yes` + `mise upgrade` (honours the version constraints in `~/.config/mise/config.toml`). `self-update` warns, rather than fails, when mise was installed via brew/apt. |
48	| `uv` | `uv self update` + `uv tool upgrade --all`. Covers every tool listed in [`python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml) and [`llm_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/llm_tools/defaults/main.yml). |
49	| `npm` | `npm -g update`, falling back to `mise exec -- npm -g update` when `npm` is not directly on PATH (same detection as [`js_cli_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/js_cli_tools/tasks/main.yml) / [`bitwarden`](../../dot_ansible/roles/bitwarden/tasks/main.yml)). |
50	| `cargo` | If absent, bootstraps the `cargo-update` crate, then `cargo install-update -a`. Covers pueue (Linux) plus any future entries in [`rust_cargo_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/defaults/main.yml). |
51	| `dotnet` | Parses tool names from [`dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml) and runs `dotnet tool update --global <name>` per tool (via the mise dotnet shim). Falls back to `dotnet tool list --global` if parsing finds nothing. |
52	| `gem` | `gem update --system` + `gem update` via the mise ruby shim. |
53	| `flatpak` | `flatpak update --user --noninteractive --assumeyes` for user-scope Flathub apps (Discord et al. when `discordChannel=flatpak` — see [`docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md`](../playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md)). Skipped when `flatpak` is absent OR when no user-scope apps are installed. System-scope (`flatpak update --system`) is intentionally NOT covered — it requires `sudo` and is rare in this repo's flow; run manually if needed. |
54	| `warp` | **Linux only.** `sudo apt-get update` + `sudo apt-get install --only-upgrade -y warp-terminal` via the shared sudo session. macOS Warp is handled by `cat_brew` (cask `warp` + `--greedy`); this category short-circuits with `SKIPPED` on Darwin. The on-disk binary is replaced but the running Warp process is **not** restarted — quit + relaunch Warp to load the new version. The in-app `warp_finish_update <token>` graceful-restart only works from inside a live Warp session (Warp-injected shell function, not on `$PATH` otherwise) — see [`docs/tools/warp.md`](../tools/warp.md) for the full mechanism. |
55	| `agents` | Re-runs the official `curl \| bash` installers for **tools already present** only — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Ollama (Linux), llmfit (Linux), RTK. Bootstrap list mirrors [`coding_agents`](../../dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml). |
56	| `plugins` | `nvim --headless "+Lazy! sync" +qa` → `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/bin/update_plugins all` → refresh installed `claude-hud` via [`claude_hud_sync.py`](../../dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/files/claude_hud_sync.py) → `pre-commit autoupdate` (on the dotfiles repo root) → `tldr --update` → `gh extension upgrade --all`. Each step is guarded on the relevant binary being present. |
57	
58	### Run order
59	
60	```mermaid
61	flowchart LR
62	    externals["externals<br/>(chezmoi + externals)"] --> brew
63	    brew["brew<br/>(formulas + casks greedy + Brewfile)"] --> mise
64	    mise["mise<br/>(self-update + runtimes)"] --> uv
65	    uv["uv<br/>(self update + tools)"] --> npm
66	    npm["npm<br/>(-g update)"] --> cargo
67	    cargo["cargo<br/>(install-update -a)"] --> dotnet
68	    dotnet["dotnet<br/>(tool update --global)"] --> gem
69	    gem["gem<br/>(gem update)"] --> flatpak
70	    flatpak["flatpak<br/>(--user update)"] --> warp
71	    warp["warp<br/>(Linux apt-only)"] --> agents
72	    agents["agents<br/>(curl \| bash installers)"] --> plugins
73	    plugins["plugins<br/>(Lazy, TPM, pre-commit, tldr, gh)"] --> summary((Summary))
74	```
75	
76	Rationale: package managers themselves go first (`externals` to maybe swap chezmoi; `brew` because mise/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem may be Homebrew-installed; `mise` before the language-scoped ones because `mise upgrade` can swap the runtime `npm`/`cargo`/`dotnet`/`gem` belong to). `agents` + `plugins` last because they depend on everything above being current.
77	
78	`claude-hud` stays out of [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl): it uses a versioned cache path and rewrites `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`, so it fits the explicit `plugins` upgrade path better than chezmoi externals. Upstream `v0.0.12+` also switched usage rendering to Claude Code's official stdin `rate_limits`, which means the old credential-derived `Max` badge may disappear after upgrade.
79	
80	## Semantics: best-effort, not all-or-nothing
81	
82	Each category is wrapped in a `run_category` helper:
83	
84	- Individual command failures inside a category do **not** abort the rest of the category. Everything is best-effort.
85	- A category failure does **not** abort the next category. The script keeps going.
86	- Categories return `77` when the prerequisite is missing (e.g. no `dotnet` binary) — that is reported as **SKIPPED**, not FAILED.
87	- The final summary groups into three buckets:
88	
89	```text
90	[INFO] Upgrade Summary
91	[SUCCESS] OK:      externals brew mise uv npm cargo agents plugins
92	[WARN] SKIPPED: gem (prerequisite missing)
93	[ERROR] FAILED:  dotnet
94	[ERROR]    - dotnet: rc=1
95	```
96	
97	Overall process exit code is `1` iff at least one category is in FAILED. `--dry-run` always exits `0` because no real command runs.
98	
99	## Sample: `just upgrade-dry-run`
100	
101	```text
102	────────────────────────────────────────────
103	[INFO] upgrade_tools.sh — categories: externals brew mise uv npm cargo dotnet gem agents plugins (dry-run)
104	[WARN] DRY-RUN MODE — commands are printed, not executed
105	────────────────────────────────────────────
106	[INFO] ── category: externals ──
107	[INFO] Upgrading chezmoi binary itself
108	+ chezmoi upgrade
109	[INFO] Force-refreshing chezmoi externals (.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl)
110	+ chezmoi apply --refresh-externals
111	[SUCCESS] category 'externals' completed
112	────────────────────────────────────────────
113	[INFO] ── category: brew ──
114	+ brew update
115	+ brew upgrade
116	+ brew upgrade --cask --greedy
117	+ brew bundle --file=/Users/me/.config/homebrew/Brewfile
118	+ brew bundle --file=/Users/me/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin
119	+ brew cleanup
120	[SUCCESS] category 'brew' completed
121	...
122	```
123	
124	## Things intentionally excluded
125	
126	- **No `state: latest` rewrites of ansible roles.** `chezmoi apply` semantics stay conservative; the upgrade path uses package-manager commands directly.
127	- **No `apt upgrade` / system package bumps.** Keeps the default scope sudo-light and noise-free. Run `sudo apt upgrade && sudo apt autoremove` manually if you want that.
128	- **No daemon restart** for LiteLLM / Ollama / pueued / anything `systemd`-managed. We only refresh the binaries; restarting is your call.
129	- **No automatic scheduling.** There is no cron, launchd, or systemd timer wired up. Running `just upgrade-all` is an intentional action you take when you have time to review diffs / deal with breakage.
130	- **`scripts/**` is ignored by chezmoi** ([`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiignore.tmpl) line 29) — the script is *not* deployed to `$HOME`. It runs from the dotfiles repo checkout directly (where `chezmoi cd` takes you). That is a deliberate choice: upgrade logic is repo-local, not per-user.
131	
132	## Troubleshooting
133	
134	- **`chezmoi upgrade` fails.** `chezmoi upgrade` only works when chezmoi was installed via the official install script or `go install`. Homebrew/apt installs will surface an error — upgrade via *that* channel instead. The script treats this as a warning, not a failure.
135	- **`mise self-update` / `uv self update` fails.** Same pattern — both refuse when installed via a system package manager. Treated as a warning.
136	- **macOS cask pkg installer hangs on sudo.** The script calls `sudo_session_init "upgrade-brew"` on macOS, which prompts once and warms the ticket. If you ran the script over SSH with no TTY, that step becomes `non-interactive` and cask pkg bumps may stall. Fix: run locally, or `ssh -t`, or pre-warm with `sudo -v` yourself before `just upgrade-brew`.
137	- **`cargo install-update -a` fails halfway through.** One crate break does not abort the rest (best-effort). Re-run `just upgrade-cargo` — cargo-update is itself rebuilt if missing.
138	- **`pre-commit autoupdate` bumped a hook that now errors.** That is a repo-file change, not an environment change. Review `.pre-commit-config.yaml` diff; `git checkout -p .pre-commit-config.yaml` to partially revert if needed.
139	
140	## Extending
141	
142	Three ways to add a new tool to the upgrade flow:
143	
144	1. **Tool already managed by an existing category (brew / uv / npm / cargo / dotnet / gem / mise).** Nothing to do — the generic `upgrade-<category>` picks it up because it uses the package manager's own bulk command.
145	2. **New `curl | bash` installer.** Add a guarded block inside `cat_agents()` in [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](../../scripts/upgrade_tools.sh). Gate on the binary being present so the upgrade path never bootstraps on machines that don't have the tool.
146	
147	   ```bash
148	   if command -v newtool >/dev/null 2>&1; then
149	     info "Upgrading newtool"
150	     _run_sh "curl -fsSL https://newtool.dev/install.sh | bash" || any_fail=1
151	     ran_any=1
152	   fi
153	   ```
154	
155	3. **Brand-new strategy (e.g. GitHub release binary with custom download logic).** Add a `cat_<name>` function, register it in:
156	   - `ALL_CATEGORIES` array
157	   - The dispatch `case` in the main loop
158	   - A matching `just upgrade-<name>` recipe in [`justfile`](../../justfile)
159	   - This doc's [category matrix](#category-matrix)
160	
161	Keep the return-value contract: `0` = success, `77` = skipped (prerequisite missing), any other non-zero = failure.
162	
163	## Cross-references
164	
165	- [`AGENTS.md` § Hard repo invariants](../../AGENTS.md#install-vs-upgrade-is-split-on-purpose) — short version (install-vs-upgrade rule) written for AI agents touching this repo.
166	- [`README.md` § Keeping tools up-to-date](../../README.md) — short version written for humans arriving from the front page.
167	- [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](../../scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) — the implementation.
168	- [`scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`](../../scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) — the sudo-session helper reused for macOS cask installers.
169	- [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl) — the `refreshPeriod` entries that `upgrade-externals` force-refreshes.
170	- Ansible role defaults consumed for enumeration: [`dotnet_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml), [`python_uv_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml), [`llm_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/llm_tools/defaults/main.yml), [`coding_agents`](../../dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml).
171
```

```text
1	# Shell Script Testing
2	
3	How this repo tests shell code, the landscape of shell-testing tools, and when to reach for each.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## TL;DR for this repo
8	
9	| Tool | Role | Scope |
10	|------|------|-------|
11	| [**bats-core**](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core) | Behaviour / unit tests | `tests/unit/`, `tests/smoke/` |
12	| [**shellcheck**](https://www.shellcheck.net/) | Static analysis (bugs, bad quoting) | Pre-commit on `scripts/*.sh` |
13	| [**shfmt**](https://github.com/mvdan/sh) | Formatter (consistency check) | Pre-commit on `scripts/*.sh` |
14	
15	Run everything with `just check-all`. Run just the fast unit suite with `just bats`. See [the repo tests/ tree](#how-this-repo-structures-tests) below.
16	
17	**What's intentionally _not_ in scope:** ansible-role tests, bootstrap / `run_once` tests, chezmoi-template expansion tests, Python script tests, GitHub Actions CI. Coverage is deliberately narrow — this is a personal dotfiles repo, not a library.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## The three shell-testing frameworks
22	
23	Most people pick between Bats, ZUnit, and ShellSpec. Short version of when each makes sense:
24	
25	### Bats (Bash Automated Testing System) — what this repo uses
26	
27	A Bash testing framework. Tests go in `*.bats` files; each test is a `@test "name" { ... }` block. Provides `run`, `$status`, `$output`, `setup`, `teardown`, plus TAP / JUnit output for CI.
28	
29	Pick Bats when:
30	
31	- You mainly write Bash.
32	- You're testing CLI scripts or zsh scripts via **black-box** behaviour (run the command, check exit code + stdout/stderr).
33	- You want the most popular / best-documented shell testing ecosystem.
34	
35	Not ideal when:
36	
37	- You're testing zsh-specific functions (plugins, autoload, `${(P)var}`, parameter expansion flags) at the function level — Bats has no zsh affinity.
38	- You need mocking, coverage, or BDD grammar.
39	
40	Companion libraries (optional, **not vendored here** to keep ceremony low):
41	
42	- [`bats-assert`](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-assert) — `assert_equal`, `assert_output --partial`, etc.
43	- [`bats-file`](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-file) — file-system assertions.
44	- [`bats-support`](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-support) — shared helpers for the above.
45	
46	### ZUnit — zsh-native
47	
48	A [ZSH testing framework](https://github.com/zunit-zsh/zunit). Testcase syntax is similar to Bats but written in zsh, so zsh-specific constructs work naturally in both the tests and the code under test.
49	
50	Pick ZUnit when:
51	
52	- You're writing a zsh plugin, autoload function, or zsh-heavy library.
53	- You want the test harness to _be_ zsh rather than drive zsh from bash.
54	
55	Trade-off: smaller ecosystem than Bats, needs [Revolver](https://github.com/molovo/revolver) as a dependency. Not installed by this repo.
56	
57	### ShellSpec — full-featured, cross-shell
58	
59	[ShellSpec](https://github.com/shellspec/shellspec) is a BDD framework that runs on dash, bash, ksh, zsh, and POSIX shells. Supports mocking, parameterised tests, parallel execution, coverage.
60	
61	Pick ShellSpec when:
62	
63	- You're shipping a shell library that must work across multiple shells.
64	- You want RSpec-style `Describe` / `It` / `When` / `The output should …` syntax.
65	- You need mocking or coverage reports.
66	
67	Trade-off: heavier to learn than Bats; overkill for simple CLI behaviour checks.
68	
69	### How to decide
70	
71	| Situation | Pick |
72	|-----------|------|
73	| Bash CLI script, short & simple tests | **Bats** |
74	| zsh plugin / autoload-heavy code you want tested at the function level | ZUnit |
75	| Cross-shell library, or need mocking / coverage / BDD | ShellSpec |
76	| zsh CLI script tested via its external behaviour | **Bats** (drive zsh from bash, assert on output) |
77	
78	This repo falls in the last row — most "zsh" code here is really "zsh script invoked as a CLI," so Bats is the simplest fit even though the code under test is zsh.
79	
80	---
81	
82	## How this repo structures tests
83	
84	```
85	tests/
86	├── test_helper.bash          # shared helpers, sourced by every .bats file
87	├── unit/
88	│   ├── zsh_proxy.bats        # proxy helpers in 50_networking.zsh
89	│   ├── ghget.bats            # GitHub tree-URL parsing in 41_github.zsh
90	│   └── lan_scan.bats         # pure helpers in lan-scan.sh
91	└── smoke/
92	    └── docker_install.bats   # runs inside Docker after full install
93	```
94	
95	### `tests/test_helper.bash`
96	
97	Small helper library (<40 lines). Provides:
98	
99	- `$REPO_ROOT` — absolute path to the chezmoi source.
100	- `setup_path_stub` — creates a temp dir and prepends it to `PATH`. Exposes the path via `$BATS_STUB_DIR` (not stdout), so the export survives — **do not wrap it in `$(...)`**. Command substitution runs the helper in a subshell and the `export PATH` is lost.
101	- `cleanup_path_stubs` — removes any stub dirs registered during the test.
102	- Default `teardown()` that calls `cleanup_path_stubs`. If a test file defines its own `teardown()`, call `cleanup_path_stubs` at the end to preserve cleanup.
103	
104	### `tests/unit/zsh_proxy.bats`
105	
106	Exercises the proxy helpers in `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh`:
107	
108	- `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` takes precedence over probing.
109	- Active Clash config (`mixed-port:` or `port:`/`socks-port:`) takes precedence over generic loopback probing.
110	- Port probe order: `7890 → 7891 → 1087 → 8118 → 8080`.
111	- `_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE=none` when nothing responds.
112	- `__zsh_net_all_proxy_url` returns `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` when set; falls back to the HTTP cache otherwise.
113	- `proxy-on` exports all six env vars (`http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `all_proxy`).
114	- Split HTTP / SOCKS wiring regression guard (commit `fa4c063`).
115	- `proxy-off` clears all six plus `NO_PROXY` / `no_proxy`, and drops cached detection state.
116	- `proxy-status` exit codes: `1` when unavailable, `0` when available.
117	
118	Key technique: each test runs `zsh -f -c '...'` (no startup files) so the in-file cache (`$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE`) can't leak between tests, and `nc` is stubbed via a temp dir on `PATH` — no real network traffic.
119	
120	### `tests/unit/ghget.bats`
121	
122	Pins URL parsing for `ghget` in `dot_config/zsh/tools/41_github.zsh`:
123	
124	- Rejects missing / non-GitHub / `/blob/` (file, not tree) URLs with exit 1.
125	- For valid URLs, checks that `owner`, `repo`, `branch`, and the subdir path all reach the `curl` + `tar` invocations intact. Query strings and trailing slashes are stripped.
126	- Refuses to overwrite an existing destination directory before touching the network.
127	
128	Key technique: `curl` and `tar` are stubbed with bash scripts that log their args to `$CAPTURE_LOG`. The `tar` stub also fabricates the expected extracted directory (reading `-C` target and the last positional) so the post-extract `mv` in `ghget` succeeds — no real network, no real tarball.
129	
130	### `tests/unit/lan_scan.bats`
131	
132	Pins pure helpers in `dot_config/television/executable_lan-scan.sh`:
133	
134	- `is_usable_ip` — accepts normal host IPs; rejects link-local (`169.254/16`), multicast (`224–239/4`), broadcast, network address, and `.0` / `.255` in the host octet.
135	- `vendor_for_mac` — normalises colon / dash / no-sep MAC formats, looks up the 6-hex prefix in an nmap-style OUI database.
136	
137	Key technique: the script dispatches at load time (line 325+), so bare `source` runs the `all` subcommand and tries to probe the network. Work around by sourcing with `clean` as the first positional arg against an isolated `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` — `clean` is harmless under an isolated cache dir, and the function definitions remain in scope afterwards.
138	
139	### `tests/smoke/docker_install.bats`
140	
141	Runs inside the Dockerfile-built test image after `chezmoi apply` + ansible have completed. Asserts post-install state:
142	
143	- `chezmoi apply` is idempotent (re-apply produces empty `chezmoi diff`).
144	- `zsh -n` passes on `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zshenv`, and every `~/.config/zsh/**/*.zsh`.
145	- `nvim --headless "+lua print('ok')" +qa` exits 0.
146	- Core CLI tools on `PATH`: `nvim rg fd fzf zsh just bats`.
147	- oh-my-zsh plugins present (`zsh-autosuggestions`, `zsh-syntax-highlighting`, `zsh-completions`).
148	- Unit tests pass under the container's zsh (catches "works on my Mac" regressions).
149	
150	Invoked by `just docker-test` → `docker compose run --build --rm test` → `bats /tmp/dotfiles-source/tests/smoke`.
151	
152	---
153	
154	## Running tests
155	
156	```bash
157	# Fast feedback loop (no Docker, no network, sub-second)
158	just bats
159	
160	# Smoke tests inside a clean Ubuntu container (slow — builds image)
161	just docker-test
162	
163	# Everything: ansible syntax + pre-commit + bats + docker-test
164	just check-all
165	```
166	
167	---
168	
169	## Patterns worth reusing
170	
171	### Testing zsh code from bats
172	
173	Bats is bash-based, so drive zsh as a subprocess. Use `zsh -f -c 'source FILE; <call>'` to skip startup files (isolates the code under test) and capture output via `run` or `$(...)`:
174	
175	```bash
176	@test "my zsh function does X" {
177	  result="$(zsh -f -c "
178	    source '$REPO_ROOT/dot_config/zsh/tools/my_file.zsh'
179	    my_function arg1 arg2
180	  ")"
181	  [ "$result" = "expected" ]
182	}
183	```
184	
185	### Stubbing external commands
186	
187	Prepend a temp dir to `PATH` containing a fake binary:
188	
189	```bash
190	@test "probe order regression" {
191	  setup_path_stub   # populates $BATS_STUB_DIR, updates $PATH
192	
193	  cat > "$BATS_STUB_DIR/nc" <<'EOF'
194	#!/usr/bin/env bash
195	port=""
196	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do port="$1"; shift; done
197	[ "$port" = "$EXPECT_PORT" ] && exit 0 || exit 1
198	EOF
199	  chmod +x "$BATS_STUB_DIR/nc"
200	
201	  EXPECT_PORT=1087 zsh -f -c "source '$REPO_ROOT/.../file.zsh'; my_probe"
202	}
203	```
204	
205	Bats runs every `@test` block in its own subshell, so `PATH` modifications don't leak across tests. `cleanup_path_stubs` (default `teardown`) removes the temp dirs.
206	
207	### Asserting zsh variables from bash
208	
209	Inside `zsh -f -c '...'`, use zsh indirect expansion (`${(P)v}`) to print a variable named in another variable:
210	
211	```bash
212	for v in http_proxy https_proxy HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy; do
213	  printf '%s=%s\n' "$v" "${(P)v}"
214	done
215	```
216	
217	Then bats asserts on the `$output`:
218	
219	```bash
220	[[ "$output" == *"http_proxy=http://test:1234"* ]]
221	```
222	
223	---
224	
225	## shellcheck + shfmt
226	
227	[shellcheck](https://www.shellcheck.net/) is a static analyser for shell scripts. [shfmt](https://github.com/mvdan/sh) is a formatter / format-check. Both run via pre-commit in this repo. For generic pre-commit mechanics (cache location, `uv`-managed bootstrap Python, debugging broken hook envs), see [`docs/tools/pre-commit.md`](../tools/pre-commit.md).
228	
229	Pre-commit hook sources (see `.pre-commit-config.yaml`):
230	
231	- [`shellcheck-py`](https://github.com/shellcheck-py/shellcheck-py) — ships a Python-installable wheel of shellcheck, so pre-commit environments don't need a system-wide `shellcheck` binary.
232	- [`pre-commit-shfmt`](https://github.com/scop/pre-commit-shfmt) — pre-commit wrapper around `shfmt` with no Go toolchain required.
233	
234	### Other config-file syntax checks
235	
236	In addition to shell tooling, `.pre-commit-config.yaml` runs these [pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks](https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks) validators:
237	
238	- `check-yaml` — ansible playbooks, role definitions, docker-compose, pre-commit itself.
239	- `check-toml` — TV cable channel configs, starship, yazi, alacritty, etc. `.tmpl` files are excluded because chezmoi's `{{ ... }}` go-template tokens aren't valid TOML until rendered.
240	- `check-json` — VS Code settings, claude config, lazyvim lockfile, etc.
241	- `check-merge-conflict`, `check-added-large-files`, `detect-private-key`, `end-of-file-fixer`, `trailing-whitespace`.
242	
243	Ansible **playbook syntax** is checked via `just ansible-syntax-check` / `just lint`, not pre-commit — running a full playbook parse on every commit is too slow for the pre-commit hot path. Run `just lint` manually before pushing ansible-touching changes.
244	
245	Hook scope (see `.pre-commit-config.yaml`): **`^scripts/[^/]+\.sh$` only**. This excludes:
246	
247	- `dot_config/zsh/**/*.zsh` — zsh-specific syntax (`(( ... ))` math, `${(P)v}` expansion flags, `print -u2`, `emulate -L zsh`, `zmodload`) trips shellcheck's bash parser and produces too many false positives.
248	- `*.sh.tmpl` — chezmoi go-template tokens (`{{ if eq .profile "macos" }}`) look like unbalanced braces to shellcheck.
249	- `scripts/adhoc/*.sh` — experimental / throwaway scripts by convention.
250	
251	If a zsh file needs static analysis later, the best options are:
252	
253	- Run shellcheck with `# shellcheck shell=bash` and manually silence known-false positives — tedious.
254	- Switch to a zsh-aware linter (there isn't a widely adopted one).
255	- Or just write a Bats test that covers the behaviour you care about.
256	
257	Quick commands:
258	
259	```bash
260	# Run only shellcheck on all files
261	pre-commit run shellcheck --all-files
262	
263	# Run only shfmt
264	pre-commit run shfmt --all-files
265	
266	# shfmt is in diff mode (-d) — to actually rewrite files, install shfmt
267	# locally and run:
268	shfmt -i 2 -ci -bn -w scripts/*.sh
269	```
270	
271	---
272	
273	## Adding a new test
274	
275	1. Decide unit vs smoke:
276	   - Pure logic with stub-able inputs → `tests/unit/`.
277	   - Assertions about post-install system state → `tests/smoke/`.
278	2. Create `tests/unit/<thing>.bats` (or smoke/). Start with:
279	   ```bash
280	   #!/usr/bin/env bats
281	   load "../test_helper.bash"
282	
283	   @test "brief description" {
284	     run some-command
285	     [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
286	   }
287	   ```
288	3. Run `just bats` (or `just docker-test`) to verify.
289	4. If the test needs a stub, use `setup_path_stub` + `$BATS_STUB_DIR`.
290	
291	Rule of thumb for deciding whether a test is worth adding: **would a silent regression here cost me more than ten minutes to diagnose?** If no, skip the test. Personal dotfiles don't need 80% coverage.
292

 `./docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md`

```text
1	# Shared sudo session for `chezmoi apply`
2	
3	All three `run_*` scripts (`run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl`, `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`, `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl`) share a single sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`. The user is prompted **once** at the very start of `chezmoi apply` and every downstream script reuses the cached credential silently.
4	
5	> **Hard rule for new run-scripts**: do NOT re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper instead.
6	
7	## How it's wired
8	
9	- Helper lives at `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` (plain bash, ~270 lines). It is **never deployed** — `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`.
10	- Each `run_*.sh.tmpl` inlines the helper at render time via `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` — no runtime sourcing, no path lookup back to the source tree.
11	- A template-time `NEED_SUDO` flag (`1`/`0`) short-circuits the whole mechanism when no script in the flow will touch sudo (e.g. `noRoot=true` on Linux, or macOS without `installBrewApps`/`installInputMethod`).
12	
13	## Runtime state
14	
15	Lives under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/` (mode 0700; falls back to `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/` when `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is unset):
16	
17	| File | Mode | Contents |
18	|------|------|----------|
19	| `sudo.pass` | 0600 | raw password + `\n`, piped into `sudo -S` by `sudo_run` |
20	| `ansible-become.yml` | 0600 | `ansible_become_password: "…"` YAML for `ansible-playbook -e @file` |
21	| `keepalive.pid` | 0600 | detached watchdog PID |
22	| `chezmoi.pid` | 0600 | ancestor chezmoi PID the watchdog watches |
23	
24	## Cleanup model
25	
26	Hybrid, because per-script `trap … EXIT` would wipe state before the *next* script can reuse it:
27	
28	- Signal traps on `INT`/`TERM`/`HUP` → `sudo_session_abort` kills the watchdog + `rm -rf`s the state dir. User Ctrl+C never leaves the secret on disk.
29	- End-of-flow cleanup → the watchdog (detached via `setsid`) watches the chezmoi ancestor PID. When chezmoi exits, the watchdog self-terminates and `rm -rf`s the state dir. Refreshes the TTY sudo timestamp every 50 s so cask pkg installers (`sudo /usr/sbin/installer`) find a live ticket.
30	
31	## Public API
32	
33	All three run-scripts use these:
34	
35	| Function | Purpose |
36	|---|---|
37	| `sudo_session_init [label]` | Idempotent: if state valid re-exports env vars; else prompts once on `/dev/tty`, validates, writes files, spawns watchdog. Returns non-zero when neither passwordless nor TTY-interactive. Call this BEFORE any sudo. |
38	| `sudo_run <cmd ...>` | Thin wrapper: `sudo -S -p '' -- "$@" <sudo.pass` — pipes cached password, never puts it in argv. Falls back to plain `sudo` when passwordless. Use for bootstrap's `apt-get` calls. |
39	| `sudo_session_skip_reason` | Branch helper. Prints `"cached"` / `"passwordless"` / `"non-interactive"` / `""`. Used by ansible + brew scripts to pick between `-e @file`, `""` flags, or manual-instruction fallback. |
40	| `sudo_session_warm_cache` | Refreshes the current TTY's sudo timestamp with the cached password. Call before tools like `brew bundle` whose cask pkg installers invoke `sudo` internally and rely on timestamp caching rather than accepting a piped password. |
41	
42	**Exports on success**: `CHEZMOI_SUDO_STATE_DIR`, `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASS_FILE`, `CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE`, `CHEZMOI_SUDO_KEEPALIVE_PID`.
43	
44	## Non-interactive password injection (`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE`)
45	
46	Used by remote orchestrators that have no TTY at the consuming end — currently
47	[`scripts/fleet_apply.py`](../../scripts/fleet_apply.py) over SSH.
48	
49	When `sudo_session_init` is called and:
50	
51	1. The shared state dir is **not** already populated, AND
52	2. Sudo is **not** passwordless, AND
53	3. `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` env var points to a readable file containing
54	   the password (one line, optional trailing `\n`),
55	
56	then the file is read, validated with `sudo -S -v -p ''`, and adopted into the
57	shared state dir exactly as if it had been entered interactively. The watchdog
58	spawns the same way; subsequent run-scripts hit the cached-state branch and
59	never see the env var (it's `unset` after adoption).
60	
61	If the password is rejected by sudo, init fails with a clear stderr message
62	instead of silently falling through to the TTY branch.
63	
64	The orchestrator on the controller side is responsible for placing that 0600
65	file on the remote and cleaning it up — see
66	[`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](fleet-apply.md) for the contract.
67	
68	## Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script
69	
70	1. `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top of the template.
71	2. Decide the `NEED_SUDO` template flag for your script (mirror the conditions in existing run-scripts).
72	3. Call `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"`; branch on the return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason`.
73	4. Run privileged commands via `sudo_run …` (simple cases) or pass `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` to ansible.
74	
75	## Do NOT
76	
77	- Run `sudo -k` (it invalidates the shared cache for the entire flow).
78	- Register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
79	- Read the password into a shell variable and leave it there — always via `sudo -S <file`, never as an env var or command argument.
80
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# `.chezmoiscripts/` layout
2	
3	This repo organises auto-run scripts into a two-bucket layout under
4	`.chezmoiscripts/` that encodes **scope** (which machines should re-run
5	when the script changes) in the directory name:
6	
7	```
8	.chezmoiscripts/
9	├── global/   # Runs on every machine that consumes this repo
10	│   ├── run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl
11	│   ├── run_onchange_after_25_bat_theme.sh.tmpl
12	│   ├── run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl
13	│   ├── run_onchange_after_32_raycast_config.sh.tmpl
14	│   └── run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl
15	└── repo/     # Runs only when the chezmoi source dir IS this repo working tree
16	    └── run_onchange_after_45_bootstrap_skills.sh.tmpl
17	```
18	
19	Plus four `run_*before_*` scripts that intentionally stayed at the
20	repo root — see [What's still at the repo root](#whats-still-at-the-repo-root-and-why)
21	below.
22	
23	## What's still at the repo root (and why)
24	
25	Four `run_*before_*` scripts deliberately stayed at the repo root:
26	
27	| Script | Phase | Why not moved |
28	|---|---|---|
29	| `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` | once, before | sudo session init + locale fix; `run_once_*` is path-keyed in chezmoi state, so moving forces a re-run on every machine |
30	| `run_before_01_backup_dotfiles.sh.tmpl` | every, before | Backs up dotfiles before chezmoi overwrites. Three modes via `backupMode`: `smart` (default; uses `chezmoi status` to back up only files apply would modify/delete — clean host produces no backup), `full` (hardcoded allowlist, onboarding mode), `off`. Inspect via `just list-backups` / `just diff-backup <TS>`. |
31	| `run_once_before_02_fix_intel_homebrew.sh.tmpl` | once, before | Intel Mac brew prefix migration; same `run_once_*` state-tracking concern as `00` |
32	| `run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl` | once, before | One-shot opencode CLI config migration; would re-run if path changes |
33	
34	The `run_once_*` scripts are state-tracked **by path** in
35	`chezmoi state` (the `scriptState` bucket is keyed on a hash that
36	includes the script's source path). Moving them would either re-run the
37	once-only logic on every existing machine, or require coordinated
38	`chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=scriptState` surgery on each host.
39	The `run_onchange_after_*` scripts moved earlier had the same property
40	but their re-run cost was acceptable (idempotent ansible / brew bundle);
41	for `run_once_before_*` the cost is higher and less predictable
42	(`00_bootstrap` reinstalls base packages, `50_opencode_migrate` re-applies
43	a one-shot migration).
44	
45	Plus there's no scope ambiguity to resolve: all four are global. The
46	`global/` vs `repo/` split that motivated the move for `_after_` scripts
47	doesn't exist on the `_before_` side, so the directory wouldn't carry
48	information.
49	
50	If a future `run_*before_*` script genuinely needs `repo/` scope
51	(e.g. a project-skills bootstrap that must run before chezmoi applies),
52	revisit this decision — at that point the bucket starts to encode
53	scope and the move is worth the re-run cost.
54	
55	## Why nested?
56	
57	Two reasons:
58	
59	1. **Scope is a hard contract** — `repo/` scripts must NOT fire on machines
60	   that only consume the repo (e.g. a remote server `chezmoi init`'d from
61	   the GitHub URL). Encoding the scope in the path makes the contract
62	   visible at a glance and harder to violate by accident; the script
63	   itself still has to gate on `eq .chezmoi.sourceDir <repo-root>`.
64	2. **Repo-root tidiness** — six `run_onchange_after_*.sh.tmpl` files at
65	   the top level pushed past the noise threshold. The 2-bucket split keeps
66	   `ls` of the repo root scannable without losing the numeric phase
67	   ordering that controls run order within each bucket.
68	
69	## Why this works (chezmoi behaviour)
70	
71	`.chezmoiscripts/` accepts subdirectories. They are not part of any public
72	"feature" but the behaviour has been confirmed in chezmoi issues:
73	
74	- [twpayne/chezmoi#2013 — `.chezmoiscripts` sub directories](https://github.com/twpayne/chezmoi/issues/2013)
75	- [twpayne/chezmoi#3246 — ASCII ordering in subdirectories](https://github.com/twpayne/chezmoi/issues/3246)
76	
77	The maintainer's own dotfiles use the same pattern:
78	[twpayne/dotfiles](https://github.com/twpayne/dotfiles).
79	
80	### Application order
81	
82	Within each `before_` / `after_` phase, chezmoi sorts scripts by their
83	**full path** in ASCII order (case-sensitive). For our layout:
84	
85	```
86	.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl
87	.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_25_bat_theme.sh.tmpl
88	.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl
89	.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_32_raycast_config.sh.tmpl
90	.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl
91	.chezmoiscripts/repo/run_onchange_after_45_bootstrap_skills.sh.tmpl
92	```
93	
94	`g` < `r` in ASCII, so `global/` always sorts before `repo/`. Within
95	each bucket the numeric prefix takes over (`20 < 25 < 30 < …`). The
96	overall order matches what the flat layout produced — by design — so
97	this refactor was a pure structural change with no behaviour delta.
98	
99	If we later add `darwin/` / `linux/` subdirs underneath `global/`, those
100	nested scripts still sort by their full path; mixing
101	`global/run_onchange_after_20_*` with `global/darwin/run_onchange_after_30_*`
102	will alphabetise as:
103	
104	```
105	global/darwin/run_onchange_after_30_…    # `d` < `r`, so subdir wins!
106	global/run_onchange_after_20_…
107	```
108	
109	This is a footgun: **adding a subdir under `global/` will reorder existing
110	scripts** because directory names sort against file names alphabetically.
111	If/when we add OS subdirs, plan the rename so the order is intentional
112	(e.g. prefix the OS dirs with `_darwin/` `_linux/` to push them past
113	top-level files alphabetically).
114	
115	## What goes where
116	
117	- **`global/`** — anything that must converge state on every machine
118	  consuming this repo. Examples:
119	  - Ansible roles (system packages, dotfile-adjacent tools)
120	  - Brewfile sync
121	  - bat theme rebuild
122	  - Raycast config import (gated on `syncRaycast` opt-in)
123	  - Global skills restore (`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` → `~/.agents/skills/`)
124	
125	- **`repo/`** — anything that ONLY makes sense when the local source dir
126	  IS this repo's working tree (not a deploy-from-GitHub consumer). Today
127	  this is just project-scope skills bootstrap (`./skills-lock.json` →
128	  `./.agents/skills/`); the script's first action is to check
129	  `[[ "$(cd ~/.local/share/chezmoi && pwd)" == "$source_dir" ]]` and
130	  exit 0 otherwise.
131	
132	If you add a script that should run **only on Apple Silicon** or
133	**only with sudo** — that's still scope, but a different axis (OS / capability),
134	and the current 2-bucket layout doesn't carve a place for it. Three options:
135	
136	1. Put it in the appropriate scope bucket and gate inside the script with
137	   a chezmoi template guard (`{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" }}exit 0{{ end }}`).
138	   This is what we do today; works for ≤ 2 OS-only scripts.
139	2. Add `global/darwin/` and `global/linux/` subdirs once OS-only scripts
140	   reach ~3+. Re-evaluate the alphabetical-ordering footgun above first.
141	3. Document an alternative layout in `backlog/chezmoiscripts-namespace-refactor.md`
142	   and revisit the structural decision wholesale.
143	
144	## Cross-references
145	
146	- Decision log: [`backlog/chezmoiscripts-namespace-refactor.md`](../../backlog/chezmoiscripts-namespace-refactor.md)
147	- Auto-run scripts table: [`docs/this_repo/architecture.md`](architecture.md)
148	- chezmoi docs: [`.chezmoiscripts/`](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/special-directories/chezmoiscripts/),
149	  [Application order](https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/application-order/)
150
```

```text
1	# Fleet apply — multi-host `chezmoi update` orchestrator
2	
3	> **TL;DR** — `just fleet-apply` runs `chezmoi update --init` on every host
4	> listed in `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`, in parallel, with optional sudo
5	> password injection sourced from plaintext / interactive prompt / Bitwarden
6	> CLI. Per-host logs land under `logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log`
7	> and the process exits with the number of failed hosts (capped at 125).
8	
9	Implementation: [`scripts/fleet_apply.py`](../../scripts/fleet_apply.py)
10	(uv inline-script: `asyncssh` + `tyro` + `rich`).
11	
12	See also: [fleet-apply-vs-fabric.md](fleet-apply-vs-fabric.md) for an
13	archaeological comparison against the author's 2018-era Fabric `fabfile.py`
14	on RaspPi-Cluster — same problem shape, ~7 years of operational lessons
15	encoded into the current implementation.
16	
17	## When to use
18	
19	You edited dotfiles on the workstation, pushed to the repo's git remote, and
20	now want every laptop / VM / lab box to pick up the change without sshing into
21	each one and typing the sudo password by hand.
22	
23	## When NOT to use
24	
25	- This tool **does not** push the dotfiles repo itself — every remote runs
26	  `chezmoi update`, which does `git pull` on the remote's source dir. Your
27	  changes must already be reachable by the remotes (push to GitHub / your
28	  internal git host first).
29	- It does not run `just upgrade-*` on remotes. That's a separate concern; this
30	  tool stays scoped to chezmoi apply.
31	- It does not provision new hosts. Each remote must already have `chezmoi`
32	  installed and `chezmoi init` completed at least once.
33	
34	## Inventory file
35	
36	Path: `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`. Seeded **once** by chezmoi from
37	[`dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl).
38	The `create_private_` prefix means:
39	
40	- `create_` → chezmoi seeds the file on first apply, then never touches it
41	  again. Your edits survive every `chezmoi apply`.
42	- `private_` → file mode 0600. Safe to keep plaintext sudo passwords here.
43	- To reset the seed: `rm ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml && chezmoi apply`.
44	
45	### Schema
46	
47	```toml
48	[defaults]                    # merged into every host (host keys override)
49	chezmoi_path    = "chezmoi"   # PATH binary; e.g. "~/.local/bin/chezmoi" if no-root
50	connect_timeout = 15
51	command_timeout = 1800
52	
53	[[hosts]]
54	name            = "lab-box"   # required, unique display name
55	ssh_alias       = "lab-box"   # preferred: matches `Host lab-box` in ~/.ssh/config
56	# OR explicit connection (used when no ssh_alias):
57	hostname        = "203.0.113.42"
58	user            = "dwlee"
59	port            = 22
60	identity_file   = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
61	
62	no_root_machine = false       # MUST mirror the chezmoi `noRoot=` value used at
63	                              # `chezmoi init` time on that remote (see below)
64	chezmoi_path    = "chezmoi"   # override defaults per-host
65	local           = false       # set true to run chezmoi locally (no SSH); see
66	                              # "Local host execution" section below
67	extra_env       = { FOO = "bar" }   # extra env vars for the remote chezmoi run
68	
69	password_source = { type = "...", ... }   # see "Password sources" below
70	```
71	
72	### Password sources
73	
74	| `type` | Extra keys | Behaviour |
75	|---|---|---|
76	| `none` (default) | — | No password injected. Suitable for `no_root_machine = true` hosts. |
77	| `plain` | `value = "..."` | Read straight from TOML. Relies on file mode 0600. |
78	| `prompt` | — | `getpass()` once at startup, never persisted to disk. |
79	| `bitwarden` | `item = "ssh-host-sudo"` | `bw get password <item>` at startup. Requires `bw unlock` + `BW_SESSION` exported. |
80	
81	### `no_root_machine` semantics
82	
83	This flag **describes** the remote, it does not change it. Each remote was
84	configured at `chezmoi init` time with a `noRoot` boolean (see
85	[`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:48`](../../.chezmoi.toml.tmpl)) that's now baked into
86	`~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` on that machine.
87	
88	- Set `no_root_machine = true` for hosts where the remote's `noRoot = true` —
89	  fleet_apply skips sudo entirely (no password file written, run-scripts'
90	  `sudo_session_init` returns "non-interactive" branch and skips sudo work).
91	- Set `no_root_machine = false` for hosts where the remote's `noRoot = false`
92	## How sudo password reaches the remote
93	
94	`scripts/fleet_apply.py` does **not** echo the password into the command line.
95	The remote command (assembled by `build_remote_command()`) reads stdin into
96	`~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass` (mode 0600, `umask 077`), exports
97	`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE=$PWD/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass`, runs
98	`chezmoi update`, then `trap … EXIT` removes the file (even on crash).
99	
100	On the remote, `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh::sudo_session_init` was extended
101	with a non-interactive injection path: when `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE`
102	points to a readable file, the password is validated with `sudo -S -v`, then
103	adopted into the shared state dir (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/`)
104	exactly the same way an interactive prompt would be — including the watchdog
105	that holds the sudo timestamp warm and writes `ansible-become.yml` for
106	ansible roles. **Subsequent run-scripts inside the same `chezmoi update` see
107	the cached state and never re-prompt.**
108	
109	Pass file lifecycle:
110	- `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass` is the orchestrator's drop-off; removed
111	  by the SSH command's `trap` once chezmoi exits.
112	- `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/sudo.pass` is the shared state dir
113	  managed by `sudo_shared.sh`; cleaned up by the existing watchdog when the
114	  ancestor `chezmoi` PID exits.
115	
116	## Connection: ssh_config alias vs explicit
117	
118	`asyncssh.connect(host=...)` reads `~/.ssh/config` like the OpenSSH client.
119	Prefer `ssh_alias`:
120	
121	```
122	# ~/.ssh/config
123	Host lab-box
124	    HostName 10.0.0.42
125	    User dwlee
126	    ProxyJump bastion
127	    IdentityAgent ~/.1password/agent.sock     # 1Password SSH agent
128	```
129	
130	```toml
131	# machines.toml
132	[[hosts]]
133	name      = "lab-box"
134	ssh_alias = "lab-box"          # ← inherits everything above, including ProxyJump
135	```
136	
137	If a host has no ssh_config entry, fall back to explicit
138	`hostname` / `user` / `port` / `identity_file`.
139	
140	## Local host execution (`local = true`)
141	
142	To include the orchestrator machine itself in a fleet apply, add a host
143	with `local = true`:
144	
145	```toml
146	[[hosts]]
147	name            = "self"
148	local           = true
149	no_root_machine = true   # set false if your local apply needs sudo
150	```
151	
152	Local hosts skip asyncssh entirely — chezmoi runs as a direct
153	subprocess (`asyncio.create_subprocess_exec`) inheriting the
154	orchestrator's PATH, sudoers state, and tty. Sudo password injection
155	is not used; if chezmoi needs root it'll prompt on the parent terminal.
156	The `kill-orphans` subcommand also skips local hosts (killing local
157	chezmoi processes from the same shell session would kill `fleet_apply`
158	itself). All other features — log files, live table, `--force`,
159	`--keep-going`, `--command-timeout`, parallelism — work identically.
160	
161	`ssh_alias`, `hostname`, `user`, `port`, `identity_file` are ignored
162	when `local = true`. `chezmoi_path = "auto"` still works (subprocess
163	inherits the calling shell's PATH, which is where the orchestrator
164	itself found `chezmoi`).
165	
166	## Commands
167	
168	```bash
169	just fleet-apply                                # parallel, all hosts, update --init
170	just fleet-apply-dry-run                        # `chezmoi diff` instead of update
171	just fleet-apply-one lab-box                    # single host, --serial mode
172	just fleet-apply --hosts lab-box,vps-tokyo      # subset
173	just fleet-apply --exclude throwaway-vm         # all except
174	just fleet-apply --max-parallel 3               # throttle SSH fan-out
175	just fleet-apply --no-init                      # `chezmoi apply` (skip update)
176	just fleet-apply --serial                       # one at a time, no live table
177	just fleet-apply --command-timeout 600          # tighter timeout for warm fleets
178	just fleet-apply-kill                           # kill orphan chezmoi/ansible on every host
179	```
180	
181	### Vibe-loop recipes (fast iteration)
182	
183	```bash
184	just fleet-diff lab-box                         # `chezmoi diff` on ONE host, serial output
185	just fleet-apply-file .zshrc                    # apply ONE file across the fleet, skip ansible
186	just fleet-apply-file .config/zsh/aliases.zsh --hosts lab-box
187	just fleet-apply-branch feature/new-tmux        # pin remotes to a branch (ff-only)
188	just fleet-apply-branch-force feature/new-tmux  # … allow `git reset --hard` (after rebase)
189	```
190	
191	`fleet-apply-file PATH` is the headline vibe-loop command:
192	
193	- Skips `chezmoi update` (and thus the slow `run_*` scripts: ansible, Brewfile, Linuxbrew refresh).
194	- Prepends `git -C $(chezmoi source-path) pull --ff-only` so the remote checkout has your latest commit before `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts <PATH>` re-renders just that one target.
195	- PATH is a chezmoi *target* path (relative to `$HOME`), e.g. `.zshrc`, `.config/tmux/tmux.conf`, `.gitconfig`. NOT a source path like `dot_zshrc`.
196	- Round-trip on a warm fleet is typically ~5-15 seconds per host vs 5-30 minutes for a full `fleet-apply`.
197	- You still need to `git push` first — the remote runs `git pull` on its checkout. Local hosts (`local = true`) skip the pull because the source IS your editor's working tree.
198	- Drift / `--force` semantics are unchanged: pass `--force` if you've also edited the file by hand on the remote and want to overwrite.
199	
200	`fleet-apply-branch BRANCH` lets you iterate on a feature branch without polluting `main`:
201	
202	- Each remote runs `git fetch origin BRANCH && git checkout -B BRANCH origin/BRANCH && git merge --ff-only origin/BRANCH` before `chezmoi apply`.
203	- Mode is forced to `apply` (since `chezmoi update` would re-pull `main` and undo the checkout).
204	- Default merge is `--ff-only`: fails loud if the remote checkout has divergence. Use `fleet-apply-branch-force` (which adds `--force-checkout`) to swap in `git reset --hard origin/BRANCH` — necessary after you've force-pushed a rebased topic branch.
205	- Local hosts ignore `--branch` entirely: their source dir is your working tree, switching it under your editor would be hostile. The skip is logged.
206	- Compose with `--apply-only-path` for the fastest possible loop: `just fleet-apply --branch tmp/test --apply-only-path .config/foo/bar.toml --hosts lab-box`.
207	
208	
209	## Conflict handling: `--force` vs `--keep-going`
210	
211	When a remote file has drifted from what chezmoi last wrote (someone
212	edited it directly on the host), chezmoi normally prompts on `/dev/tty`
213	to ask whether to overwrite. fleet_apply runs without a PTY, so that
214	prompt dies with `chezmoi: <file>: could not open a new TTY: open
215	/dev/tty: no such device or address`. Two flags control the response:
216	
217	| Flag | Default | Effect on the conflicting file | Effect on the rest of the apply |
218	|---|---|---|---|
219	| `--keep-going` / `--no-keep-going` | **on** | Left **unchanged** (no override) | Continues — other files still apply |
220	| `--force` / `--no-force` | **off** | **Overwritten** with template render | Same |
221	
222	Default combination (`--keep-going`, no `--force`) = **non-destructive**:
223	all clean files apply, drifted files are skipped. fleet_apply parses the
224	chezmoi stderr; if the host's *only* failure is "could not open a new TTY"
225	on one or more drifted targets, it classifies the host as **`drift`**
226	(yellow `⚠`) instead of **`failed`** (red `✗`). The summary lists the
227	drifted files per host so you know exactly what needs attention:
228	
229	```
230	Summary: 5 hosts, 3 ok, 1 failed, 1 drift, 0 skipped
231	  ✗ david_ubuntu  rc=1  log=…/david_ubuntu.log     # real failure
232	  ⚠ hanru_mac     drift in: .config/foo.toml       # only a drift skip
233	                  log=…/hanru_mac.log
234	                  (resolve: --force, or sync edits back to source)
235	```
236	
237	Drift hosts do **not** count toward the process exit code — only `failed`
238	hosts do. This is intentional: drift is a "do something later" signal, not
239	a CI failure. If a host has BOTH a drift skip AND an unrelated error
240	(ansible task, network timeout, etc.) it will be classified as `failed`,
241	not `drift`, so real errors are never silently downgraded.
242	
243	To resolve a drift, either:
244	
245	- Migrate the drift into a per-machine override file (e.g. `~/.gitconfig.local`,
246	  see below) and re-run.
247	- Or run `just fleet-apply --force` once to let the canonical template win
248	  (also accepts `--hosts <name>` to scope it).
249	- Or, for a single file you've already decided about, ssh in and run
250	  `chezmoi apply --force <relpath>` directly — fastest fix when the
251	  template is right but the target is stale.
252	
253	## Per-machine git overrides (`~/.gitconfig.local`)
254	
255	Common drift on `.gitconfig` is host-specific git config that legitimately
256	belongs to that one machine — `[safe] directory = /mnt/NAS/...` (host-mounted
257	NAS), `[credential "https://gitlab.com"]` (glab CLI helper), `[http] proxy = ...`
258	(corporate proxy), etc. Putting these in the chezmoi-managed
259	`dot_gitconfig.tmpl` is wrong (they don't apply to other hosts);
260	hand-editing them onto each remote also fails because every fleet apply
261	then trips the "drifted from template" prompt.
262	
263	`dot_gitconfig.tmpl` therefore ends with:
264	
265	```gitconfig
266	[include]
267	    path = ~/.gitconfig.local
268	```
269	
270	`include.path` is silently skipped by git when the file doesn't exist
271	(no error), so machines without overrides are unaffected. `~/.gitconfig.local`
272	is git-ignored by chezmoi via `.chezmoiignore` — chezmoi will never seed,
273	overwrite, or diff it. Same self-managed pattern as `~/.zshrc.adhoc`
274	for shell customisations.
275	
276	To migrate per-host lines that already drifted on a remote:
277	
278	```bash
279	ssh <host> 'chezmoi --no-pager diff .gitconfig'   # see what diverged
280	ssh <host> bash -s <<'EOF'
281	  # Move the host-specific block out of the managed file:
282	  # (manually copy the [safe] / [credential] / [http] sections from
283	  # ~/.gitconfig into ~/.gitconfig.local with your editor of choice)
284	  ${EDITOR:-vi} ~/.gitconfig.local
285	  ${EDITOR:-vi} ~/.gitconfig         # delete the migrated lines
286	EOF
287	just fleet-apply-one <host>                       # should now be clean
288	```
289	
290	## Timeouts
291	
292	| Flag | Default | Rationale |
293	|---|---|---|
294	| `--connect-timeout` | 30 s | SSH banner + auth handshake. Bump for high-latency or relay-heavy hosts. |
295	| `--command-timeout` | 7200 s (2 h) | Generous to cover first-run apply: Linuxbrew install (10–20 min) + 22 ansible roles + Brewfile cask downloads (GUI apps; can be 20+ min on slow links) + python_uv_tools / npm / cargo bootstrap. After your fleet is past first-run, drop to e.g. `--command-timeout 600` (10 min) — steady-state re-apply on a warm machine usually finishes in 1–5 min. |
296	
297	If `--command-timeout` fires, the orchestrator sends SIGTERM via the SSH
298	channel **and** closes the channel (which delivers SIGHUP to the remote
299	shell, which the wrapper's trap propagates to chezmoi). The remote should
300	fully exit within seconds.
301	
302	### When a host hangs
303	
304	`command_timeout` is the **outer** budget — it kills the entire chezmoi+ansible chain when blown. Ansible itself has **no per-task timeout**, so a stuck `npm install`, `apt update` retry loop, or `git clone` against a slow mirror will burn the whole 2-hour budget if you let it.
305	
306	Typical hang symptoms:
307	
308	- `--status` shows the host as `running pids=...` for tens of minutes
309	- `--tail HOST` log stops at a `[N] TASK · …` line and never advances
310	- Drilling into the remote: `ssh HOST pstree -p $PID` shows `python3 → /bin/sh -c "… npm install …"` (or apt / git / cargo equivalents) at the leaf
311	
312	Recovery flow:
313	
314	1. **Identify the stuck task** via `--tail HOST` (last visible TASK number) and `ssh HOST pstree` to confirm the leaf process.
315	2. **Kill the run**: `just fleet-apply-kill --hosts HOST` — broadcasts `pkill -TERM` then `-KILL` to chezmoi/ansible/orphans.
316	3. **Bound the next attempt**: re-run with `--command-timeout 600` (or whatever's reasonable for steady-state) so a recurrence won't burn 2 hours again.
317	4. **If the same task keeps stuck**: it's an ansible role / network issue, not a fleet-apply bug. Add `timeout: 300` or `async: 600 poll: 30` to the offending ansible task in `dot_ansible/roles/<role>/tasks/main.yml`.
318	
319	`abandoned` state in `--status` (red, "no sentinel — wrapper SIGKILL'd?") means a previous run died abnormally — the wrapper got SIGKILL before its trap could write the exit sentinel. Common causes: parent OOM-killed, manual `kill -9`, or process-tree teardown cascading from a hung child. Treat it as a failure that left no recovery breadcrumb.
320	
321	## Killing orphans, checking status, re-attaching
322	
323	Local Ctrl+C, network drop, laptop sleep, or any other premature
324	disconnect is handled three ways:
325	
326	1. **In-band cleanup**: `build_remote_command()` wraps chezmoi in a shell
327	   wrapper with `trap '… pkill -TERM -P $_cz_pid …' INT TERM HUP`. asyncssh
328	   uses `request_pty='force'`, so the SSH channel close delivers SIGHUP to
329	   that wrapper shell on the remote — chezmoi (and any ansible-playbook
330	   children) get SIGTERM-ed and the wrapper proxies the exit code back.
331	   In practice this fires whenever asyncssh actually closes the channel
332	   (which is most cases, including normal SIGINT on the controller).
333	
334	2. **Out-of-band rescue**: if even the in-band trap didn't fire (e.g.
335	   `kill -9` on `fleet_apply.py`, or asyncssh closed the channel
336	   "cleanly" without a HUP delivery), the remote chezmoi/ansible may
337	   still be running:
338	
339	   ```bash
340	   just fleet-apply-kill                       # all hosts
341	   just fleet-apply-kill --hosts lab-box       # specific host
342	   ```
343	
344	   This connects to each host and runs `pkill -TERM -u "$(id -un)" -x
345	   chezmoi`, then `pkill -TERM -x ansible-playbook` and `ansible`, waits
346	   1 s, then SIGKILLs anything still alive. No chezmoi command is sent,
347	   so this is safe to run any time the fleet looks "stuck".
348	
349	3. **Status probe + live tail re-attach** (added after observing that
350	   asyncssh + a slow laptop-side kill sometimes leaves remote work
351	   running for many minutes silently):
352	
353	   ```bash
354	   just fleet-apply-status                     # which hosts are still busy?
355	   just fleet-apply-status --hosts ts_nas      # one host
356	   just fleet-apply-watch                      # poll every 10s until idle
357	   just fleet-apply-tail jingle207             # follow latest run on this host
358	   just fleet-apply-tail jingle207:20260422T140446Z
359	                                               # pin a specific run id
360	   ```
361	
362	   Each remote run tees chezmoi's combined stdout/stderr to
363	   `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/logs/<run_id>.log` and drops a sentinel
364	   `<run_id>.exit` file containing the final exit code when the run
365	   finishes. `--status` reads both: it shows `running` (live PIDs +
366	   their numbers), `finished` (with the exit code), or `idle` per host,
367	   plus the last 5 lines of the latest log inline for quick context.
368	   `--tail` does a `tail -F` on the log over a fresh SSH session and
369	   exits cleanly when the sentinel appears (or you Ctrl+C the viewer
370	   — the remote run keeps going).
371	
372	   `--watch N` (or `just fleet-apply-watch` which presets N=10) repeats
373	   `--status` every N seconds until every host reports finished/idle,
374	   then exits 0. Use this as a passive "wait for the fleet to settle"
375	   cursor after killing the controller — no need to keep pressing
376	   ↑↩ to re-poll. Subsequent polls suppress the per-host log tail to
377	   keep output compact.
378	
379	   **Self / `local = true` hosts** are first-class here: their logs
380	   land in `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/logs/` on the orchestrator (same
381	   dir, no SSH round-trip). `--status` and `--tail self` work
382	   identically to SSH hosts. The PID filter excludes the probe's own
383	   process and parent so a `--status` invocation doesn't see itself.
384	
385	   Both probes are read-only: they never send a chezmoi command and
386	   never kill anything. Combine with `fleet-apply-kill` if you decide
387	   the remote work should stop.
388	
389	### Log retention
390	
391	Each per-host log dir keeps the **10 most recent** runs (`.log` +
392	`.exit` pair); older pairs are deleted at the end of the next run.
393	Override with `--keep-logs N` (`N=0` disables GC entirely if you want
394	to accumulate forever — you'll need to `rm -rf ~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/
395	logs` periodically yourself). GC happens AFTER the sentinel is
396	written, so the just-finished run is always inside the keep window.
397	
398	## Exit codes
399	
400	| Exit | Meaning |
401	|---|---|
402	| 0 | All selected hosts finished `chezmoi update` with rc 0, or only had recoverable drift skips (state = `drift`) |
403	| `N` (1–125) | `N` hosts genuinely failed (rc != 0 with errors *other than* drift skips, SSH error, timeout, or skipped due to missing sudo password) |
404	| 125 | More than 125 hosts failed (capped) |
405	| 2 | Config error (missing TOML, malformed schema) |
406	
407	`drift` hosts intentionally do NOT count as failures — see "Conflict
408	handling" above. They appear in the summary as `⚠` so a human notices, but
409	CI / cron loops keep passing as long as no real errors occur.
410	
411	## Logs
412	
413	Per-host log file: `logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log`. Each line is
414	prefixed `[out]` or `[err]`. The first two lines record the host metadata and
415	the **literal** remote command sent (which contains no password — only the
416	shell that pipes stdin into the pass file).
417	
418	`logs/` is **not** in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` because it lives in the source
419	repo only when you run `just fleet-apply` from inside the repo. Add it to
420	your local `.gitignore` if you don't already have one for build artifacts.
421	
422	## Troubleshooting
423	
424	- **`zsh:1: command not found: chezmoi` / rc=127** — non-interactive SSH
425	  shells don't source `~/.zshrc`, so `~/.local/bin` (or wherever your
426	  package manager put chezmoi) is not on PATH. The default
427	  `chezmoi_path = "auto"` already augments PATH with `~/.local/bin`,
428	  `~/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin`,
429	  `/usr/local/bin`, `/snap/bin` before invoking chezmoi — covers ~all
430	  installs. If your binary lives elsewhere, pin it explicitly:
431	  ```toml
432	  [[hosts]]
433	  name         = "weird-box"
434	  chezmoi_path = "/opt/custom/bin/chezmoi"
435	  ```
436	  Run `ssh <host> command -v chezmoi` (interactive) vs
437	  `ssh <host> 'command -v chezmoi'` (non-interactive) to see the gap.
438	- **`chezmoi: <file>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty: no such device or address`** —
439	  the file drifted on the remote and chezmoi tried to prompt. With the
440	  default `--keep-going`, the file is left untouched and the rest of
441	  the apply continues (host still reports rc!=0 so drift is visible).
442	  See [Conflict handling](#conflict-handling---force-vs---keep-going)
443	  for the resolution flow; for `.gitconfig` specifically, migrate the
444	  per-host lines to [`~/.gitconfig.local`](#per-machine-git-overrides-gitconfiglocal)
445	  instead of using `--force`.
446	- **`bw get password` fails** — run `bw unlock`, then `export BW_SESSION=...`.
447	- **`asyncssh.PermissionDenied`** — the alias resolves but auth failed.
448	  Test with `ssh <alias> echo ok` first; if you use the 1Password agent,
449	  ensure `IdentityAgent` is set in ssh_config and the agent is unlocked.
450	- **First-time host rejected with "Host key verification failed"** —
451	  fleet_apply uses `known_hosts=None` (= skip its own check, defer to your
452	  `~/.ssh/known_hosts`). Run `ssh <alias>` manually once to TOFU the key.
453	- **Remote chezmoi prompts for the noRoot question and stalls** — the host
454	  was never `chezmoi init`'d. SSH in and run `chezmoi init` once interactively.
455	- **Sudo phase fails immediately on a no_root_machine=false host** — the
456	  password the orchestrator resolved was wrong. The remote
457	  `sudo_shared.sh` rejects it with an explicit message in stderr (caught in
458	  the per-host log).
459	- **Host hangs forever during `chezmoi diff` / `update`** — usually chezmoi
460	  spawned its configured pager (`bat`, `delta`, `less`) which blocked
461	  waiting for terminal input. fleet_apply already passes `--no-pager` to
462	  every chezmoi invocation, but if you've added a custom subcommand /
463	  hookScript that bypasses chezmoi's pager handling, kill the orphan with
464	  `just fleet-apply-kill --hosts <host>` and check that subcommand for
465	  pager / `read` calls.
466	- **Run looks dead after Ctrl+C** — when you Ctrl+C `fleet_apply.py`
467	  asyncio cancels each task, which calls `proc.terminate()` and closes the
468	  SSH connection. The remote wrapper's trap catches the resulting SIGHUP
469	  and SIGTERMs the chezmoi tree. If anything still survives, run
470	  `just fleet-apply-kill` to broadcast `pkill -TERM` (then SIGKILL) to
471	  every host's `chezmoi` / `ansible-playbook` / `ansible` processes.
472

## Rime / Squirrel 客製化

Rime 的客製化原則是：不要直接改內建 schema 或發行版 yaml，而是使用 `*.custom.yaml` 搭配 `patch:` 覆寫。這也是官方 wiki 在 [CustomizationGuide](https://github.com/rime/home/wiki/CustomizationGuide) 中反覆使用的做法。

macOS 的 Squirrel 對應檔通常是：

- `squirrel.custom.yaml`：Squirrel 前端相關設定，例如 `style`、`app_options`
- `<schema>.custom.yaml`：特定方案的覆寫，例如 `bopomofo.custom.yaml`
- `default.custom.yaml`：全域預設覆寫

一個精簡、有代表性的 `squirrel.custom.yaml` 例子：

\```yaml
patch:
  app_options:
    com.microsoft.VSCode:
      ascii_mode: true
    com.apple.Terminal:
      ascii_mode: true
      no_inline: true
      vim_mode: true
      inline_preedit: false
\```

### `app_options`、`ascii_mode`、`no_inline`、`vim_mode`

- `app_options`：針對特定 app 的 bundle identifier 設定行為
- `ascii_mode: true`：該 app 預設以西文模式起始
- `no_inline: true`：停用行內組字 (inline composing)，通常在終端或編輯器更穩定
- `vim_mode: true`：目標是讓 Vim 類場景在離開 insert mode 時回到西文狀態，但在 macOS Terminal 類 app 上並不可靠
- `inline_preedit: false`：常和 `no_inline` 一起使用，降低終端內組字與 `Esc` 互動的干擾

這些選項在 Squirrel 內建的 `squirrel.yaml` 就能看到預設範例，例如 `com.apple.Terminal`、`com.googlecode.iterm2`、`org.vim.MacVim`。

### 修改後如何生效

修改 `*.custom.yaml` 後，需要在 macOS 輸入法選單對鼠鬚管執行「重新佈署」(redeploy)。

根據 Rime wiki 的說法，鼠鬚管是在系統語言文字選單中選擇「重新佈署」；對設定的修改會在重新佈署後生效。

### 查 app identifier

`app_options` 需要 bundle identifier。最直接的查法：

\```bash
osascript -e 'id of app "Visual Studio Code"'
osascript -e 'id of app "Terminal"'
\```

本機已驗證：

- `Visual Studio Code` -> `com.microsoft.VSCode`
- `Terminal` -> `com.apple.Terminal`

如果是第三方 app，也可以先用 Finder 確認正式 app 名稱，再用同樣方式查。

## 目前最在意的問題

### App 切換時輸入法狀態不可靠

目前痛點非常明確：在不同視窗或 app 之間切換後，很難確定當前到底是中文還是英文狀態。

典型情境：

1. 在某個視窗切成英文
2. `Command+Tab` 到下一個視窗
3. 狀態變成中文
4. 再切回原本視窗，狀態仍然可能是中文

這不是單靠 `app_options` 就能完全解決的問題。`app_options` 比較像是「進入 app 時的偏好」，不是可靠的全域狀態同步機制。

### `vim_mode` 在 Terminal 類 app 上不可靠

截至 `2026-03-31`，[`rime/squirrel#1023`](https://github.com/rime/squirrel/issues/1023) 仍是 open，問題標題就是「Terminal Vim_mode 無作用」，描述的現象與目前痛點一致：

- VS Code 可部分工作
- Terminal 內按 `Esc` 後不一定能回到西文
- 導致 `h j k l` 等按鍵仍進入中文輸入狀態

因此目前比較保守的結論是：

- `vim_mode` 可以保留，因為在部分 app 或部分情境仍有幫助
- 但不要把它當成 Terminal / iTerm / TUI 場景的可靠保證

## 已知限制與 upstream 狀態

以下狀態都以 `2026-03-31` 查閱 GitHub 為準。

### 1. 全域中英狀態目前仍無可靠官方解法

- [`rime/home#202`](https://github.com/rime/home/issues/202) 仍為 open。這個 issue 自 `2017-12-24` 起就在問「全域統一中英切換」。
- [`rime/squirrel#145`](https://github.com/rime/squirrel/issues/145) 仍為 open。主題就是「是否有可能將中英文輸入狀態作全域管理？」
- [`rime/librime#294`](https://github.com/rime/librime/issues/294) 仍為 open。它把問題提升到 librime 層，直接討論是否要讓所有 client app 共用 global input session / state。

綜合這幾個 issue，可以合理推論目前的限制不只是單一 app 設定問題，而是牽涉到 Squirrel 與 librime 的狀態模型 (state model)。

### 2. `global_ascii` 目前不能當成已正式可用的功能

- [`rime/squirrel#201`](https://github.com/rime/squirrel/pull/201) 是一個想把 `ascii_mode` 做成跨 app 全域狀態的舊 PR；截至 `2026-03-31` 已 closed，未合併
- [`rime/squirrel#1054`](https://github.com/rime/squirrel/pull/1054) 嘗試用 `global_ascii` 配置項處理這件事；截至 `2026-03-31` 也已 closed，且沒有 merged 標記

本機安裝的 Squirrel `1.1.2` 內容裡也找不到 `global_ascii` 關鍵字，因此目前不應把 `global_ascii` 寫成已可依賴的方案。

### 3. 實務上的結論

目前比較務實的策略是：

- 用 `app_options` 管理每個 app 的「偏好初始狀態」
- 在終端與編輯器場景搭配 `no_inline: true`
- 視需要保留 `vim_mode: true`，但承認它在 Terminal 類 app 上不可靠
- 如果重點是「可見性」(visibility)，用額外工具顯示當前輸入法狀態，而不是期待 Rime 已經解決全域同步

## 狀態可見性工具

[ShowyEdge](https://github.com/pqrs-org/ShowyEdge/) 的定位很清楚：它是 macOS 的「current input source 可視化指示器」(visualization indicator)。

這類工具的價值在於：

- 讓你一眼看出現在是 ABC、注音、拼音或其他輸入來源
- 降低 app / 視窗切換之後的狀態不確定感

但它不是 Rime / Squirrel / librime 的全域狀態修復器。比較準確的期待應該是：

- 它能改善觀測 (observation)
- 不能保證改善切換行為本身

## 備份策略

這一輪的預設策略是：只備份「手寫設定」與「手動維護內容」，不把所有執行時產物 (runtime artifacts) 都當成 source of truth。

### Rime：建議備份

優先備份：

- `~/Library/Rime/*.custom.yaml`
- 目前最重要的是 `~/Library/Rime/squirrel.custom.yaml`

如果之後開始客製 schema，也一併把這些視為手寫設定：

- `~/Library/Rime/default.custom.yaml`
- `~/Library/Rime/bopomofo.custom.yaml`
- 其他 `<schema>.custom.yaml`

### Rime：先不要直接納入 chezmoi 的內容

以下檔案不建議直接當成 repo 內主要真相來源：

- `~/Library/Rime/build/`
- `~/Library/Rime/installation.yaml`
- `~/Library/Rime/user.yaml`
- `~/Library/Rime/*.userdb/`

原因：

- `build/` 是重新佈署後的編譯產物
- `installation.yaml` 偏向機器與安裝資訊
- `user.yaml` 偏向執行狀態與最近使用的方案
- `*.userdb/` 是 live user dictionary / frequency data，變動頻繁，直接納管很吵

### Rime：`sync/` 的定位

`~/Library/Rime/sync/<installation_id>/` 應該視為同步或匯出產物，不是主要 source of truth。

它有兩個用途：

- 跨機同步時，可作為 Rime 自己輸出的可攜資料 (portable data)
- 在需要救援或搬機時，可作為 userdb 快照與 custom 檔副本

但 repo 策略上，仍建議以手寫的 `*.custom.yaml` 當主要真相來源，而不是以 `sync/` 內容反推設定。

### McBopomofo：建議備份

McBopomofo 官方手冊明確提到：

- 使用者詞彙分頁管理的是純文字檔
- 這些文字檔位置可以自行決定
- 甚至可以放到 Google Drive / OneDrive / iCloud Drive 方便備份

以本機目前狀態，建議優先備份：

- `~/Library/Application Support/McBopomofo/data.txt`
- `~/Library/Application Support/McBopomofo/data-plain-bpmf.txt`
- `~/Library/Application Support/McBopomofo/exclude-phrases.txt`
- `~/Library/Application Support/McBopomofo/exclude-phrases-plain-bpmf.txt`
- `~/Library/Application Support/McBopomofo/phrases-replacement.txt`

### McBopomofo：可選備份

可選：

- `~/Library/Preferences/org.openvanilla.inputmethod.McBopomofo.plist`

理由：

- 這裡主要是偏好設定與行為選項
- 對於詞庫與自訂詞本身不是唯一來源
- 如果目標是低噪音、可審查、適合版本控制 (version control)，文字詞庫的優先級更高

## 之後若要正式納入 chezmoi

這一輪先不把輸入法資料正式納管進 repo，但如果下一輪要做，建議優先順序如下：

1. `squirrel.custom.yaml`
2. 其他手寫的 Rime `*.custom.yaml`
3. McBopomofo 的 `*.txt` 詞庫檔
4. 最後才考慮是否要納入 McBopomofo 的 plist

不建議一開始就把整個 `~/Library/Rime/` 或 `~/Library/Application Support/McBopomofo/` 直接整包納入，因為會混入大量執行時資料。

## Linux Appendix

這裡只補最小必要資訊，不展開 Linux 端排障。

### ibus-rime 設定目錄

根據 Rime wiki，IBus 的使用者資料夾通常是：

- `~/.config/ibus/rime/`

舊版本可能還會看到：

- `~/.ibus/rime/`

### ibus-rime 重新部署

根據 Rime wiki 的 `CustomizationGuide`，如果找不到狀態欄上的 deploy 按鈕，可在終端觸發：

\```bash
touch ~/.config/ibus/rime/
ibus restart
\```

如果未來這個 repo 要把 Linux 端 Rime 設定一起納管，建議也同樣只從 `*.custom.yaml` 開始，而不是直接處理整個資料夾。
