```text
1	# aicapture — AI review of past shell commands
2	
3	Capture a past shell command's block from tmux scrollback, pipe it to a coding-agent CLI (Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex / Cursor Agent) in non-interactive mode, get back a fix or explanation. Advisory by default: agent prints suggestions, doesn't touch files.
4	
5	Built on [OSC 133 semantic prompts](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/Per_Bothner/specifications/blob/master/proposals/semantic-prompts.md) — the shell emits `A`/`C`/`D` line-attribute markers, tmux stores them, our helpers navigate by them. For background on how this compares to `thefuck`, Warp, `wut`, `tmuxai`, `atuin`, etc., see [instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md](../this_repo/instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md).
6	
7	## Quick start
8	
9	```sh
10	# Any command that produced useful output or an error…
11	cargo build --release
12	
13	# …is one keystroke away from a diagnose + fix:
14	aifix
15	```
16	
17	Output in your terminal:
18	
19	```
20	aifix ← block -1
21	⠋ claude haiku (json)…                                  # spinner while agent thinks
22	claude (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) | in=12 out=87 cache=(r:24402,w:12487) | cost=$0.0008 3812ms
23	
24	## Fix for `cargo build` error
25	
26	Your `Cargo.toml` is missing the `serde` dependency. Add:
27	
28	    [dependencies]
29	    serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
30	
31	Then re-run `cargo build --release`.
32	```
33	
34	Reply is rendered as Markdown via `glow` (auto-falls back to `bat --language=md`, then raw text if neither is installed).
35	
36	## Commands
37	
38	### Capture (no AI call)
39	
40	Each prints captured text to stdout (pipe-friendly) **and** copies it to the system clipboard via tmux's OSC 52 bridge (works over SSH). Defaults to N=1 (most recent); pass a positive integer for N-back lookback.
41	
42	| Command | Scope |
43	|---|---|
44	| `cpcmd [N]` | Nth-latest command's **input line** (from zsh history — works outside tmux too) |
45	| `cpout [N]` | Nth-latest command's **output** only (via tmux + OSC 133) |
46	| `cpblock [N]` | Nth-latest command's **full block**: prompt + input + output (Warp-style) |
47	
48	```sh
49	cpblock                          # last block → clipboard + stdout
50	cpblock 3                        # 3rd-latest
51	cpout 2 | tee /tmp/snapshot.log  # pipe output to file while also copying
52	cpcmd                            # just the command string (no output)
53	```
54	
55	### AI review
56	
57	Same positional `[N]` as the capture helpers, plus flags:
58	
59	| Command | Default prompt |
60	|---|---|
61	| `aifix [N]` | *"Diagnose any errors and suggest a concrete fix. Be brief and specific."* |
62	| `aiexplain [N]` | *"Explain what happened in plain language. Be concise."* |
63	
64	Both accept:
65	
66	- `-a AGENT` — `claude` / `opencode` / `codex` / `cursor-agent`. Default: auto-detect (first one found on `$PATH`).
67	- `-p PROMPT` — override the default prompt.
68	- `--raw` — skip glow/bat prettify; print the agent's raw Markdown text.
69	- `--no-meta` — suppress the stderr metadata line (model / tokens / cost / duration).
70	- `-h` / `--help` — print the full signature and current env-var values.
71	
72	```sh
73	aifix                               # last block, default fix prompt
74	aifix 3 -a opencode                 # 3rd-latest, force OpenCode
75	aifix -p "is this safe on prod?"    # custom prompt
76	aiexplain 2 --raw                   # no prettify
77	aifix --no-meta | tee /tmp/ans.md   # pipe-friendly
78	```
79	
80	### Interactive TUI
81	
82	```sh
83	aiblock
84	```
85	
86	Launches a [questionary](https://github.com/tmbo/questionary) + [rich](https://github.com/Textualize/rich) TUI ([`scripts/aiblock.py`](../../scripts/aiblock.py)) that walks through:
87	
88	1. **Checkbox picker** over the last 20 commands. Space toggles, Enter confirms. Picking none defaults to "last block".
89	2. **Preview** — each selected block shown in its own rich panel (multi-select concatenates in chronological order with `--- Block -N ---` separators so the agent can tell the turns apart).
90	3. **Prompt edit** — default is the `aifix` fix-prompt; edit inline.
91	4. **Action** — one of:
92	   - *Print reply here* — rendered as Markdown in a rich panel with the metadata as subtitle.
93	   - *Copy reply to clipboard* — via tmux OSC 52 / pbcopy / xclip / xsel / wl-copy.
94	   - *Spawn new tmux window running `<agent>`* — opens a fresh interactive agent session with your selected blocks pre-loaded into tmux's `aiblock` paste-buffer. Pull via `prefix + =`.
95	
96	The TUI depends on `uv` (PEP 723 inline deps) — no separate install step required; first run populates the uv cache.
97	
98	## Non-tmux alternatives
99	
100	When you're not in tmux (VSCode integrated terminal, bare Ghostty without tmux, quick SSH session), `cpblock` / `aifix` / `aiexplain` / `aiblock` can't see scrollback — they depend on tmux's OSC 133 line attributes. Three Tier 1 wrappers cover the common cases without magic (no shell hooks, no PTY proxy, no `script(1)` wrapping — see [`backlog/ai-capture-non-tmux-output.md`](../../backlog/ai-capture-non-tmux-output.md) for why we reject those paths):
101	
102	| Command | Source of context | Typical use |
103	|---|---|---|
104	| `aifix-stdin` | whatever you pipe in | `tail -100 build.log \| aifix-stdin` |
105	| `aifix-run -- CMD [ARG...]` | runs `CMD`, tees stdout+stderr to a log, reviews | `aifix-run -- cargo build --release` |
106	| `aifix-rerun` | re-executes the previous shell command (confirm prompt) | `aifix-rerun` after a transient error |
107	
108	All three accept the same flags as `aifix` (`-a AGENT` / `-p PROMPT` / `--raw` / `--no-meta`). `aifix-rerun` adds `-y` to skip the "⚠ side effects" confirmation. Default prompt for each is the `aifix` "diagnose + fix"; use `-p "explain what happened"` if you want the explain behaviour.
109	
110	```sh
111	# stdin — compose with any producer
112	tail -200 /var/log/nginx/error.log | aifix-stdin
113	curl -sS https://weird.api/thing | aifix-stdin -p "what is this JSON telling me?"
114	aifix-stdin < /tmp/build-fail.log
115	
116	# run — capture a fresh invocation (double-run safe, no prior history needed)
117	aifix-run -- ls /missing
118	aifix-run -p "is this safe on prod?" -- ansible-playbook deploy.yml
119	
120	# rerun — thefuck-style, re-execute last cmd. Confirms by default.
121	mvn compile      # fails
122	aifix-rerun      # "⚠ side effects…  Proceed? [y/N]"
123	aifix-rerun -y   # skip confirm
124	```
125	
126	**isatty caveat** for `aifix-run`: teeing makes CMD's stdout a pipe, so TUI apps (vim, less, htop) render in degraded mode. Don't `aifix-run` an interactive tool — pipe its log file via `aifix-stdin` after the fact instead.
127	
128	**Side-effect warning** for `aifix-rerun`: re-running `rm`, `curl -X POST`, `git push`, migrations, etc. is dangerous. The confirmation prompt is there for a reason; don't `-y` without reading what will be re-executed.
129	
130	## Configuration
131	
132	Put any of these in `~/.zshrc`, a `99_local_*.zsh` override, or export them per-session:
133	
134	```sh
135	# Model per agent (auto-detected order: claude → opencode → codex → cursor-agent)
136	export AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL=haiku                              # alias or full name (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6)
137	export AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL=github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5  # provider/model format
138	export AICAP_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-5-mini
139	export AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL=                                    # empty = cursor-agent picks
140	
141	# Output behaviour
142	export AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=1   # 0 to mute the stderr "claude (...) | in=... cost=..." line
143	export AICAP_PRETTIFY=1        # 0 to always print raw Markdown (skip glow/bat)
144	export AICAP_SPINNER=1         # 0 to disable the stderr spinner animation
145	```
146	
147	Check current settings any time with `aifix --help`.
148	
149	Defaults are tuned for Haiku-class models — fast (~5s round-trip) and cheap (~$0.001/call with cache hits). If you want Opus/Sonnet for harder diagnoses, set `AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL=sonnet` either globally or per-invocation:
150	
151	```sh
152	AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL=sonnet aifix 3
153	```
154	
155	## Requirements
156	
157	| What | For |
158	|---|---|
159	| `zsh` | All commands (cpcmd, aifix, etc. are zsh functions) |
160	| `tmux 3.3+` | `cpout` / `cpblock` / `aifix` / `aiexplain` / `aiblock` (scrollback navigation) |
161	| OSC 133 shell integration | The hook in `dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh` emits the A/C/D markers tmux needs. Run `exec zsh` after install so the hook fires in your current shell. |
162	| At least one coding-agent CLI | `claude` (recommended), `opencode`, `codex`, or `cursor-agent` — install via your usual channel |
163	| `glow` (optional) | Markdown prettify on agent replies |
164	| `bat` (optional) | Prettify fallback when `glow` isn't present |
165	| `jq` (optional) | Parses Claude's `--output-format json` for the metadata line (tokens / cost) |
166	| `uv` (optional) | Needed only for the `aiblock` TUI — installs its Python deps lazily |
167	
168	## Standalone setup (no chezmoi)
169	
170	If you don't want to adopt the whole dotfiles repo, grab these four files and source them from your `~/.zshrc`. They're self-contained apart from the listed optional tools above.
171	
172	```sh
173	REPO=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main
174	mkdir -p ~/.config/zsh/tools
175	
176	# Shell side: OSC 133 hook + cpblock family + aifix family
177	for f in 02_shell_integration.zsh 03_tmux_capture.zsh 04_ai_capture.zsh; do
178	  curl -fsSL "$REPO/dot_config/zsh/tools/$f" -o "$HOME/.config/zsh/tools/$f"
179	done
180	
181	# Optional TUI (needs uv)
182	mkdir -p ~/.local/share/aicapture
183	curl -fsSL "$REPO/scripts/aiblock.py" -o ~/.local/share/aicapture/aiblock.py
184	chmod +x ~/.local/share/aicapture/aiblock.py
185	
186	# Append to ~/.zshrc (or equivalent)
187	cat >> ~/.zshrc <<'EOF'
188	for f in ~/.config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh \
189	         ~/.config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh \
190	         ~/.config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh; do
191	  [[ -r "$f" ]] && source "$f"
192	done
193	EOF
194	
195	# Reload
196	exec zsh
197	```

199	The `aiblock` shell function resolves the TUI path via `chezmoi source-path`; if you're not on chezmoi, edit the `aiblock()` function in `04_ai_capture.zsh` to point at `~/.local/share/aicapture/aiblock.py` instead:
200	
201	```zsh
202	# replace the chezmoi source-path block with:
203	_AIBLOCK_SCRIPT="$HOME/.local/share/aicapture/aiblock.py"
204	```

206	### Read source on GitHub

208	- [`dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh) — OSC 133 precmd/preexec hooks (A marker embedded in `$PROMPT` via `%{...%}` — see [`pitfalls/zsh-osc133-precmd-printf-a-not-stored.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/zsh-osc133-precmd-printf-a-not-stored.md) for why)

211	- [`scripts/aiblock.py`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/scripts/aiblock.py) — Python TUI (PEP 723 inline deps)
212	
213	## Troubleshooting
214	
215	### `cpblock returned empty` / `aifix ← block -1` then nothing
216	
217	Your current shell was started before the hook was installed. The precmd/preexec hooks that emit OSC 133 markers need to be registered via `add-zsh-hook`, which only happens when `02_shell_integration.zsh` is sourced. Fix:
218	
219	```sh
220	exec zsh                                             # reload shell in place
221	echo $precmd_functions | tr ' ' '\n' | grep osc133   # verify
222	# expected: _osc133_precmd
223	```
224	
225	If `exec zsh` doesn't help, open a fresh tmux window — some terminal states don't propagate cleanly through `exec`.
226	
227	### `aiblock`: "Shell history is empty — no commands to pick from"
228	
229	Should no longer happen after commit `3993b7b`. If it does, the zsh wrapper that dumps history via `fc -ln -30` isn't running. Verify:
230	
231	```sh
232	which aiblock     # should show the function from 04_ai_capture.zsh
233	type aiblock      # should show the fc-dump logic
234	```
235	
236	Workaround: the TUI also falls back to parsing `$HISTFILE` directly, so `HISTFILE=~/.zsh_history aiblock` works even if the wrapper is broken.
237	
238	### Metadata line shows `claude (?)` instead of the model
239	
240	`jq` failed to find `.modelUsage | keys | first` in Claude's JSON output. Either `jq` is out of date (install latest) or Claude CLI changed its JSON shape. Set `AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=0` to bypass until fixed.
241	
242	### Spinner doesn't appear / doesn't disappear
243	
244	Spinner auto-skips when stderr isn't a tty. If you're redirecting with `2>/tmp/err` or piping through `tee` you won't see it — by design.
245	
246	If the spinner leaves a stale `⠋ ...` line after the agent returns, the `kill $_AICAP_SPIN_PID` + `\r\e[K` cleanup didn't run (usually because of a signal during a subshell). Press `Ctrl+L` to redraw, then report it.
247	
248	### tmux scrollback looks "broken" / ghost frames
249	
250	Not directly an aicapture issue but adjacent — see [`pitfalls/tmux-scrollback-tui-repaint-ghosting.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/tmux-scrollback-tui-repaint-ghosting.md) and the `scroll-on-clear off` + `prefix + [` workflow.
251

1	# Coding-agent CLI overlays (Cursor / OpenCode / Codex)
2	
3	This repo manages the *global* config files of three coding-agent CLIs via chezmoi `modify_` overlays:
4	
5	| CLI | Live file | Source script | Merge engine |
6	|---|---|---|---|
7	| Cursor | `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` | [`dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl`](../../dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
8	| OpenCode (server/runtime) | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | [`dot_config/opencode/modify_opencode.json.tmpl`](../../dot_config/opencode/modify_opencode.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
9	| OpenCode (TUI) | `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` | [`dot_config/opencode/modify_tui.json.tmpl`](../../dot_config/opencode/modify_tui.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
10	| Codex | `~/.codex/config.toml` | [`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl) | Python `tomllib` + inline emitter |
11	
12	Overlay payloads live under [`.chezmoitemplates/agents/`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/) and are sourced via `{{ template ... }}` includes so the merge logic can be tested independently of overlay contents.
13	
14	## Why `modify_` and not full file management
15	
16	All three CLIs **rewrite their config file at runtime** to record machine-local state: auth tokens, telemetry IDs, per-project trust grants, marketplace registrations with absolute paths, plugin-cache hashes, last-used provider hints, etc. Tracking the whole file as managed content would:
17	
18	1. Leak secrets (`authInfo`, `auth.json` content) into the dotfiles repo.
19	2. Bake one machine's absolute paths (`/Users/me/.codex/.tmp/...`) into another machine's apply.
20	3. Produce constant `chezmoi diff` noise as the CLI churns the file.
21	
22	The `modify_` overlay model deep-merges only the keys we explicitly enforce; everything else passes through verbatim.
23	
24	## What each overlay enforces
25	
26	### Cursor — [`agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json)
27	
28	```json
29	{
30	  "editor": { "vimMode": true }
31	}
32	```
33	
34	- `editor.vimMode = true` — universal preference; sibling `editor.fontSize` etc. survive the deep merge.
35	- **`permissions.allow` / `permissions.deny` arrays are intentionally NOT in the overlay.** `jq '. * $overlay'` replaces arrays wholesale at the same key path, so listing any entries here would clobber the user's live machine-specific allow-list on every `chezmoi apply`. Manage those per machine via the live file directly, or move to a `--argjson allow $merged` array-union approach if you ever need a shared baseline.
36	
37	### OpenCode — [`agents/opencode.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/opencode.overlay.json)
38	
39	```json
40	{
41	  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
42	  "autoupdate": true,
43	  "default_agent": "build",
44	  "small_model": "github-copilot/gpt-5-mini",
45	  "agent": { "title": { "reasoningEffort": "low" } },
46	  "provider": {
47	    "github-copilot": {
48	      "options": { "timeout": 600000 }
49	    }
50	  }
51	}
52	```
53	
54	- `$schema` — keeps editors aware of the schema for autocomplete.
55	- `autoupdate = true` — let the CLI self-update.
56	- `default_agent = "build"` — primary agent on TUI/CLI startup. Override per-session via `--agent` or the picker.
57	- `small_model = "github-copilot/gpt-5-mini"` — cheap model for title generation, summarisation, and other lightweight calls. Avoids billing Claude Opus quota for trivial tasks. Pairs with `agent.title.reasoningEffort = "low"`.
58	- `agent.title.reasoningEffort = "low"` — cheap completions for short title generation; sibling `agent.*` entries (per-agent provider, model overrides) survive.
59	- `provider.github-copilot.options.timeout = 600000` (10 min) — request-level timeout. Default is 5 min; bumped to give long Claude Opus generations more room before the SDK aborts the whole call. **Note**: `chunkTimeout` is intentionally NOT set here, see [docs/tools/opencode.md → Claude Opus stream stall](opencode.md#claude-opus-stream-stall-on-github-copilot) for the rationale (upstream bug [anomalyco/opencode#20466](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/20466) — SSE-chunk-timeout errors aren't retried, so setting `chunkTimeout` would convert silent hangs into hard failures with no recovery).
60	
61	### OpenCode TUI — [`agents/opencode.tui.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/opencode.tui.overlay.json)
62	
63	```json
64	{
65	  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/tui.json",
66	  "keybinds": { "leader": "ctrl+x" },
67	  "mouse": true,
68	  "diff_style": "auto",
69	  "scroll_acceleration": { "enabled": true }
70	}
71	```
72	
73	The TUI lives in a **separate file** from server/runtime config: `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` with its own schema `https://opencode.ai/tui.json`. See upstream docs:
74	
75	- [Config → TUI](https://opencode.ai/docs/config/#tui) — file location, schema URL, precedence
76	- [TUI → Configure → Options](https://opencode.ai/docs/tui/#options) — per-key semantics
77	
78	Key-by-key rationale:
79	
80	- `$schema = "https://opencode.ai/tui.json"` — TUI schema (different from `opencode.json`'s `config.json` schema). Lets editors validate + autocomplete.
81	- `keybinds.leader = "ctrl+x"` — explicit pin of the upstream default. Declaring it ensures muscle memory + the `<leader>` references in [docs/keybinds](https://opencode.ai/docs/keybinds/) survive any future upstream default change. The other ~80 keybind defaults are intentionally NOT pinned here — they stay tracking upstream so new actions added by OpenCode become available without overlay churn.
82	- `mouse = true` — explicit pin of the upstream default. Trades terminal-native select-to-copy for OpenCode's in-TUI mouse support (scroll, click).
83	- `diff_style = "auto"` — adapts diff layout to terminal width (vs `"stacked"` which forces single-column). Pinning the upstream default makes intent explicit.
84	- `scroll_acceleration.enabled = true` — macOS-style smooth/accelerated scrolling. Per upstream docs this **takes precedence over and overrides** `scroll_speed`, so we deliberately omit `scroll_speed` from the overlay (setting both would mislead — the latter would be silently ignored).
85	
86	What's intentionally NOT in the TUI overlay:
87	
88	- `theme` — left unset so OpenCode's auto light/dark detection stays in effect (matches the system theme just like `ghostty` and the `tmux` theme switcher in this repo).
89	- Individual `keybinds.*` entries beyond `leader` — see above. fzf's shell-level `Ctrl+T` and OpenCode's `variant_cycle = ctrl+t` do not collide because they live in disjoint namespaces (shell prompt vs OpenCode TUI).
90	- `username_toggle` / `tips_toggle` / `display_thinking` — these are persisted by the TUI's `/help` customisation panel at runtime. Pinning them in the overlay would clobber the user's last in-app choice on every `chezmoi apply`, same anti-pattern as managing `plugin` paths or auth tokens.
91	- `scroll_speed` — see `scroll_acceleration.enabled` above; OpenCode ignores `scroll_speed` whenever acceleration is enabled.
92	
93	### Codex — [`agents/codex.config.overlay.toml`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/codex.config.overlay.toml)
94	
95	```toml
96	personality = "pragmatic"
97	model = "gpt-5.4"
98	model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"
99	
100	[features]
101	codex_hooks = true
102	unified_exec = true
103	shell_snapshot = true
104	steer = true
105	multi_agent = true
106	
107	[plugins."github@openai-curated"]
108	enabled = true
109	
110	[plugins."google-drive@openai-curated"]
111	enabled = true
112	
113	[plugins."computer-use@openai-bundled"]
114	enabled = true
115	```
116	
117	- Top-level model + reasoning preferences.
118	- `[features]` — opt into the experimental flags this user always wants on.
119	- `[plugins."<id>".enabled]` — curated plugin set; user-installed plugins appear under their own `[plugins."..."]` blocks and are preserved by the deep merge.
120	
121	## What is intentionally NOT managed
122	
123	| File / subtree | CLI | Why |
124	|---|---|---|
125	| `~/.cursor/{authInfo,auth*,privacyCache,statsigBootstrap,version,hasChangedDefaultModel,...}` | Cursor | Auth + telemetry; runtime-only. |
126	| `~/.cursor/{extensions,plugins,projects,worktrees,workers,browser-logs,chats,plans,prompt_history.json,argv.json,ide_state.json,agent-cli-state.json,ai-tracking,mcp.json,skills-cursor}` | Cursor | CLI-managed state, per-project, machine-local. |
127	| `~/.config/opencode/{node_modules,package.json,bun.lock,package-lock.json,plugins/}` | OpenCode | Node runtime + locally-installed plugin source trees. |
128	| `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` keys outside the TUI overlay (`theme`, `keybinds.*` other than `leader`, `username_toggle`, `tips_toggle`, `display_thinking`, `scroll_speed`) | OpenCode | TUI runtime customisation panel persists user choices here; overlay only pins stable preferences. |
129	| `~/.codex/auth.json` | Codex | OpenAI auth token. **Never** check in. |
130	| `~/.codex/[projects."<absolute-path>"]` | Codex | Per-project trust grants — absolute paths are machine-specific. **Round-tripped** by the modify_ script (see below). |
131	| `~/.codex/[marketplaces.<id>]` | Codex | Marketplace registrations with absolute `source = "/Users/.../.codex/.tmp/..."` paths. **Round-tripped**. |
132	| `~/.codex/{installation_id,history.jsonl,session_index.jsonl,sessions/,logs_*.sqlite*,state_*.sqlite,cache/,tmp/,log/,sqlite/,memories/,vendor_imports/,shell_snapshots/,models_cache.json,plugins/,skills/,rules/,ambient-suggestions/,version.json,AGENTS.md,.tmp/}` | Codex | Sessions, logs, sqlite, plugin/skills directories, machine-local notes. |
133	
134	The `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` presence-gates the entire `~/.cursor/`, `~/.codex/`, and `~/.config/opencode/` trees with a `stat` check so uninstalled CLIs never produce phantom directories.
135	
136	## How the Codex TOML merge works
137	
138	`jq` doesn't speak TOML and `mikefarah/yq`'s TOML emitter produces invalid output for keys with special characters (e.g. `github@openai-curated`). The Codex `modify_` script uses Python instead:
139	
140	1. Read live file into a `dict` via `tomllib` (Python 3.11+ built-in; `tomli` fallback for 3.10).
141	2. Pop `[projects]` and `[marketplaces]` subtrees into `state`.
142	3. Read overlay TOML into a `dict`.
143	4. Deep-merge: `live_minus_state <- overlay <- state`. Argument order is merge precedence (later wins). State wins last so per-project trust never gets clobbered by an overlay churn.
144	5. Emit TOML via a 30-line writer that quotes all non-bareword keys (handles `github@openai-curated` and `/Users/me/foo`-style project keys).
145	
146	The script falls through to passing the live file untouched if `python3` or `tomllib`/`tomli` are missing; chezmoi will skip the file for that apply.
147	
148	## OpenCode legacy `config.json` migration
149	
150	OpenCode docs now recommend `opencode.json` as the canonical filename, but installations from before that change use `config.json`. The repo manages only the modern filename; a one-shot script handles the migration:
151	
152	- [`run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`](../../run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl) runs once per source-state hash, before chezmoi deploys files. It:
153	  1. No-ops if `~/.config/opencode/config.json` is absent.
154	  2. If only the legacy file exists: rename it to `opencode.json`.
155	  3. If both exist: deep-merge legacy into modern (modern wins on conflict, since it's presumed newer), then delete legacy.
156	
157	After this script runs, the `modify_opencode.json` overlay enforces the managed keys on the unified file. The legacy filename never reappears because OpenCode itself only writes `opencode.json` going forward.
158	
159	The migration script can be removed from the repo a few months after rollout (once all machines have run `chezmoi apply` at least once); it is idempotent and a no-op on fresh machines, so it's safe to leave indefinitely.
160	
161	## Refresh recipe
162	
163	To change what an overlay enforces, edit the corresponding `.chezmoitemplates/agents/<cli>.overlay.{json,toml}` file. Do **not** `chezmoi add` the live config — that would strip the `modify_` prefix and overwrite the script with the runtime file (which contains your secrets).
164	
165	To pull a new key from the live file into the overlay (e.g. you changed a Cursor permission you want shared):
166	
167	```bash
168	# 1. Inspect the live file
169	jq . ~/.cursor/cli-config.json
170	
171	# 2. Edit the overlay JSON / TOML and add the key
172	$EDITOR .chezmoitemplates/agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json
173	
174	# 3. Verify the rendered modify_ script outputs what you expect
175	chezmoi execute-template < dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl > /tmp/m.sh
176	chmod +x /tmp/m.sh
177	cat ~/.cursor/cli-config.json | /tmp/m.sh
178	
179	# 4. Apply
180	chezmoi apply
181	```
182	
183	## Tests
184	
185	[`tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats`](../../tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats) covers:
186	
187	- Each overlay enforces its declared keys.
188	- Live runtime keys outside the overlay are preserved verbatim.
189	- Codex `[projects.*]` and `[marketplaces.*]` round-trip unchanged (the round-trip property is the load-bearing invariant — break it and machines start clobbering each other's per-project trust).
190	- The modify_ scripts are idempotent (running output through the script again produces the same output).
191	- The OpenCode migration handles all three input states: legacy-only, both-present, neither-present.
192	- The Claude hook-aware merger (see next section): notify.sh added when missing; CodeIsland entries preserved; idempotency on re-apply; non-hook deep-merge preserves user siblings.
193	
194	Run with `just bats` (or directly: `bats tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats`).
195	
196	## CodeIsland integration (macOS-only)
197	
198	[CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland) is a macOS notch-area HUD (positioning analogous to [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar)) that surfaces real-time activity from 11+ coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode, AntiGravity, Trae, Qoder, Factory, CodeBuddy, Kimi). It works by injecting per-CLI hook entries that fire `~/.codeisland/codeisland-bridge` (or `codeisland-hook.sh`), which streams events over a Unix socket at `/tmp/codeisland-<uid>.sock` to the SwiftUI app.
199	
200	### Why macOS-only
201	
202	- Swift app, requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later.
203	- The notch UI assumes a MacBook display geometry.
204	- Distribution is via brew cask (`wxtsky/tap`) or `.dmg`.
205	
206	There is no Linux fallback — the wire format depends on the macOS-specific bridge binary and socket path. We deliberately install nothing for CodeIsland on Linux and skip all related concerns there.
207	
208	### Install
209	
210	The `codeisland` cask is added in [`dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`](../../dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl) inside the `{{ if .installAiDesktopApps }}` block alongside the other agent desktop apps:
211	
212	```ruby
213	tap "wxtsky/tap"
214	cask "codeisland"
215	```
216	
217	### How we coexist with the app
218	
219	CodeIsland's settings panel calls itself "Auto hook install" with "auto-repair and version tracking" — meaning the **app actively writes and re-writes** hook entries into each detected CLI's config on every launch. Two coexistence patterns:
220	
221	> **Note (2026-04-25)**: CodeIsland v1.0.23 dropped `ExitPlanMode` from the default `HookServer.autoApproveTools` whitelist — plan-mode exit now prompts a real confirm dialog, and Settings → Behavior → "Auto-approve Tools" lets users toggle individual tools. See [`pitfalls/codeisland-auto-approves-permissionrequest.md`](../../pitfalls/codeisland-auto-approves-permissionrequest.md). Our merger continues to *additively* preserve every CodeIsland hook entry — no subtractive logic was added, because the upstream fix is the right path and the `PermissionRequest` hook is now a legitimate input source for the notch popup, not a bypass mechanism.
222	
223	#### Pattern A — Sidecar files (always-ignored)
224	
225	CLIs whose hooks live in a dedicated sidecar (containing nothing but CodeIsland hooks) are simply unmanaged by chezmoi. Concretely:
226	
227	| File | CLI | Why unmanaged |
228	|------|-----|---------------|
229	| `~/.codex/hooks.json` | Codex | Pure CodeIsland sidecar (also extended by Superset's notify.sh in some setups, but that's installed by Superset, not us) |
230	| `~/.cursor/hooks.json` | Cursor | Same |
231	| `~/.copilot/hooks/codeisland.json` | GitHub Copilot CLI | Pure CodeIsland sidecar |
232	| `~/.gemini/settings.json` | Gemini CLI | Currently nothing else to enforce there |
233	| `~/.antigravity/settings.json` | AntiGravity (CLI, not the editor) | Currently nothing else to enforce there |
234	
235	These paths are added to [`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiignore.tmpl) as **always-ignore** so accidentally running `chezmoi add ~/.codex/hooks.json` won't pull a CodeIsland-owned file into the source tree (which would clobber the app's runtime updates and create a ping-pong with its auto-installer).
236	
237	If you later want to manage non-hook prefs in `~/.gemini/settings.json` or `~/.antigravity/settings.json`, write a `modify_` overlay that follows the hook-aware pattern below — and remove the corresponding ignore line.
238	
239	#### Pattern B — Mixed files (hook-aware merger)
240	
241	Files where stable user prefs and CodeIsland hooks coexist need a smarter overlay. Currently the only such file is **`~/.claude/settings.json`** — Claude Code stores model selection, plugins, statusLine, and `permissions.defaultMode` in the same file as `hooks.<event>` arrays. A naive `jq '. * $overlay'` deep-merge replaces arrays wholesale: declaring a `hooks.Notification` entry in our overlay would silently delete every CodeIsland entry on each `chezmoi apply`, then CodeIsland would re-install on next launch — endless ping-pong producing diff noise and broken integrations.
242	
243	[`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_settings.json) solves this with a hook-aware merger:
244	
245	1. **Non-hook keys** (`enabledPlugins`, `extraKnownMarketplaces`, `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`, `permissions.defaultMode`, `statusLine`, …) deep-merge normally via `base * overlay_no_hooks`. Note: `permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"` is set deliberately to work around Claude Code resetting the active permission mode after every interactive prompt (`AskUserQuestion`, CodeIsland popup, remote-control inject); see [`pitfalls/claude-code-permission-mode-resets-after-interactive-prompt.md`](../../pitfalls/claude-code-permission-mode-resets-after-interactive-prompt.md). The deep-merge writes the `defaultMode` scalar without touching sibling `permissions.allow` / `permissions.deny` arrays — those remain machine-local.
246	2. **`hooks.<event>` arrays** are merged additively: for each event the overlay declares, append entries whose `.hooks[0].command` isn't already represented in the live array (string-equality match). Live entries are preserved verbatim, no entry is ever removed.
247	
248	The full filter (jq):
249	
250	```jq
251	. as $base
252	| ($overlay | del(.hooks)) as $non_hook_overlay
253	| ($overlay.hooks // {}) as $overlay_hooks
254	| ($base * $non_hook_overlay) as $merged
255	| $merged
256	| .hooks = (
257	    ($merged.hooks // {}) as $live_hooks
258	    | reduce ($overlay_hooks | to_entries[]) as $ev (
259	        $live_hooks;
260	        .[$ev.key] = (
261	          (.[$ev.key] // []) as $live_arr
262	          | ($live_arr | map(.hooks[0].command? // "")) as $live_cmds
263	          | $live_arr + (
264	              $ev.value
265	              | map(select(
266	                  (.hooks[0].command? // "") as $cmd
267	                  | ($cmd == "") or (($live_cmds | index($cmd)) == null)
268	                ))
269	            )
270	        )
271	      )
272	  )
273	```
274	
275	Test coverage in `tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats`:
276	
277	- `claude modify_settings: notify.sh added to empty hooks, codeisland entries preserved` — proves the additive append works without removing CodeIsland entries.
278	- `claude modify_settings: idempotent when notify.sh already present` — proves no duplicate appears on re-apply.
279	- `claude modify_settings: empty live file produces overlay-only output` — bootstrap on a fresh machine.
280	- `claude modify_settings: non-hook deep-merge preserves siblings` — proves user-added plugins/marketplaces survive.
281	
282	> **Sibling overlay**: `~/.claude/keybindings.json` is managed by a separate, simpler `modify_` script — [`dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json). It is NOT hook-aware (CodeIsland doesn't write to keybindings.json). See [Claude Code keybindings](claude-code-keybindings.md) for its design, the `chat:cycleMode`-only mode-jump limitation, and how to add personal binding overrides.
283	
284	### Future work (deferred)
285	
286	- **Apprise-to-webhook expansion of `~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh`**: the script already calls `apprise --tag desktop` for local OS notifications. Could be extended to also fire `apprise --tag webhook` for remote chat-app delivery (Slack, Discord, Telegram, …) using URLs configured in `~/.config/apprise/apprise.yaml`. Open question: noise filtering — should webhook fire on every `Notification`/`Stop`, or only on permission-request and session-end? Likely needs an env-var gate (`CLAUDE_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK=1`) so each machine opts in. Track in a separate change.
287	- **Managed overlays for `~/.gemini/settings.json` and `~/.antigravity/settings.json`**: defer until concrete prefs need enforcing. When added, follow the hook-aware merger pattern from Claude (each of those files also has CodeIsland-injected `hooks` blocks today).

```

```text
1	# Agent pane discovery
2	
3	Find — and jump to — coding-agent sessions (`claude`, `cursor-agent`, `codex`,
4	`opencode`) that are currently running in *any* tmux pane on this host.
5	
6	The pain this solves: you start `claude` in pane A on session `chezmoi`, hop
7	into pane B in another window for a quick test, drift over to a `vibe/foo`
8	session for a Codex task, and three windows later you can't remember which
9	pane has the agent you wanted to nudge. CodeIsland (macOS) tells you which
10	**terminal app** is running an agent, but not the specific tmux pane —
11	useless once you have more than one agent inside one terminal.
12	
13	Two complementary surfaces ship in this repo, both backed by tmux:
14	
15	| Tool | Scope | Best at |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| `tv agent-panes` | All four agents (Claude / Codex / OpenCode / Cursor) | "Where am I running stuff?" cross-agent overview, jump-to-pane |
18	| `recon` (optional) | Claude-only, with live status (Working / Idle / Waiting) parsed from pane capture | "Which Claude needs my attention?" — recon's live status detection is richer than what we replicate in tv |
19	
20	## `tv agent-panes` (primary)
21	
22	Open the picker with `prefix + a` inside tmux, or via the popup menu
23	(`prefix + Space → → Agents → Live agent panes (tv)`), or from any shell
24	with `tv agent-panes`.
25	
26	Each row is one running agent pane. The status column shows ● (busy) or
27	○ (idle) for Claude (read from `~/.claude/sessions/{pid}.json`); blank for
28	others.
29	
30	```
31	[cc] ● chezmoi:1.1     │  discover-coding-agent-sessions          │  chezmoi
32	[cc] ○ chezmoi:2.1     │  fix-nvm-lazy-loader-permission-request  │  chezmoi
33	[cc] ●  vibe/foo:4.1   │  refactor auth module                    │  foo
34	[oc]   vibe/bar:0.0    │  Generate migration script               │  bar
35	```
36	
37	### Keybindings (in the picker)
38	
39	| Key | Action |
40	|---|---|
41	| `Enter` / `Alt+T` | Switch tmux focus to that session/window/pane |
42	| `Alt+K` | Kill the pane (with `[y/N]` confirm) |
43	| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy the pane target (`session:win.pane`) to clipboard |
44	| `Alt+P` | Copy directory path |
45	| `Alt+R` | Copy session ID |
46	| `Alt+S` | Copy matched `.specstory/history/*.md` path |
47	| `Ctrl+F` | Cycle preview: live `tmux capture-pane` snapshot ↔ stored transcript |
48	| `Esc` | Close the picker |
49	
50	### How resolution works
51	
52	- **Claude** — Claude Code writes a per-process file at
53	  `~/.claude/sessions/{claude_pid}.json` containing `sessionId`, `cwd`,
54	  `status`, and (when set) a friendly `name`. The discovery walker reads
55	  these directly — *zero heuristics* for Claude. It then walks each
56	  `claude_pid`'s parent chain via `ps -o ppid=` until it finds a tmux
57	  `pane_pid`, which gives the pane target.
58	- **Codex / OpenCode / Cursor** — `pgrep -x <bin>` finds running agent
59	  PIDs, parent-chain walked the same way. Session ID is best-effort: the
60	  walker queries each agent's storage (`opencode.db`, `~/.codex/sessions`,
61	  `~/.cursor/chats`) for the most-recent matching session whose `cwd`
62	  equals the pane's `pane_current_path`. If multiple sessions share a
63	  cwd, the most recently updated wins. The pane is still listed even if
64	  no session ID matches — the row is useful for jump-to-pane regardless.
65	
66	## `recon` (Claude-only fast popup, optional)
67	
68	[`gavraz/recon`](https://github.com/gavraz/recon) is a Rust TUI dashboard
69	that focuses on Claude Code only but pays attention to live agent status by
70	parsing the Claude TUI status bar via `tmux capture-pane`. Worth keeping
71	around when you're juggling several Claude sessions and want
72	"who's blocked on me?" at a glance.
73	
74	### Install
75	
76	Installed automatically via the `rust_cargo_tools` ansible role on
77	`chezmoi apply`:
78	
79	```bash
80	cargo install --git https://github.com/gavraz/recon --locked
81	```
82	
83	Upgrades flow through the standard cargo path:
84	
85	```bash
86	just upgrade-cargo   # or scripts/upgrade_tools.sh cargo
87	```
88	
89	### Use
90	
91	Open it from the popup menu: `prefix + Space → → Agents → Claude
92	dashboard (recon)`. There's no top-level keybind by default — `prefix + g`
93	(recon's upstream default) is taken by the sesh picker on this repo.
94	Promote it to a top-level binding in `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` if
95	you find yourself reaching for it often.
96	
97	The `→ Agents` submenu only shows the recon row when `recon` is on `PATH`,
98	so it disappears cleanly on hosts that haven't installed it.
99	
100	## Troubleshooting
101	
102	### "I don't see my running Claude"
103	
104	Stale `~/.claude/sessions/{pid}.json` files are skipped automatically — if
105	the PID isn't a descendant of any tmux pane, the row is omitted. If you
106	expect to see a session that isn't there:
107	
108	```bash
109	~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py panes        # raw TSV, see what it finds
110	ls -lt ~/.claude/sessions/                          # what files exist
111	ps -p <pid_from_filename>                           # is the process alive?
112	tmux list-panes -aF '#{pane_id} #{pane_pid} #{pane_current_command}'
113	```
114	
115	If the claude PID is alive but `_find_pane_for_pid` doesn't reach a tmux
116	pane (e.g., claude was launched outside tmux), the row is correctly
117	omitted — `tv agent-panes` only shows panes you can `switch-client` to.
118	
119	### "Codex/OpenCode/Cursor row has no session ID"
120	
121	The cwd-based reverse lookup couldn't find a stored session whose
122	`directory` matches the pane's `pane_current_path`. Common causes: agent
123	was started with `--cd` to a path that doesn't match storage; storage
124	was migrated. The pane still shows up — Enter still jumps to it; you just
125	won't get an automatic "resume this exact session" handle.
126	
127	### "I jumped to a pane and tmux says it doesn't exist"
128	
129	The picker is a snapshot. If a pane closes between snapshot and switch,
130	the action falls back to a `tmux display-message` warning and stays put.
131	Re-open the picker (`prefix + a`) to refresh.
132	
133	### "Recon doesn't appear in the Agents submenu"
134	
135	`menu-agents.sh` probes `command -v recon` and only adds the row when the
136	binary is on `PATH`. If you've just installed it, your tmux server may
137	need a fresh shell environment — `tmux source ~/.tmux.conf` is enough; no
138	restart required.
139	
140	## Related
141	
142	- [tmux keybindings](tmux/keybindings.md) — popup-menu surface
143	  (`prefix + Space`) where `→ Agents` lives, plus the full `prefix + ?`
144	  binding map.
145	- [Agent sessions browser](agent-overlays.md) — sister channel
146	  `tv agent-sessions` that browses **stored** session history (resume an old
147	  session vs. jump to a running one).
148	- [SpecStory internals](specstory-internals.md) — explains the
149	  `<!-- Provider Session UUID -->` reverse-lookup that lets the picker
150	  surface the matching `.specstory/history/*.md` for each row.
151	- Sibling deferred work: per-pane working/idle status glyph in the tmux
152	  window list itself (Option C of
153	  [`backlog/tmux-window-status-indicators.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/tmux-window-status-indicators.md)).
154
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Agent skills (`vercel-labs/skills`)
2	
3	This repo manages [`vercel-labs/skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills)
4	agent skills two ways, with sharply different scopes.
5	
6	## TL;DR
7	
8	| Scope | Lock file | Where the skill lives | Restored by |
9	|---|---|---|---|
10	| **Global** (every project, every shell) | `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` (chezmoi-managed) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` on every `chezmoi apply` |
11	| **Project** (only inside this repo's working tree, for editing skills) | `./skills-lock.json` (git-tracked) | `./.agents/skills/<name>/` | `.chezmoiscripts/repo/run_onchange_after_45_bootstrap_skills.sh.tmpl` on every `chezmoi apply` (when source dir == repo); manual fallback: `just bootstrap-skills` |
12	
13	The two scopes happen to overlap today (both install
14	`project-knowledge-harness`), but they serve different purposes — see "Why two
15	scopes?" below.
16	
17	## Global scope: must-have skills, on every machine
18	
19	The skills CLI does **not** yet support `npx skills install -g` from a lock
20	file ([upstream issue #283](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/283),
21	[#549](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549)). So we hand-roll
22	restore in two pieces:
23	
24	### `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` — the merger
25	
26	A `modify_` script that owns `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`. Every `chezmoi
27	apply`:
28	
29	1. Reads the live lock file via stdin.
30	2. Merges the **managed-set** declared in `$managed` (top of the script) into
31	   `.skills`, preserving any `installedAt`/`updatedAt`/`skillFolderHash` from
32	   the live entry.
33	3. Preserves any `.skills.<name>` entries **not** in the managed-set (so
34	   ad-hoc `npx skills add … -g` installs survive).
35	4. Preserves `.dismissed` and `.lastSelectedAgents` per-machine state
36	   verbatim.
37	
38	To declare a new must-have global skill, edit the inline `$managed` JSON in
39	that script:
40	
41	```json
42	{
43	  "skills": {
44	    "your-new-skill": {
45	      "source": "owner/repo",
46	      "sourceType": "github",
47	      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/owner/repo.git",
48	      "skillPath": "skills/your-new-skill/SKILL.md"
49	    }
50	  }
51	}
52	```
53	
54	Then run `chezmoi apply`. The merger writes the new entry into the lock; the
55	restore script (next section) sees the missing on-disk skill and installs it.
56	
57	### `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` — the restorer
58	
59	`onchange` hash trigger is the merger script's own SHA256 — so this script
60	re-runs whenever the **managed-set** is edited (not whenever the live lock
61	mutates from random `npx skills update -g` activity).
62	
63	For each entry in `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`:
64	
65	- If `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` exists → skip (already installed).
66	- Otherwise → `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y`.
67	
68	This is idempotent: a re-run on a fully-installed machine prints
69	"All globally-managed agent skills present; nothing to install" and exits.
70	
71	### After installing a new skill manually
72	
73	If you `npx skills add foo/bar -g` interactively on a machine and want it to
74	become managed across the fleet:
75	
76	1. `cat ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` — find the entry the CLI just wrote.
77	2. Copy `source` / `sourceType` / `sourceUrl` / `skillPath` into the
78	   `$managed.skills` block of `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl`.
79	3. Commit. Other hosts pick it up at next `chezmoi apply`.
80	
81	If you only want it on one machine, do nothing — the merger preserves the
82	live entry on the source machine, and other hosts simply never see it.
83	
84	## Project scope: editing-this-repo convenience
85	
86	`./skills-lock.json` + `./.agents/skills/` exist purely so that **when you're
87	editing the chezmoi repo itself**, agents launched from the repo root can use
88	`project-knowledge-harness` against the repo it documents. They are **not**
89	deployed (chezmoi-ignored: see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `.agents/skills`,
90	`.claude/skills`, `skills-lock.json`) and **not** git-tracked except for
91	`skills-lock.json` (`.gitignore` covers `.agents/`, `.claude/skills/`).
92	
93	Restore is automatic on `chezmoi apply` via
94	`.chezmoiscripts/repo/run_onchange_after_45_bootstrap_skills.sh.tmpl`. The script:
95	
96	1. Checks whether `.chezmoi.sourceDir` contains a `skills-lock.json` (i.e.
97	   this machine's chezmoi source dir IS the repo). If not, exits silently —
98	   project skills only matter when you're editing the repo with an agent.
99	2. Fast-path: if every skill named in the lock already has a
100	   `./.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, exits without invoking npx.
101	3. Otherwise runs `npx skills@latest experimental_install` from the source
102	   dir to rebuild `./.agents/skills/...` and `./.claude/skills/...` symlinks.
103	
104	Trigger hash: SHA256 of `skills-lock.json` content, so the script only
105	re-runs when the lock actually changes.
106	
107	Manual fallback (if you want to force a re-bootstrap, or you cloned the repo
108	to a path that isn't your chezmoi source dir):
109	
110	```sh
111	just bootstrap-skills
112	# → npx skills@latest experimental_install
113	```
114	
115	## Why two scopes?
116	
117	| Use case | Where to install |
118	|---|---|
119	| Skill you want available in every project, on every machine | Global (edit `$managed` in the merger script) |
120	| Skill that only makes sense inside this specific repo | Project (`npx skills add ... -y` from repo root, commit `skills-lock.json`) |
121	| Skill you're prototyping locally before deciding | Project, then promote to global once stable |
122	
123	`project-knowledge-harness` is in **both** scopes today because (a) the harness
124	itself targets *any* project so it belongs globally, and (b) we want to use it
125	on the chezmoi repo immediately, which the global install covers but
126	project-scope makes the lock-file dependency explicit for anyone reading
127	`skills-lock.json` here.
128	
129	## How `npx skills` actually wires agents (mechanism reference)
130	
131	Verified by reading [`vercel-labs/skills/src/agents.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/agents.ts)
132	and [`installer.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/installer.ts).
133	Important because the CLI's "I installed your skill for agent X" message does
134	**not** mean agent X actually reads from `~/.agents/skills/` at runtime — that
135	is a per-agent convention, not a guarantee.
136	
137	### Two install strategies
138	
139	| Strategy | What the CLI writes | Agents that use it |
140	|---|---|---|
141	| **Universal** (`skillsDir: '.agents/skills'`) | Nothing in agent-specific dir; agent reads `~/.agents/skills/` (global) or `./.agents/skills/` (project) directly | `cursor`, `opencode`, `codex`, `gemini-cli`, `copilot`, `antigravity`, `warp`, `replit`, `cline`, `kimi-cli`, `firebender`, `deep-agents` |
142	| **Per-agent symlink** | Symlink `~/.<agent>/skills/<name>` → `~/.agents/skills/<name>` (copy on Windows) | `claude-code`, `augment`, `bob`, `cortex`, `crush`, `goose`, `junie`, `kilo`, `kiro`, `kode`, `roo`, `trae`, `windsurf`, etc. |
143	
144	The skip happens at `installer.ts`:
145	
146	```ts
147	if (isGlobal && isUniversalAgent(agentType)) {
148	  return { /* skipped: no symlink, no copy */ };
149	}
150	```
151	
152	So `npx skills add foo -g -a cursor -a opencode` produces **zero** files in
153	`~/.cursor/skills/` or `~/.opencode/skills/`. Whether Cursor and OpenCode
154	actually pick up `~/.agents/skills/foo/SKILL.md` at runtime is up to those
155	agents (Anthropic's Skills spec is Claude Code's; others adopt by convention,
156	not contract).
157	
158	### Lock filename collision (easy to confuse)
159	
160	| Path | Scope | Owner |
161	|---|---|---|
162	| `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` | Global, **singular** `skill-` | Skills CLI |
163	| `./skills-lock.json` | Project, **plural** `skills-` | Skills CLI |
164	
165	Schema differs (global is v3 with `dismissed`/`lastSelectedAgents`; project is
166	flatter). Don't symlink one to the other.
167	
168	### Restore commands and their quirks
169	
170	| Command | What it does |
171	|---|---|
172	| `npx skills experimental_install` | Restores **project** lock (`./skills-lock.json`) only |
173	| `npx skills experimental_install -g` | `-g` is **silently ignored**, still project-only ([#283](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/283), [#549](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549)) |
174	| `npx skills update -g` | Updates already-installed global skills; does **not** backfill missing entries from the lock |
175	| `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y` | The only working "restore one missing global skill" idiom — what `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` loops over |
176	
177	### CLI flag gotchas
178	
179	- **Repo shorthand requires `/skills` suffix when skills live under `skills/`**.
180	  `npx skills add owner/repo` looks at `.agents/skills/` in that repo;
181	  `npx skills add owner/repo/skills` looks at `skills/`. Most third-party skill
182	  repos use the latter layout.
183	- **`-a` does NOT take comma-separated values**. Repeat the flag:
184	  `-a claude-code -a opencode -a cursor`.
185	- **Agent names are normalised** (`claude-code` not `claude`,
186	  `gemini-cli` not `gemini`, `copilot` not `github-copilot`). Run
187	  `npx skills add --list` (or trigger the validation error) to see the
188	  canonical list.
189	
190	### Per-agent env var overrides
191	
192	Agents that respect a custom config dir change where the symlink/skill is
193	read from:
194	
195	| Env var | Default | Effect |
196	|---|---|---|
197	| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | `~/.claude` | Skills CLI writes symlinks here instead |
198	| `CODEX_HOME` | `~/.codex` | Codex picks up skills from here (Codex is universal, so the global install relies on `~/.agents/skills/` regardless) |
199	| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | `~/.config` | Affects Cursor/OpenCode/Gemini-CLI lookup paths |
200	
201	If you set any of these and re-run `npx skills add -g`, the CLI writes to the
202	new location; chezmoi's lock-file management still uses
203	`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` (the lock is location-independent).
204	
205	## Anti-patterns
206	
207	- **Don't put skill source files (`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`,
208	  templates, etc.) in chezmoi source.** They're owned by the npx skills CLI;
209	  chezmoi managing them creates a constant fight with the CLI's
210	  `skillFolderHash`. Only the **lock file** is chezmoi-managed.
211	- **Don't run `chezmoi re-add ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`** to capture local
212	  changes. Edit the merger's `$managed` block instead — that's the
213	  source-of-truth list. `re-add` would freeze a snapshot of one machine's
214	  state into the source, defeating the merger's per-machine preservation.
215	- **Don't commit `./.agents/skills/`**. They're skill source clones that the
216	  npx CLI rewrites on every `update`; tracking them creates noisy diffs and
217	  accidental conflicts with upstream skill updates.
218	- **Don't add `-g` to `bootstrap-skills`**. That recipe is project-scope by
219	  design; global is owned by `chezmoi apply`.
220	
221	## References
222	
223	- Live `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` — merger source of truth
224	- Live `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` — restore loop
225	- [`vercel-labs/skills` README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) — CLI docs
226	- [Issue #283 — `skills install -g`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/283)
227	- [Issue #549 — global lock restore](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549)
228	- [`docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`](agent-overlays.md) — sibling pattern for
229	  Claude/Cursor/OpenCode `settings.json` overlays (also `modify_` based)
230
```

```text
1	# Claude Code keybindings (`~/.claude/keybindings.json`)
2	
3	Claude Code stores its TUI keymap in a separate file from `~/.claude/settings.json`. This page documents the file format, the scope of customisation, and how this repo manages it via a `modify_` overlay.
4	
5	| Surface | Path |
6	|---|---|
7	| Live file | `~/.claude/keybindings.json` |
8	| Source overlay | [`dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json) |
9	| Schema | <https://www.schemastore.org/claude-code-keybindings.json> |
10	| Docs | <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/keybindings> |
11	
12	## File shape
13	
14	```json
15	{
16	  "$schema": "https://www.schemastore.org/claude-code-keybindings.json",
17	  "$docs": "https://code.claude.com/docs/en/keybindings",
18	  "bindings": [
19	    {
20	      "context": "Chat",
21	      "bindings": {
22	        "shift+tab": "chat:cycleMode",
23	        "enter": "chat:submit",
24	        "ctrl+j": "chat:newline",
25	        "...": "..."
26	      }
27	    },
28	    { "context": "Global", "bindings": { "...": "..." } }
29	  ]
30	}
31	```
32	
33	The top-level `$schema` and `$docs` strings exist for editor integrations (autocomplete, hover-doc lookups). They are **not consumed by Claude Code itself** — but pinning them in the source-of-truth overlay keeps every machine quotable from the same canonical URLs. `$schema` is the [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) standard convention; `$docs` is a Claude-Code-specific extension that JSON Schema validators ignore. For a general primer on the mechanism — including how to author a schema for one of our own configs — see [JSON Schema in this repo](json-schema.md).
34	
35	`bindings` is an array of context-keyed entries. Each entry's `bindings` object maps a key string (`shift+tab`, `meta+p`, `ctrl+x ctrl+e` for sequences) to an action name (`chat:cycleMode`, `chat:submit`, …).
36	
37	### Contexts available
38	
39	Read from the user's live file as of 2026-04: `Global`, `Chat`, `Autocomplete`, `Settings`, `Doctor`, `Confirmation`, `Tabs`, `Transcript`, `HistorySearch`, `Task`, `ThemePicker`, `Scroll`, `Help`, `Attachments`, `Footer`, `MessageSelector`, `DiffDialog`, `ModelPicker`, `Select`, `Plugin`. Inspect your own copy for the full default set:
40	
41	```bash
42	jq '.bindings[] | .context' ~/.claude/keybindings.json
43	```
44	
45	## The `chat:cycleMode` limitation
46	
47	Permission modes (`default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `bypassPermissions`, `auto`, `dontAsk`) are switched only via the **single** action `chat:cycleMode` — bound to `shift+tab` by default. There is no documented action that jumps **directly** to a specific mode (no `chat:setMode`, no `chat:enterPlan`, etc.). Confirmed against `code.claude.com/docs/en/keybindings` 2026-04-27.
48	
49	Practical consequences:
50	
51	- You cannot bind a single key to "enter plan mode" — the only path is `Shift+Tab` `Shift+Tab` … through the cycle.
52	- The cycle order is `default → acceptEdits → plan → bypassPermissions` (and possibly `auto` if enabled in your build); to reach `bypassPermissions` from `acceptEdits` (the state you typically land in after `ExitPlanMode`, see below) you press `Shift+Tab` twice.
53	- Adding a duplicate binding (e.g. mapping a more accessible key to `chat:cycleMode`) doesn't shorten the path — it just gives you two ways to advance the same cycle. You still cycle.
54	
55	If/when Claude Code grows a per-mode action, fold the new action into [`dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json) following the merge guidance below.
56	
57	### Sibling pitfalls
58	
59	- [`pitfalls/claude-code-permission-mode-resets-after-interactive-prompt.md`](../../pitfalls/claude-code-permission-mode-resets-after-interactive-prompt.md) — the mode silently resets after `AskUserQuestion`, CodeIsland popups, remote-control inject, and `ExitPlanMode`. Lands in `acceptEdits` regardless of `permissions.defaultMode`.
60	- [`pitfalls/codeisland-auto-approves-permissionrequest.md`](../../pitfalls/codeisland-auto-approves-permissionrequest.md) — on macOS with the CodeIsland HUD installed, `ExitPlanMode` (and other permission requests) get rubber-stamped silently with `⎿ Allowed by PermissionRequest hook` / `⏺ Plan approved.` The `chat:cycleMode` recovery above is one of the visible fallout paths.
61	
62	## How the `modify_` overlay works
63	
64	[`dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json) is a tiny shell script (mirrors the shape of [`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_settings.json)). Two execution paths:
65	
66	1. **Bootstrap (empty stdin — live file does not exist yet)**: emit a minimal stub containing only `$schema` + `$docs`. Claude Code falls back to built-in defaults for any binding not present in the file.
67	2. **Steady-state (live file exists)**: pipe the live JSON into `jq '. * $overlay'`, which deep-merges the overlay over the live tree. The live `.bindings` array is preserved verbatim because the overlay has no `.bindings` key and `jq`'s `*` operator only replaces arrays that match an overlay key path.
68	
69	Verify locally:
70	
71	```bash
72	# Bootstrap path
73	echo '' | "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.claude/keybindings.json)"
74	
75	# Steady-state path
76	cat ~/.claude/keybindings.json | "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.claude/keybindings.json)" | jq '."$schema", (.bindings | length)'
77	```
78	
79	Apply / inspect via chezmoi:
80	
81	```bash
82	chezmoi diff ~/.claude/keybindings.json   # only $schema/$docs lines should ever differ
83	chezmoi apply ~/.claude/keybindings.json  # idempotent on second run
84	```
85	
86	### Adding a personal binding override (future)
87	
88	The overlay does **not** ship binding overrides today. The reason: `jq '. * $overlay'` replaces arrays wholesale at matching key paths — if we put a `bindings: [...]` entry in the overlay for one context, every other context would survive (because the merge is keyed on `$schema`/`$docs`/`bindings` at the top level, and `bindings` IS present in both), but the merge would replace the **entire** `bindings` array, clobbering every default Claude Code ships.
89	
90	To add overrides safely, extend the script's jq filter to merge `bindings` by `.context`. A sketch (not implemented):
91	
92	```jq
93	. as $base
94	| ($overlay | del(.bindings)) as $non_bindings_overlay
95	| ($overlay.bindings // []) as $overlay_bindings
96	| ($base * $non_bindings_overlay) as $merged
97	| $merged
98	| .bindings = (
99	    ($merged.bindings // []) as $live_bindings
100	    | reduce $overlay_bindings[] as $entry (
101	        $live_bindings;
102	        # If a context exists in $live, deep-merge .bindings; else append.
103	        if any(.[]; .context == $entry.context) then
104	          map(if .context == $entry.context
105	              then .bindings = (.bindings + $entry.bindings)
106	              else . end)
107	        else . + [$entry] end
108	      )
109	  )
110	```
111	
112	Don't write this filter speculatively — wait until there's a concrete binding worth pinning across machines, then implement and add a `bats` test in `tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats` alongside the existing Claude settings merger tests.
113	
114	## See also
115	
116	- [`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_settings.json) — the sibling overlay for `settings.json`. The hook-aware merger pattern there is the reference for any future array-merge work in this overlay.
117	- [`docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`](agent-overlays.md) — overall design of the coding-agent CLI overlays in this repo (Claude / OpenCode / Codex / Cursor).
118	- [`docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md`](chezmoi-prefixes.md) — `modify_` vs `create_` semantics and the rationale for choosing `modify_` here.
119
```

1	# CodexBar CLI
2	
3	[CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) shows usage stats for AI coding tools (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini, Copilot, etc.) without logging into each dashboard.
4	
5	- **macOS**: Full menu bar app + CLI
6	- **Linux**: CLI only
7	
8	## Installation
9	
10	Installed automatically via the `coding_agents` ansible role. On Linux, the binary is placed at `~/.local/bin/codexbar`.
11	
12	## Linux Usage
13	
14	On Linux, you **must** pass `--source cli` for the `usage` command. The default source (`auto`/`web`) is macOS-only.
15	
16	### Check live usage (rate limits / quotas)
17	
18	```bash
19	# Claude session/weekly limits
20	codexbar usage --provider claude --source cli
21	
22	# Other providers
23	codexbar usage --provider codex --source cli
24	codexbar usage --provider gemini --source cli
25	codexbar usage --provider copilot --source cli
26	
27	# JSON output (for scripting / Waybar)
28	codexbar usage --provider claude --source cli --json --pretty
29	```
30	
31	Example output:
32	
33	```
34	== Claude 2.1.34 (claude) ==
35	Session: 14% left [=-----------]
36	```
37	
38	### Check local cost (from JSONL logs, no auth needed)
39	
40	The `cost` command reads local log files (e.g. `~/.claude/`) and doesn't require auth.
41	
42	```bash
43	# All providers
44	codexbar cost
45	
46	# Claude only
47	codexbar cost --provider claude
48	
49	# JSON output
50	codexbar cost --provider claude --json --pretty
51	
52	# Force rescan of logs
53	codexbar cost --refresh
54	```
55	
56	Example output:
57	
58	```
59	Claude Cost (local)
60	Today: $0.54 · 851K tokens
61	Last 30 days: $8.50 · 9.1M tokens
62	```
63	
64	## Shell Aliases
65	
66	Defined in `~/.config/zsh/tools/40_codexbar.zsh`:
67	
68	| Alias | Command | Description |
69	|-------|---------|-------------|
70	| `cbu` | `codexbar usage --provider claude --source cli` | Claude usage |
71	| `cbc` | `codexbar cost --provider claude` | Claude local cost |
72	| `cbca` | `codexbar cost` | All providers local cost |
73	
74	## Supported Providers
75	
76	`codex`, `claude`, `cursor`, `opencode`, `factory`, `gemini`, `antigravity`, `copilot`, `zai`, `minimax`, `kimi`, `kiro`, `vertexai`, `augment`, `jetbrains`, `kimik2`, `amp`
77	
78	## Tips
79	
80	- Avoid `--provider all` with `usage` on Linux -- it tries each provider sequentially and can hang if a CLI isn't installed.
81	- The `cost` command works offline by scanning local JSONL log files.
82	- The `usage --source cli` command invokes the provider's CLI (e.g. `claude`) to get live rate-limit data.
83	- Config file: `~/.codexbar/config.json`
84
```

```text
1	# Ghostty & cmux
2	
3	[Ghostty](https://ghostty.org/) is a fast, native terminal emulator. [cmux](https://cmux.dev/) is a lightweight macOS terminal built on Ghostty for managing AI coding agents. Both read the same config file.
4	
5	## Managed config
6	
7	This repo manages `~/.config/ghostty/config` (via `dot_config/ghostty/config`). cmux reads this file first (before `~/Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config`).
8	
9	Key settings:
10	
11	- **`macos-option-as-alt = left`** — Left Option sends Meta/Esc+ so tmux `M-` keybindings work (theme switching `M-c`/`M-t`, layouts `M-1`..`M-5`, fine resize `M-h/j/k/l`). Right Option retains macOS compose behavior for accents and special characters.
12	- **`font-features = -calt, -liga, -dlig`** — Disables ligatures for code readability.
13	
14	> **Note**: Restart Ghostty/cmux after changing the config — it is read on launch, not hot-reloaded.
15	
16	Without `macos-option-as-alt`, macOS Option produces Unicode compose characters (e.g. `Option+c` → `ç`) instead of `Esc+c`, silently breaking all tmux Meta bindings. Alacritty and iTerm2 have their own equivalent settings (`window.option_as_alt` and Profiles > Keys > Left Option Key > Esc+ respectively).
17	
18	## `xterm-ghostty` terminfo on remote hosts
19	
20	When you SSH into a fresh remote, `$TERM=xterm-ghostty` but the remote has no matching terminfo entry. Symptoms: broken line-drawing, garbled prompts, `clear`/`tput` failures, Neovim rendering glitches. This is especially visible on the first cmux/tmux SSH into a new box.
21	
22	### Option 1 — Ghostty built-in (recommended for interactive shells)
23	
24	> - [Shell Integration - Features](https://ghostty.org/docs/features/shell-integration#ssh-integration)
25	
26	Add to `~/.config/ghostty/config`:
27	
28	```ini
29	shell-integration-features = ssh-env,ssh-terminfo
30	```
31	
32	- `ssh-terminfo`: auto-installs `xterm-ghostty` on the remote the first time you `ssh` from an interactive shell with Ghostty shell integration loaded.
33	- `ssh-env`: forwards `COLORTERM`, `TERM_PROGRAM`, `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION` via `SendEnv`, and falls back to `TERM=xterm-256color` where needed. The remote `sshd_config` needs a matching `AcceptEnv` line for the forwarded vars to take effect.
34	
35	**Limitations**: only triggers from interactive shells with the Ghostty wrapper active. It does not cover `ssh` invoked inside tmux/cmux panes, from scripts, or from wrapper tools (`rsync`, `aws`, `gcloud`, …). For those, use the manual helper below.
36	
37	### Option 2 — manual helper (works everywhere)
38	
39	A zsh function `ghostty-ssh-terminfo` is defined in [`dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh).
40	
41	```bash
42	ghostty-ssh-terminfo <ssh-host>
43	```
44	
45	What it does:
46	
47	- Validates local `infocmp` and the `xterm-ghostty` entry exist.
48	- Pipes `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty` into a **single** SSH call (no double password/MFA prompt).
49	- On the remote: probes for `tic`, creates `~/.terminfo`, and runs `TERMINFO="$HOME/.terminfo" tic -x -` — so no root/sudo needed.
50	- Suppresses only the harmless `older tic versions may treat the description field as an alias` warning (emitted by ncurses < 6.3). Real errors still surface and set a non-zero exit.
51	
52	Example:
53	
54	```bash
55	# First time connecting a new box from cmux/tmux
56	ghostty-ssh-terminfo remote
57	# → Installed xterm-ghostty terminfo on remote (in ~/.terminfo)
58	
59	# Verify
60	ssh remote 'infocmp xterm-ghostty >/dev/null && echo ok'
61	```
62	
63	### Smoke-test against `localhost`
64	
65	Yes — if `sshd` is running locally you can validate the function without touching a real remote:
66	
67	```bash
68	# Enable sshd (Linux)
69	sudo systemctl start ssh
70	# or macOS: System Settings → General → Sharing → Remote Login
71	
72	ghostty-ssh-terminfo localhost
73	```
74	
75	Caveats:
76	
77	- `localhost` already has your own `$HOME`, so this effectively writes to the *same* `~/.terminfo` your local shell reads. Useful as a wiring/error-path smoke test, not as a representative "fresh remote" check.
78	- If you already have the entry locally (which you do, otherwise `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty` would fail), the install is a no-op overwrite — still exercises the full pipeline end-to-end.
79	- For a cleaner test, point at a container or a VM where `xterm-ghostty` is definitely missing.
80	
81	## Why the warning appears (and can't be fully fixed client-side)
82	
83	The `|`-separated long description in Ghostty's terminfo is interpreted as an extra alias by `tic` / ncurses prior to 6.3. The entry still installs correctly; the warning is cosmetic. The only real fix is upgrading ncurses on the remote.
84	
85	## See also
86	
87	- [tmux](tmux.md) — tmux config and keybindings (cmux runs on top of tmux).
88	- [sesh](../sesh.md) — session picker used in the tmux setup.
89
```
</details></tool-use>
