 `./docs/tools/mirrors.md`

```text
1	# GFW / China Mirrors — `useChineseMirror`
2	
3	A single chezmoi prompt (`useChineseMirror`, answered at `chezmoi init`) drives
4	mirror configuration across every package ecosystem this repo touches. When
5	enabled, the mirror is wired up automatically on the next `chezmoi apply` —
6	no manual env-var editing needed.
7	
8	Most mirrors point at [TUNA (清华大学开源软件镜像站)](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/),
9	with a few exceptions where another mirror is the de-facto standard (npm →
10	npmmirror, Docker Hub → DaoCloud, Go modules → goproxy.cn, Ubuntu apt → Huawei Cloud).
11	
12	## Quick toggle
13	
14	```bash
15	# Check current value
16	chezmoi data | rg useChineseMirror
17	
18	# Flip the flag (re-runs the init prompt)
19	chezmoi init --force        # will re-ask useChineseMirror
20	
21	# Or edit ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml directly:
22	#   useChineseMirror = true / false
23	# Then:
24	chezmoi apply
25	```
26	
27	## Coverage matrix
28	
29	| Ecosystem | Managed by | Mirror | TUNA doc |
30	|---|---|---|---|
31	| **PyPI** (`uv` / `pip`) | `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` | Aliyun → TUNA → USTC (multi-index fallback) | [pypi](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/help/pypi/) |
32	| **npm** | `~/.npmrc` | `registry.npmmirror.com` | — |
33	| **Bun** | `~/.config/.bunfig.toml` | `registry.npmmirror.com` | — |
34	| **crates.io** (Cargo) | `~/.cargo/config.toml` | TUNA sparse index | [crates.io-index](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/help/crates.io-index/) |
35	| **RubyGems** | `~/.gemrc` | `mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/rubygems/` | [rubygems](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/help/rubygems/) |
36	| **Anaconda / Mamba** | `~/.condarc` | `mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/anaconda/{pkgs,cloud}` | [anaconda](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/help/anaconda/) |
37	| **Homebrew** (bottles + brew.git + core.git) | `$HOMEBREW_*` env vars (`~/.config/zsh/00_exports.zsh` + 2 bootstrap scripts) | `mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/homebrew-*` | [homebrew](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/help/homebrew/) |
38	| **Rustup** (dist + self-update) | `RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER` / `RUSTUP_UPDATE_ROOT` env vars | `mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/rustup` | [rustup](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/help/rustup/) |
39	| **mise** Node.js prebuilt | `MISE_NODE_MIRROR_URL` / `NODE_BUILD_MIRROR_URL` env vars | `mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/nodejs-release/` | [nodejs-release](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/help/nodejs-release/) |
40	| **Go modules** | `GOPROXY` env var | `goproxy.cn` (Qiniu; TUNA has no Go proxy) | — |
41	| **Docker Hub** (rootless Docker on Linux) | `~/.config/docker/daemon.json` via `modify_daemon.json.tmpl` | DaoCloud / USTC / NJU / ISCAS / Baidu / azk8s (fallback chain) | — |
42	| **Ubuntu apt** (Docker image only) | `Dockerfile` | Huawei Cloud | [ubuntu](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/help/ubuntu/) |
43	
44	## Where env vars are exported (three layers)
45	
46	Env-var-driven mirrors (Homebrew, Rustup, mise, Go) are exported in three
47	places so every code path gets the mirror:
48	
49	| Layer | File | Why |
50	|---|---|---|
51	| Interactive shells | `dot_config/zsh/00_exports.zsh.tmpl` | `brew install`, `rustup install`, `mise install`, `go install` from the terminal |
52	| First-run bootstrap | `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` | Installing Homebrew itself, first `brew install` + first `uv`/`ansible` setup (before `.zshrc` exists) |
53	| Ansible re-runs | `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` | `community.general.homebrew`, `mise install`, etc. in ansible subprocesses — regardless of the shell that invoked `chezmoi apply` |
54	
55	## What's NOT auto-mirrored (and why)
56	
57	- **System `apt` on real Linux hosts** — modifying `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/`
58	  requires sudo and users typically pre-configure apt during OS install.
59	  Only the Docker image sets Huawei Cloud apt (see `Dockerfile`).
60	- **`git clone` of github.com** — global `git insteadOf` rewrites break gh CLI
61	  and private repos; too invasive.
62	- **GitHub Releases / `raw.githubusercontent.com`** — TUNA has `github-release`
63	  but the mapping is incomplete; rewriting release URLs across ansible
64	  roles would be fragile.
65	- **pre-commit hooks / oh-my-zsh / TPM** — these clone from github.com;
66	  same rewrite concerns as above.
67	- **System `pip`** — `uv.toml` already covers the primary path; system pip
68	  only fires as a fallback in `security_tools` role.
69	
70	## npm postinstall scripts that download from GitHub Releases
71	
72	The npm registry is mirrored (`registry.npmmirror.com`), but **a small set
73	of npm packages run a `postinstall` script that downloads a prebuilt
74	binary directly from GitHub Releases** — bypassing the npm tarball
75	mirror entirely. From China, `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`
76	(Azure blob CDN) is frequently slow or unreachable, and these scripts
77	typically have **no env-var override** for the download URL.
78	
79	Symptom: `npm install -g <pkg>` hangs after printing
80	`Downloading https://github.com/.../releases/download/...` with no
81	further output. The npm tarball download itself succeeds (fast, from
82	npmmirror) — only the postinstall step hangs.
83	
84	| Package | Postinstall downloads | Workaround in this repo |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| `tree-sitter-cli` | `tree-sitter-{platform}-{arch}.gz` | `dot_ansible/roles/lazyvim_deps/tasks/main.yml` wraps with `timeout 180` → cargo fallback (crates.io is TUNA-mirrored) |
87	| `node-gyp` (transitive, when building native modules) | platform headers / pre-builts | No managed install — only triggers if a downstream package needs native build |
88	
89	When adding a new ansible task that runs `npm install -g <pkg>`:
90	
91	1. **Check if the package has a postinstall binary download** —
92	   `npm view <pkg> scripts.postinstall` or read its `install.js`.
93	2. If yes, **wrap with `timeout 180`** and a sensible fallback (cargo,
94	   apt, manual binary download from a mirrored host).
95	3. **Don't `set ignore_errors: true`** alone — it doesn't catch hangs,
96	   only failures. Use `failed_when: false` + an explicit
97	   `treesitter_npm.rc | default(1) != 0` gate on the fallback task so
98	   `timeout` exit 124 properly fires the next step.
99	
100	## Adding a new mirror
101	
102	1. Identify the ecosystem (env var or config file driven?).
103	2. **Env-var driven**: add to all three layers (`00_exports.zsh.tmpl` +
104	   `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` +
105	   `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`) inside the
106	   `{{ if .useChineseMirror -}} ... {{ end -}}` block.
107	3. **Config-file driven**: template the config under
108	   `dot_<tool>/<config>.tmpl` with `{{ if .useChineseMirror }} ... {{ else }} ... {{ end }}`.
109	   If the file is safe to always manage (eg. `uv.toml`, `.cargo/config.toml`), no ignore gate is needed.
110	   If it conflicts with user-managed files (eg. `.condarc`, `.gemrc`), also gate via
111	   `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`:
112	
113	   ```go-template
114	   {{- if not .useChineseMirror }}
115	   .condarc
116	   .gemrc
117	   {{- end }}
118	   ```
119	
120	4. Update the coverage matrix in this file and add a one-line entry to
121	   the `README.md` "Managed config files" section.
122	5. Test with `chezmoi execute-template --init --promptBool useChineseMirror=true < <template>` and
123	   `chezmoi diff`.
124	
125	## Troubleshooting
126	
127	### `curl: (18) Transferred a partial file` during brew install
128	
129	See [infrastructure-as-code.md → Troubleshooting](./infrastructure-as-code.md#troubleshooting).
130	
131	### Conda / Mamba: slow or failing channel refresh after toggling `useChineseMirror`
132	
133	Conda caches channel metadata. Force a refresh:
134	
135	```bash
136	conda clean -i    # invalidate index cache
137	mamba clean -i    # same for mamba
138	```
139	
140	### Rust toolchain still slow after `useChineseMirror=true`
141	
142	Rustup reads env vars at process start. If you enabled the flag but already
143	have a zsh session open, the old values are still exported. Open a new shell
144	or run `source ~/.zshrc && source ~/.config/zsh/00_exports.zsh`. Verify:
145	
146	```bash
147	echo $RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER   # should be https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/rustup
148	```
149	
150	### Go modules not using goproxy.cn
151	
152	Same as Rustup — re-source. Also check that `GOPROXY` isn't being overridden
153	by `go env -w GOPROXY=...` which persists to `~/.config/go/env` and takes
154	precedence over the env var. To unset a persistent value:
155	
156	```bash
157	go env -u GOPROXY
158	```
159	
160	## Related
161	
162	- [TUNA mirror site](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/) — full list of what TUNA hosts
163	- [TUNA Homebrew guide](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/help/homebrew/)
164	- [TUNA rustup guide](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/help/rustup/)
165	- [TUNA anaconda guide](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/help/anaconda/)
166	- [TUNA rubygems guide](https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/help/rubygems/)
167	- [goproxy.cn](https://goproxy.cn/) — Qiniu-hosted Go module proxy
168	- [npmmirror](https://npmmirror.com/) — Alibaba-hosted npm mirror
169
```

1	# Sesh - Smart Tmux Session Manager
2	
3	[Sesh](https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh) is a CLI that manages tmux sessions using zoxide, giving you instant access to your most-used projects with smart session naming, startup commands, and preview.
4	
5	## Installation
6	
7	Sesh is installed automatically by the `devtools` ansible role:
8	
9	- **macOS**: `brew install sesh`
10	- **Linux**: GitHub release binary → `~/.local/bin/sesh`
11	
12	No manual installation needed after `chezmoi apply`.
13	
14	## Keybindings
15	
16	### ZSH (`Alt+S`)
17	
18	Press `Alt+S` anywhere in the shell to open the sesh picker. This uses `fzf-tmux` as a popup with full filtering support.
19	
20	Source: `~/.config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh`
21	
22	### ZSH Helpers
23	
24	The managed zsh config provides four shell helpers, each with a distinct
25	weight class so you can pick the right tool for the moment:
26	
27	| Command | Weight | When to use | Session name |
28	|---------|--------|-------------|--------------|
29	| `shere` | Bare shell | Ad-hoc cd: just need a tmux session at `$PWD`, no editor, no layout | `<basename>` |
30	| `sroot` | Sesh defaults | Want sesh's wildcard / `default_session` behavior at the git root | sesh-determined (`dir_length=2`) |
31	| `scode` | Heavy | "Open the coding-agent layout for *this* repo" — nvim 75% \| `specstory run` 25% + btop window | `coding-agent/<repo>` |
32	| `svibe` | Heaviest | "Vibe coding" — N tiled agent panes + lazygit + nvim | `vibe/<repo>` |
33	
34	The underlying functions are `sesh-here` / `sesh-root` / `sesh-code` /
35	`sesh-vibe`; you can call them directly if you prefer function names over
36	aliases.
37	
38	#### `shere` — bare shell at `$PWD`
39	
40	Intentionally lightweight: creates a tmux session named after the basename of
41	the directory, drops you into a shell, **does not** trigger sesh's
42	`default_session.startup_command` (nvim) or any wildcard layout. Use it when
43	you've cd'd somewhere ephemeral and just want session persistence.
44	
45	```bash
46	shere                          # bare shell session at $PWD
47	shere npm run dev              # session that runs `npm run dev` instead of a shell
48	shere -c "specstory run"       # explicit --command flag
49	shere -p ~/some/dir            # explicit path; -p + bare args also works
50	```
51	
52	> **Behavior change (2026-04)**: `shere` used to inherit sesh's default
53	> startup_command, which opened nvim. It was renamed to "lightweight session"
54	> because the heavy editor-first workflow is now `scode`. If you want the old
55	> behavior, use `sroot` (which honors the sesh wildcards/defaults) or
56	> `sesh connect "$PWD"` directly.
57	
58	#### `sroot` — git root with sesh defaults
59	
60	Connects to the current git repo's top-level (or `$PWD` if not in a repo) and
61	honors all of sesh.toml: wildcard layouts (e.g. `/Volumes/Data/Program/*/*`
62	auto-applies `project.yaml`), `default_session.startup_command`, etc. This is
63	the right choice if you've been customizing sesh.toml and want those
64	customizations to apply.
65	
66	```bash
67	sroot                          # connect to git root, sesh.toml decides layout
68	sroot specstory run codex      # explicit command override
69	```
70	
71	#### `scode` — repo-scoped coding-agent layout
72	
73	`scode` creates a session **named after the current repo**, so different
74	repos no longer collide on the single `coding-agent` session name. This was
75	the headline pain point of the old `sesh connect coding-agent` workflow:
76	the second invocation from a different repo would silently reuse the
77	existing session pointing at the *wrong* repo.
78	
79	```bash
80	scode                          # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
81	scode codex                    # right pane runs `specstory run codex`
82	scode opencode                 # right pane runs `opencode` raw (not yet a specstory provider)
83	scode --no-specstory claude    # right pane runs `claude` raw (no markdown auto-save)
84	scode --on-exit kill claude    # Ctrl+C closes the right pane (vs default: drops to shell)
85	scode --on-exit restart codex  # codex auto-respawns on crash
86	scode -p ~/work/foo            # explicit repo path
87	scode --no-attach              # build the session in the background, don't switch
88	scode -h                       # help
89	```
90	
91	Layout (window 1 "editor"):
92	
93	```
94	┌─────────────────────────────┬──────────────┐
95	│ nvim                        │ specstory    │
96	│ (75% width)                 │ run [agent]  │
97	│                             │ (25% width)  │
98	└─────────────────────────────┴──────────────┘
99	```
100	
101	Window 2 "monitor": `btop` (falls back to `htop` / `top`).
102	
103	**Refuses outside a git repo** — if you're not in a repo, you don't want the
104	heavy layout. Use `shere` for bare shells or `svibe` if you really want a
105	vibe layout in a non-repo directory (svibe also requires a repo, but that's
106	because vibe layouts make even less sense without git context).
107	
108	##### Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with `--no-specstory`)
109	
110	| Argument | Right-pane command |
111	|----------|--------------------|
112	| (none) | `specstory run` (defaults to claude with auto-save md) |
113	| `claude` / `codex` / `cursor` / `droid` / `gemini` | `specstory run <name>` (known specstory providers) |
114	| `opencode` and other unknown CLIs | runs the binary directly |
115	| any agent + `--no-specstory` | runs the binary directly (raw) |
116	
117	> `opencode` is currently raw because specstory upstream doesn't support it
118	> as a provider yet. Tracked in
119	> [`backlog/specstory-opencode-support.md`](../../backlog/specstory-opencode-support.md)
120	> — when `specstoryai/getspecstory#156` lands, the case statement in
121	> `_sesh_wrap_agent` gets a one-line update and opencode joins the auto-wrap
122	> list.
123	
124	##### `--on-exit` modes
125	
126	What happens when **any** pane command exits (agent, nvim, btop in `scode`;
127	agent, lazygit, nvim in `svibe`) — clean quit, Ctrl+C, or crash:
128	
129	| Mode | Behavior |
130	|------|----------|
131	| `shell` (default) | Pane prints a yellow hint and drops into `$SHELL`. You can re-launch the command (the hint shows the exact invocation), switch windows, or close the pane manually. Costs one background `$SHELL` process per pane while the command isn't running. |
132	| `kill` | Pane/window closes when the command exits. The historical / tmux-default behavior. |
133	| `restart` | Wraps the command in `while true; do CMD \|\| true; sleep 1; done`. Use Ctrl+C twice quickly to break the loop and land in shell. Useful when iterating on a crash-prone tool. |
134	
135	> The `shell` default trades one background process per pane for far better
136	> recoverability — the most common reported pain point with the old
137	> `coding-agent` workflow was "I hit Ctrl+C in the agent and lost the pane
138	> plus the 75/25 layout"; the same applies to accidentally `:q`-ing nvim or
139	> quitting btop/lazygit.
140	
141	> The flag applies uniformly to every command-running pane in the layout —
142	> there is no per-surface override. If you want e.g. lazygit to die on quit
143	> but agents to drop to shell, file a feature request.
144	
145	##### Single-agent only
146	
147	`scode` is single-agent by design. If you want multiple agents in parallel,
148	use `svibe --agents …`. Passing `--agents` to `scode` errors with a hint to
149	switch to `svibe`.
150	
151	> The legacy `coding-agent` named session in `sesh.toml` is **kept for
152	> back-compat** (still appears in the sesh picker, still works as
153	> `sesh connect coding-agent`) but `scode` is the preferred entry point.
154	> See the "DEPRECATED" comment block in sesh.toml.
155	
156	#### `svibe` — parametric multi-agent vibe layout
157	
158	Built directly with tmux scripting (not tmuxp) because pane counts are
159	parametric and tmuxp YAML can't express that.
160	
161	Two ways to specify which agents run:
162	
163	```bash
164	# Homogeneous (positional): all panes run the same agent
165	svibe                                            # N auto-picked × claude (see below)
166	svibe 2                                          # 2× claude
167	svibe 4 codex                                    # 4× codex
168	svibe 6 opencode                                 # 6× opencode (heavy — large monitor recommended)
169	
170	# Heterogeneous (--agents): one entry per pane, list length = pane count
171	svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode       # 4 panes, mixed
172	svibe --agents claude,opencode                   # 2 panes, mixed
173	svibe --agents 'claude, codex, opencode'         # whitespace around commas tolerated
174	
175	# Other flags (work with both modes)
176	svibe --on-exit kill 4 claude                    # Ctrl+C closes panes
177	svibe --on-exit restart --agents codex,opencode  # auto-respawn loop
178	svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                    # 4× raw claude (no markdown auto-save)
179	svibe --min-width 120                            # wider panes → fewer auto columns
180	svibe -p ~/repo --agents claude,codex            # explicit path
181	svibe -h                                         # help
182	```
183	
184	Mixing positional `[N] [CLI]` with `--agents` is **rejected** to keep
185	semantics unambiguous — pick one mode.
186	
187	##### Width-aware defaults
188	
189	Both **how many panes** (when `N` is omitted) and **how they're laid out**
190	are derived from the current terminal width ÷ a min-width threshold.
191	
192	| Knob | Default | Override |
193	|------|---------|----------|
194	| `min_width` (cols) | `80` | env `SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH` or flag `--min-width COLS` |
195	| `term_width` (cols) | `$COLUMNS` with `tput cols` fallback | (read at invocation time) |
196	
197	- **Auto N** (when neither positional `N` nor `--agents` was given):
198	  `N = clamp(term_width / min_width, 1, 12)`. So on a 240-col terminal:
199	  `min-width 80` → `N=3`; `min-width 120` → `N=2`; `min-width 60` → `N=4`.
200	- **Agents-window layout**: if all `N` panes fit side-by-side at
201	  `≥ min_width` each, use `even-horizontal` (N columns). Otherwise fall
202	  back to `tiled` (grid). Press `prefix + Space` to cycle through tmux's
203	  built-in layouts interactively if you want a different view.
204	
205	Layout (3 windows):
206	
207	```
208	window 1 "agents"    — N agent panes (columns if all fit at ≥min-width,
209	                       else tiled grid; mixed agents allowed)
210	window 2 "git"       — lazygit (or `git status` fallback)
211	window 3 "edit"      — nvim
212	```
213	
214	Pane count is bounded `[1, 12]`. Above ~6 the tiled grid becomes too
215	cramped on most displays — the cap is conservative, not technical.
216	
217	##### Validation (fail-fast)
218	
219	`svibe` validates before building anything:
220	
221	1. `--agents` and positional `[N] [CLI]` cannot both be set
222	2. `--on-exit` must be `shell` / `kill` / `restart`
223	3. Pane count in `[1, 12]`
224	4. Must be inside a git repo
225	5. **Every** agent CLI in the list must exist in `$PATH`
226	
227	This avoids the "4-pane window where one pane is silently dead" failure mode
228	you'd get if validation were per-pane.
229	
230	##### `--no-specstory` and `--on-exit`
231	
232	Same semantics as `scode`. The wrapping is **per-pane**, so you can mix
233	opencode (raw) with claude (specstory-wrapped) freely:
234	
235	```bash
236	# 3 panes — opencode raw, claude wrapped, codex wrapped, all share --on-exit shell
237	svibe --agents opencode,claude,codex
238	```
239	
240	Like `scode`, `svibe` refuses outside a git repo. Use `shere` for plain
241	shells in arbitrary directories.
242	
243	### Picking between the four
244	
245	Decision tree:
246	
247	```
248	Are you in a git repo?
249	├── No  → shere (bare shell) or sroot (if you want sesh defaults)
250	└── Yes → Do you want a layout?
251	          ├── No                       → shere or sroot
252	          ├── Single editor + side    → scode
253	          └── Multiple parallel agents → svibe
254	```
255	
256	All four are idempotent: re-invoking with the same target attaches to the
257	existing session instead of creating a duplicate.
258	
259	### tmux
260	
261	All keybindings use the tmux prefix (default `Ctrl+B`).
262	
263	| Keybinding | Action |
264	|------------|--------|
265	| `prefix + g` | Open sesh picker popup (fzf with preview, icons, filtering) |
266	| `prefix + T` | Open sesh picker via television (tv) in a tmux popup |
267	| `prefix + O` | Open sesh built-in picker in a tmux popup |
268	| `prefix + W` | Open sesh window picker (fzf) -- switch or create tmux windows |
269	| `prefix + S` | Switch to last session (via `sesh last`) |
270	| `prefix + 9` | Jump to root of current git repo/worktree |
271	
272	Source: `~/.tmux.conf`
273	
274	`prefix + g` avoids relying on `Shift`, so it does not fall through to tmux's built-in `prefix + t` clock shortcut on terminals that do not report uppercase prefix bindings reliably.
275	
276	### Picker Keybindings (inside fzf popup)
277	
278	| Key | Action |
279	|-----|--------|
280	| `Ctrl+A` | Show all sessions |
281	| `Ctrl+T` | Filter: tmux sessions only |
282	| `Ctrl+G` | Filter: configured sessions only |
283	| `Ctrl+X` | Filter: zoxide directories only |
284	| `Ctrl+F` | Filter: find directories (`fd`) |
285	| `Ctrl+D` | Kill selected tmux session |
286	| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Navigate down/up |
287	
288	## Shell Completion
289	
290	ZSH tab completion for `sesh` subcommands and flags is auto-generated into `~/.zfunc/_sesh` on first load (and regenerated when sesh version changes). This follows the project's [completion pattern](zsh/zsh-completions.md).
291	
292	Manual regeneration:
293	
294	```bash
295	sesh completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_sesh
296	rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit
297	```
298	
299	## Configuration
300	
301	Config file: `~/.config/sesh/sesh.toml` (managed by chezmoi)
302	
303	### Schema Autocomplete
304	
305	The config includes a JSON Schema directive for editor autocomplete via [taplo](https://taplo.tamasfe.dev/):
306	
307	```toml
308	#:schema https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/raw/main/sesh.schema.json
309	```
310	
311	### Key Options
312	
313	| Option | Description |
314	|--------|-------------|
315	| `sort_order` | Session type display order: `tmux`, `config`, `tmuxinator`, `zoxide` |
316	| `dir_length` | Directory components in session names (default: 1) |
317	| `blacklist` | Regex patterns to hide from the picker |
318	| `cache` | Enable stale-while-revalidate caching (experimental) |
319	
320	### Default Session
321	
322	Applied to all sessions unless overridden:
323	
324	```toml
325	[default_session]
326	startup_command = "nvim"
327	preview_command = "eza --all --git --icons --color=always {}"
328	```
329	
330	- `startup_command`: runs when a new session is created
331	- `preview_command`: shown in the fzf preview pane (`{}` = session path)
332	
333	### Named Sessions
334	
335	Pin frequently used directories with custom names and commands:
336	
337	```toml
338	[[session]]
339	name = "chezmoi"
340	path = "~/.local/share/chezmoi"
341	tmuxinator = "chezmoi"    # delegates to tmuxinator for reliable multi-window setup
342	
343	[[session]]
344	name = "home"
345	path = "~"
346	disable_startup_command = true
347	```
348	
349	Available fields: `name`, `path`, `startup_command`, `preview_command`, `disable_startup_command`, `windows`.
350	
351	### Wildcard Sessions
352	
353	Apply settings to directories matching a glob pattern:
354	
355	```toml
356	[[wildcard]]
357	pattern = "~/repos/*"
358	startup_command = "nvim"
359	```
360	
361	- `*` matches one level, `**` matches recursively
362	- Explicit `[[session]]` entries take priority over wildcards
363	
364	#### Per-project layout via tmuxp `--append`
365	
366	For repos that benefit from a structured layout (editor / shell / lazygit
367	windows), wildcards can chain a `tmuxp load --append` on top of the bare
368	session sesh creates. Same trick as the `coding-agent` named session — see
369	[Approach B below](#approach-b-tmuxp-via-startup_command-active) for the
370	underlying mechanic.
371	
372	```toml
373	# All repos under /Volumes/Data/Program/<group>/<repo>
374	[[wildcard]]
375	pattern = "/Volumes/Data/Program/*/*"
376	startup_command = "cd {} && tmuxp load -a -y ~/.config/tmuxp/project.yaml && tmux kill-window -t :1 2>/dev/null; tmux select-window -t :editor 2>/dev/null"
377	```
378	
379	The `{}` placeholder is the matched path. The leading `cd {}` is
380	load-bearing, and pairs with an equally load-bearing **omission** in the
381	yaml: neither `project.yaml` nor `coding-agent.yaml` sets session-level
382	`start_directory`. Every "obvious" value silently breaks in one of three
383	ways — tmuxp resolves yaml strings via Python's `os.path.expandvars` (no
384	bash `${VAR:-default}` fallback); tmuxp resolves `.` / `./foo` against
385	the yaml **file's** directory (not the process cwd); and when libtmux
386	passes any of those results to `tmux new-window -c`, an invalid path
387	silently falls back to `$HOME`. By omitting `start_directory` entirely,
388	libtmux calls `tmux new-window` without `-c`, so tmux inherits the cwd
389	from the caller — and sesh's `send-keys` runs tmuxp from inside a pane
390	that `cd {}` has already moved to the matched path. Full write-up in
391	[pitfalls/tmuxp-append-ignores-session-start-directory.md](../../pitfalls/tmuxp-append-ignores-session-start-directory.md).
392	
393	After the append, the empty initial window sesh always creates is killed
394	(`-t :1`), and focus moves to the `editor` window so nvim is foregrounded
395	immediately.
396	
397	The pattern targets `/Volumes/Data/Program/*/*` (canonical paths) rather
398	than `~/Documents/Program/*/*` because zoxide records canonical paths
399	(see [zoxide.md](zoxide.md) → `_ZO_RESOLVE_SYMLINKS`). One pattern catches
400	both surface and canonical entries.
401	
402	### Custom multi-section preview
403	
404	The default `eza` preview only shows a file listing. The
405	[`~/bin/sesh-preview`](../../bin/executable_sesh-preview) script renders a
406	richer view in the fzf preview pane:
407	
408	1. **Header**: dir name, parent path, git branch + dirty count + ahead/behind, mtime
409	2. **README**: first 25 lines, syntax-highlighted via `bat` if available
410	3. **Recent commits**: last 5 oneline commits (git repos only)
411	4. **File tree**: `eza --tree --level=2` with build dirs ignored
412	
413	Wired in `sesh.toml`:
414	
415	```toml
416	[default_session]
417	preview_command = "~/bin/sesh-preview {}"
418	```
419	
420	Falls back to plain `head`/`ls` if `bat`/`eza` are missing, and gracefully
421	handles non-directory args (sesh sometimes hands the picker raw session
422	strings rather than paths). Output is capped under ~50 lines to avoid
423	fzf preview pane scroll on first paint.
424	
425	### Windows
426	
427	Define reusable window layouts:
428	
429	```toml
430	[[session]]
431	name = "my-project"
432	path = "~/repos/my-project"
433	windows = ["git"]
434	
435	[[window]]
436	name = "git"
437	startup_script = "lazygit"
438	```
439	
440	## Recommended tmux Settings
441	
442	These are already set in `~/.tmux.conf`:
443	
444	```
445	set -g detach-on-destroy off   # stay in tmux when closing a session
446	bind-key x kill-pane           # skip kill-pane confirmation
447	```
448	
449	## Integration with Other Tools
450	
451	### fzf
452	
453	Sesh's primary picker integration. The `fzf-tmux` wrapper renders fzf inside a tmux popup. Our setup uses `--icons` for Nerd Font glyphs and `sesh preview` for the preview pane.
454	
455	### zoxide
456	
457	Sesh uses zoxide's frecency database to suggest directories. Any directory you `cd` into is automatically tracked and appears in `sesh list -z`.
458	
459	`_ZO_RESOLVE_SYMLINKS=1` (set in
460	[`zsh/tools/20_zoxide.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/tools/20_zoxide.zsh)) makes
461	zoxide canonicalise paths before storing them, so symlink-heavy setups
462	(e.g. `~/Documents/Program -> /Volumes/Data/Program`) don't fragment a
463	single physical directory's frecency across two phantom entries. Sesh
464	wildcards should target the canonical pattern (`/Volumes/Data/Program/*/*`)
465	rather than the surface symlink.
466	
467	To bootstrap a fresh DB with the directories you'd like sesh to surface
468	immediately (without waiting for organic `cd` traffic), the simplest path
469	is a one-shot Python script that reads the binary `db.zo` (version 3
470	format: `u32 ver, u64 count, then per-entry: u64 path_len, path bytes,
471	f64 rank, u64 ts`), inserts new entries with `rank=1.0`, and writes back.
472	Existing entries with higher scores are preserved. Sample workflow lives
473	in [pitfalls/zoxide-symlink-fragmentation.md](../../pitfalls/zoxide-symlink-fragmentation.md)
474	if/when that pitfall doc is created.
475	
476	### Neovim (in-editor zoxide picker)
477	
478	For jumping between repos without leaving Neovim, [`nvim/lua/plugins/zoxide-picker.lua`](../../dot_config/nvim/exact_plugins/zoxide-picker.lua)
479	adds a snacks.picker over `zoxide query --list --score`:
480	
481	| Keymap | Action |
482	|--------|--------|
483	| `<leader>fz` | Pick repo, change tab-local cwd via `:tcd` |
484	| `<leader>fZ` | Pick repo, change global cwd via `:cd` |
485	
486	`:tcd` (tab-local) is the default to avoid confusing LazyVim's
487	project-root detection when you have buffers from multiple projects open.
488	Use `:cd` (`<leader>fZ`) when you genuinely want the whole nvim session
489	to follow.
490	
491	### Three project pickers compared
492	
493	LazyVim ends up with **three overlapping but distinct** project-jump
494	entry points. Pick the one that matches your intent:
495	
496	| Where | Trigger | Source | What it does |
497	|-------|---------|--------|--------------|
498	| Inside nvim | `<leader>fp` (or dashboard `p`) | `snacks.picker.projects` — oldfiles git roots + `fd` over `dev` dirs | `:tcd` + `persistence.nvim` restore (last buffers/windows for that cwd) |
499	| Inside nvim | `<leader>fz` / `<leader>fZ` | Full zoxide DB (frecency, 100+ entries) | Pure `:tcd` / `:cd`, no session restore |
500	| Inside tmux | `prefix + g` (sesh fzf) | tmux + sesh.toml + zoxide | Switch/create tmux session, spawn nvim + lazygit fresh |
501	
502	Rough heuristic:
503	
504	- **Already in nvim, want to peek at another repo's file** → `<leader>fz`
505	  (cheap, no session ceremony)
506	- **Already in nvim, want to fully resume work on another repo** →
507	  `<leader>fp` (restores buffers/windows you had last time)
508	- **Outside nvim, want a clean per-repo workspace** → `prefix+g` from tmux
509	  (gets you the layout from `~/.config/tmuxp/project.yaml`)
510	
511	### Configuring the snacks projects picker
512	
513	The defaults look at `~/dev` and `~/projects` (which probably don't exist
514	on your machine), plus oldfiles-derived git roots. To make `<leader>fp`
515	surface every repo under your project home, add it to `dev` —
516	[`projects.lua`](../../dot_config/nvim/exact_plugins/projects.lua) does this
517	for `/Volumes/Data/Program`:
518	
519	```lua
520	{
521	  "folke/snacks.nvim",
522	  opts = {
523	    picker = {
524	      sources = {
525	        projects = {
526	          dev = { "/Volumes/Data/Program" },  -- canonical path, not the symlink
527	          max_depth = 2,                       -- catches <group>/<repo>
528	        },
529	      },
530	    },
531	  },
532	}
533	```
534	
535	To **manually pin** a project that doesn't have a `.git` (or you want it
536	permanently surfaced regardless of `fd` discovery), set `projects` to
537	a list of paths:
538	
539	```lua
540	projects = {
541	  vim.fn.expand("~/.local/share/chezmoi"),
542	  vim.fn.expand("~/.config/nvim"),
543	  "/Volumes/Data/Program/Personal/some-repo",
544	},
545	```
546	
547	Both `dev` (auto-discovered via `fd`) and `projects` (manual list) are
548	merged with oldfiles entries before fzf renders. Snacks dedupes by path.
549	
550	The `confirm = "load_session"` default delegates to `persistence.nvim`
551	(also wired in `projects.lua`); it restores the last buffer/window
552	layout for that cwd. If `persistence.nvim` isn't installed, `load_session`
553	silently falls back to opening the file picker after `:tcd`.
554	
555	### Television (tv)
556	
557	[Television](https://github.com/alexpasmantier/television) has a built-in [sesh channel](https://alexpasmantier.github.io/television/community/channels-unix/#sesh). Television is installed by the `devtools` ansible role (`brew install television` on macOS; Linuxbrew on Linux when available, otherwise skipped with a warning because upstream currently ships only `unknown-linux-gnu` binaries that require glibc ≥ 2.39 — incompatible with Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. See [docs/linux-package-sources.md](../linux-package-sources.md)).
558	
559	**tmux keybinding:** `prefix + T` opens television's sesh channel in a tmux popup.
560	
561	```
562	bind-key "T" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Sesh (tv) ' "tv sesh"
563	```
564	
565	Use `Ctrl-s` to cycle through sources (all, tmux, config, zoxide, fd), and `Ctrl-d` to kill the highlighted session.
566	
567	A custom cable channel config at `~/.config/television/cable/sesh.toml` overrides the built-in channel with richer source cycling and actions matching our fzf picker setup.
568	
569	### Raycast (macOS)
570	
571	The [sesh Raycast extension](https://www.raycast.com/joshmedeski/sesh) provides GUI-based session switching outside the terminal.
572	
573	## Customization Tips
574	
575	1. **Add project sessions**: Edit `~/.config/sesh/sesh.toml` (via `chezmoi edit ~/.config/sesh/sesh.toml`) to pin your most-used projects.
576	
577	2. **Wildcard for monorepos**: Use `pattern = "~/work/monorepo/packages/*"` to auto-configure all sub-projects.
578	
579	3. **Per-project startup**: Set `startup_command` to launch dev servers, editors, or TUI tools automatically.
580	
581	4. **Preview with bat**: Use `preview_command = "bat --color=always {}/README.md"` to show project READMEs in the picker.
582	
583	5. **Multiple windows**: Define `[[window]]` entries and reference them in sessions for multi-pane layouts (e.g., editor + lazygit).
584	
585	## Pane Layouts (Advanced)
586	
587	### Sesh Limitations
588	
589	Sesh **cannot** create pane splits natively. Each `[[window]]` gets exactly one pane with one `startup_script`. There is no `panes`, `layout`, `size`, or `ratio` configuration.
590	
591	If you need predefined pane layouts (e.g., "left pane = nvim 75%, right pane = specstory run 25%"), you must use an external tool.
592	
593	### The `tmuxp` Field is Dead Code (as of sesh v2.24)
594	
595	**Important**: The `tmuxp` field in `sesh.toml` (on `[[session]]` and `[default_session]`) is defined in the Go struct and JSON schema, but **never read or used** by sesh's source code. Only `tmuxinator` has a working integration.
596	
597	Evidence from source code:
598	- `startup/config.go` checks `Tmuxinator` and `StartupCommand` but **not** `Tmuxp`
599	- `connector/connect.go` has a `tmuxinatorStrategy` but **no** `tmuxpStrategy`
600	- Setting `tmuxp = "..."` in sesh.toml does nothing -- the session falls through to `default_session.startup_command`
601	
602	### Approach B: tmuxp via `startup_command` (Active)
603	
604	Use sesh's `startup_command` to call `tmuxp load --append`, which appends windows from a tmuxp YAML into the sesh-created session, then kill the initial empty window.
605	
606	Config in `sesh.toml`:
607	```toml
608	[[session]]
609	name = "coding-agent"
610	path = "~"
611	startup_command = "cd ~ && tmuxp load -a -y ~/.config/tmuxp/coding-agent.yaml && tmux kill-window -t coding-agent:1"
612	```
613	
614	(The leading `cd ~` is load-bearing for the same tmuxp-append reason
615	described under the wildcard section above.)
616	
617	Layout defined in `~/.config/tmuxp/coding-agent.yaml`:
618	```yaml
619	session_name: coding-agent
620	windows:
621	  - window_name: editor
622	    layout: main-vertical
623	    options:
624	      main-pane-width: 75%    # 3:1 ratio
625	    panes:
626	      - shell_command: nvim
627	      - shell_command: specstory run
628	  - window_name: monitor
629	    panes:
630	      - shell_command: btop
631	```
632	
633	**How it works:**
634	1. `sesh connect coding-agent` → sesh creates a tmux session named `coding-agent` at `~`
635	2. `startup_command` runs inside the first pane via `tmux send-keys`
636	3. `tmuxp load -a -y` appends the "editor" and "monitor" windows to the current session
637	4. `tmux kill-window -t coding-agent:1` removes the initial empty window sesh created
638	
639	**Pros:** tmuxp already installed, declarative YAML, `--append` avoids session conflict.
640	**Cons:** brief flash of empty window being killed; `startup_command` is `send-keys` so timing-sensitive.
641	
642	**Requires:** `tmuxp` (`pip install tmuxp` or `uv tool install tmuxp`)
643	
644	### Approach C: tmuxinator Native Integration (Alternative)
645	
646	Sesh has full native support for tmuxinator. When `tmuxinator` field is set, sesh **bypasses** its own `NewSession` + `startup.Exec` and delegates entirely to `tmuxinator start`.
647	
648	Config in `sesh.toml`:
649	```toml
650	[[session]]
651	name = "coding-agent"
652	path = "~"
653	tmuxinator = "coding-agent"
654	```
655	
656	Layout defined in `~/.config/tmuxinator/coding-agent.yml`:
657	```yaml
658	name: coding-agent
659	root: <%= @settings["root"] || "~" %>
660	on_project_start: tmux set-window-option main-pane-width 75%
661	windows:
662	  - editor:
663	      layout: main-vertical
664	      panes:
665	        - nvim
666	        - specstory run
667	  - monitor:
668	      panes:
669	        - btop
670	```
671	
672	**How it works:**
673	1. `sesh connect coding-agent` → sesh detects `tmuxinator` field
674	2. `connector/tmuxinator.go` calls `tmuxinator start coding-agent` directly
675	3. tmuxinator creates the entire session with all windows and panes
676	4. sesh then switches/attaches to the session
677	
678	**Pros:** cleanest integration, no empty window hack, sesh natively manages the lifecycle.
679	**Cons:** requires tmuxinator (`gem install tmuxinator`), Ruby dependency.
680	
681	**Requires:** `tmuxinator` (installed by `ruby_gem_tools` ansible role)
682	
683	### Approach A: Pure Shell Script (Fallback)
684	
685	For environments without tmuxp or tmuxinator, use raw tmux commands:
686	
687	```toml
688	[[session]]
689	name = "coding-agent"
690	path = "~"
691	startup_command = "tmux split-window -h -p 25 'specstory run' && tmux select-pane -L && tmux new-window -n monitor 'btop' && tmux select-window -t 1 && nvim"
692	```
693	
694	**Pros:** zero extra dependencies.
695	**Cons:** fragile, hard to read, hard to maintain.
696	
697	### Comparing Approaches
698	
699	Both `coding-agent` (tmuxp) and `coding-agent-mux` (tmuxinator) are configured in `sesh.toml` for A/B comparison:
700	
701	```bash
702	sesh connect coding-agent       # Approach B: tmuxp --append
703	sesh connect coding-agent-mux   # Approach C: tmuxinator native
704	```
705	
706	After testing, keep the one you prefer and remove/comment the other.
707	
708	## try + sesh Integration
709	
710	[try-cli](https://github.com/tobi/try) creates ephemeral project workspaces under `~/src/tries/`. A sesh wildcard automatically applies `startup_command = "nvim"` to any try project.
711	
712	### Usage
713	
714	```bash
715	# One-step: open project and start coding session
716	try-sesh some-project
717	try-sesh https://github.com/user/repo
718	
719	# Two-step: try first, then sesh
720	try some-project
721	shere                    # sesh connect "$PWD"
722	```
723	
724	The `try-sesh` function (alias: `tsesh`) runs `try` then immediately `sesh connect "$PWD"`. Session names follow `dir_length=2` convention: `tries/2026-04-14-some-project`.
725	
726	Source: `~/.config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh`
727	
728	## Upstream Issues (tmuxp)
729	
730	Sesh's `tmuxp` config field is documented in the schema and README, but **not implemented** in the source code. Relevant upstream issues:
731	
732	- [#87 - Add tmuxp support](https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/issues/87) -- Feature request to add tmuxp support. Status: Closed (marked "Done" on project board), but the implementation only added the field to the config struct/schema without wiring it into the connect/startup logic.
733	- [#198 - Built-in Window and Pane management](https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/issues/198) -- Request for native pane/window layout support (avoiding tmuxp/tmuxinator dependency). Status: Closed. Sesh v2.25 added basic window support but still no pane splits.
734	- [#188 - startup_command sent too early](https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/issues/188) -- Bug where startup_command is sent before the shell is ready. Status: Open. This can affect Approach B (`tmuxp load -a`) if there's a timing issue.
735	
736	## See also
737	
738	- [`docs/tools/worktrunk.md`](worktrunk.md) — git-worktree manager (`wt`)
739	  for the **branch** layer below sesh's project layer. The recommended
740	  three-tier mental model is **sesh = repo, wt = worktree within repo,
741	  tmux = pane within worktree**. See the
742	  [three-layer navigation](worktrunk.md#the-three-layer-navigation-sesh--wt--wtcd)
743	  and [tmux session per worktree](worktrunk.md#tmux-session-per-worktree-and-how-it-interacts-with-scodesvibe)

32	---
33	
34	## Mental model
35	
36	Three orthogonal axes of "what am I working on":
37	
38	| Axis | Tool | Granularity | Example |
39	|------|------|-------------|---------|
40	| **Project** | `sesh` (`shere`/`sroot`/`scode`/`svibe`) | One per repo / dir | `coding-agent/dotfiles` |
41	| **Branch** | `wt` (worktrunk) | One per parallel task within a project | `dotfiles.feat-x`, `dotfiles.fix-y` |
42	| **Pane** | `tmux` | Editor / agent / logs / git | nvim ▏ claude ▏ btop |
43	
44	Without worktrunk, parallel agents inside one repo step on each other
45	(checkout conflicts, stale `node_modules`, dev server port clashes). With
46	worktrunk, each agent gets its own checkout dir + branch + (optional) port +
47	(optional) DB, addressed by **branch name**.
48	
49	The **chezmoi-managed [`~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml`](../../dot_config/worktrunk/config.toml)**
50	in this repo is intentionally minimal — only aliases (`sw`/`ls`/`rm`/`cc`/`oc`)
51	are active. Hooks and LLM commits are commented as opt-in templates. Enable
52	them per-project as the need actually surfaces, not preemptively.
53	
54	---
55	
56	## Install & shell integration in this repo
57	
58	Auto-installed by the `devtools` ansible role:
59	
60	- **macOS**: `brew install worktrunk` (Homebrew formula).
61	- **Linux**: GitHub release musl tar.xz → `~/.local/bin/wt`. Ansible task
62	  ensures `xz-utils` is present and downloads
63	  `worktrunk-{x86_64,aarch64}-unknown-linux-musl.tar.xz` from
64	  `max-sixty/worktrunk`. Same fallback pattern as `sesh`.
65	
66	Shell integration lives in
67	[`dot_config/zsh/tools/37_worktrunk.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/tools/37_worktrunk.zsh):
68	
69	1. `eval "$(wt config shell init zsh)"` — wraps `wt` as a zsh function so
70	   `wt switch` actually `cd`s the parent shell. Same approach as
71	   starship/zoxide/direnv; **does not** call `wt config shell install`
72	   (which would edit `~/.zshrc` and fight chezmoi).
73	2. Auto-generates `~/.zfunc/_wt` on Linux only via `COMPLETE=zsh wt`
74	   (clap dynamic completion). On macOS the brew formula already ships
75	   `_wt` to `/opt/homebrew/share/zsh/site-functions/`, so the generator
76	   is skipped.
77	3. Defines `wtcd` — a small fzf-tmux helper for cross-worktree navigation
78	   that **doesn't** change tmux/sesh session (see next section).
79	
80	> **Why not just `wt config shell install`?** It writes a block to
81	> `~/.zshrc`, which chezmoi manages from `dot_zshrc.tmpl`. Every
82	> `chezmoi apply` would either undo it or perpetually report drift. The
83	> `eval "$(wt config shell init zsh)"` form gives the same wrapper without
84	> touching the rc file.
85	
86	---
87	
88	## The three-layer navigation: sesh + wt + wtcd
89	
90	The single biggest mental shift moving to worktrees is realising **moving
91	between worktrees is NOT the same as moving between projects**. Three
92	distinct keystrokes for three distinct intents:
93	
94	| I want to... | Use | What it does | Side effects |
95	|--------------|-----|--------------|--------------|
96	| Switch **project** | `Alt+S` (sesh picker), `sroot`, `scode` | Detaches from current tmux session, attaches to project's session | Full session swap |
97	| Switch **worktree** in current project | `wt switch <branch>` (or `wt sw`, or `wt switch` with no arg → picker) | `cd`s parent shell, runs hooks (`pre/post-start`) | New dir; if hook spawns tmux session for the worktree, you can attach to that |
98	| **Peek** at sibling worktree | `wtcd` (fzf picker) | `cd`s parent shell only | Stays in same tmux/sesh session; useful for diffing, copying files |
99	
100	### Concrete example
101	
102	```bash
103	# Morning: open the dotfiles project
104	$ sroot                              # → tmux session "dotfiles" (or whatever sesh names it)
105	
106	# Pick up where I left off on the worktrunk-docs branch
107	$ wt switch worktrunk-docs           # → cd to ../dotfiles.worktrunk-docs, post-start hooks run
108	
109	# Quick look at what main looks like right now (don't lose my place)
110	$ wtcd                               # → fzf shows all worktrees → pick "main" → cd, no session change
111	$ git log --oneline -5
112	$ cd -                               # back to worktrunk-docs
113	
114	# New parallel task: spin up a worktree + Claude in one go
115	$ wt cc fix-tmux-menu -- 'Investigate the popup menu height issue documented in pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md'
116	# Now there's a 2nd Claude running in ../dotfiles.fix-tmux-menu while I keep editing here.
117	```
118	
119	### The `wtcd` rationale
120	
121	`wt switch` is the right tool 95% of the time. But `wt switch` runs
122	`pre-start` / `post-start` hooks — start dev servers, copy ignored files,
123	spawn agents. That's heavy. When you only want to **look** at a sibling
124	worktree (find a file, copy a snippet, run `git log`), you don't want
125	hook side effects. `wtcd` skips hooks entirely; it's a pure `cd`.
126	
127	```zsh
128	# Defined in dot_config/zsh/tools/37_worktrunk.zsh
129	function wtcd() {
130	    local target
131	    target=$(wt list --format=json 2>/dev/null \
132	        | jq -r '.worktrees[].path' \
133	        | fzf-tmux -p 60%,40% --prompt='wt cd ❯ ') || return
134	    [[ -n "$target" ]] && cd -- "$target"
135	}
136	```
137	
138	Add a per-project keybinding to your tmux config if you use it a lot:
139	`bind-key W run-shell 'tmux send-keys "wtcd" Enter'`.
140	
141	---
142	
143	## Per-worktree Claude / OpenCode
144	
145	The single most useful pattern for parallel coding agents. Each worktree
146	runs its own agent in its own checkout dir; they can't collide on file
147	edits, branches, or git state.
148	
149	The aliases live in `~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml` (NOT in zsh — putting
150	them there means they also work from `wt switch`'s interactive picker, and
151	from any shell):
152	
153	```toml
154	[aliases]
155	cc = "wt switch --create --execute=claude"
156	oc = "wt switch --create --execute='opencode run'"
157	```
158	
159	Usage:
160	
161	```bash
162	# Three Claude agents working in parallel, one prompt each
163	wt cc add-auth        -- 'Add JWT auth middleware. See docs/auth.md for the schema.'
164	wt cc fix-pagination  -- 'Fix the off-by-one in /api/list. Repro in tests/pagination.test.ts:42.'
165	wt cc write-tests     -- 'Write integration tests for /api/checkout.'
166	
167	# Or with OpenCode
168	wt oc refactor-store  -- 'Migrate redux → zustand. Start with src/state/user.ts.'
169	
170	# Check on progress (markers come from the Claude/OpenCode plugins; 🤖 = working, 💬 = waiting)
171	wt list
172	#   Branch          Status   ...  Marker  ...
173	# @ main                            ^
174	# + add-auth        +   ↕↑    ↑3   🤖
175	# + fix-pagination  +   ↕↑    ↑1   💬     ← needs my input
176	# + write-tests     +   ↕     ↑2   🤖
177	
178	# Jump to the one waiting for input
179	wt switch fix-pagination
180	```
181	
182	### Caveats
183	
184	- `--execute` (`-x`) launches the agent **in the foreground** of the new
185	  shell. If you want the agent to run in a separate tmux session/window
186	  rather than blocking your prompt, use the [tmux session per worktree](#tmux-session-per-worktree-and-how-it-interacts-with-scodesvibe)
187	  pattern below — `wt switch -x 'tmux new-session -d ...'`.
188	- The `cc` / `oc` aliases assume you've already authenticated each agent
189	  CLI globally (`claude`/`opencode`). They inherit your shell environment.
190	- For SpecStory transcript capture (this repo's coding-agent overlay), the
191	  `scode`/`svibe` sesh helpers wrap the agent in `specstory run`; `wt cc`
192	  does NOT. If you want both, write your own alias:
193	  `wsc = "wt switch --create --execute='specstory run claude'"`.
194	
195	---
196	
197	## Per-worktree dev server (`hash_port`)
198	
199	Three parallel agents editing a Next.js app all want to run `npm run dev`.
200	With one repo: port collision, last one wins, the others crash. With
201	worktrunk + `hash_port`: each branch deterministically gets its own port
202	in the 10000-19999 range, derived from the branch name.
203	
204	Add to a project's local `.config/wt.toml` (per-project, not your global
205	config — different projects need different commands):
206	
207	```toml
208	[post-start]
209	server = "npm run dev -- --port {{ branch | hash_port }}"
210	
211	[list]
212	url = "http://localhost:{{ branch | hash_port }}"
213	
214	[pre-remove]
215	server = "lsof -ti :{{ branch | hash_port }} -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs kill 2>/dev/null || true"
216	```
217	
218	Now:
219	
220	```bash
221	wt cc fix-checkout-ui -- 'Make the checkout button green'
222	# post-start runs `npm run dev -- --port 14823` in the background
223	# Hook output goes to a log file; tail it with:
224	tail -f "$(wt config state logs get --hook=user:post-start:server)"
225	
226	wt list
227	# URL column shows http://localhost:14823 (clickable in iTerm/Ghostty)
228	# Port is deterministic — fix-checkout-ui ALWAYS gets 14823, on any machine
229	
230	# When done, wt remove cleans up:
231	wt remove fix-checkout-ui
232	# pre-remove kills the dev server before unlinking the worktree
233	```
234	
235	### Why this matters more than it sounds
236	
237	- **No port juggling**: you don't think about ports at all.
238	- **Bookmarkable**: the URL for `fix-checkout-ui` is stable across reboots
239	  and across machines (laptop and desktop both compute port 14823).
240	- **CORS / cookies**: each worktree is on its own port, so cookies don't
241	  leak between branches. Combine with the [Caddy subdomain
242	  pattern](https://worktrunk.dev/tips-patterns/#subdomain-routing-with-caddy)
243	  if you need clean URLs without ports.
244	- **Database isolation**: same `hash_port` trick works for spawning a
245	  per-worktree Postgres container — see
246	  [worktrunk.dev/tips-patterns#database-per-worktree](https://worktrunk.dev/tips-patterns/#database-per-worktree).
247	
248	> Project-local `.config/wt.toml` should usually be **committed** to the
249	> repo so all collaborators (and all your machines) share the same hooks.
250	> The chezmoi-managed `~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml` is for personal
251	>   defaults that apply across all repos.
252	
253	---
254	
255	## tmux session per worktree (and how it interacts with `scode`/`svibe`)
256	
257	Two competing models for "where does my coding-agent layout live":
258	
259	### Model A — `scode` / `svibe` per **project** (current default)
260	
261	[`sesh-code`/`sesh-vibe`](sesh.md) (aliases `scode`/`svibe`) create one
262	tmux session **per repo**, named `coding-agent/<repo>` or `vibe/<repo>`,
263	with a fixed nvim + agent + lazygit layout. All worktrees of that repo
264	share the same session — you `wt switch` inside it to move between them.
265	
266	✅ **Best for**: solo coding, sequential work on different branches, low
267	parallel agent count.
268	❌ **Limitation**: only one Claude/OpenCode pane visible at a time. If
269	you have 5 parallel agents, you can't watch them all simultaneously.
270	
271	### Model B — tmux session per **worktree**
272	
273	Spin up a dedicated tmux session for each worktree, with its own multi-pane
274	layout. Worktrunk's official recipe:
275	
276	```toml
277	# project's .config/wt.toml
278	[pre-start]
279	tmux = """
280	S={{ branch | sanitize }}
281	W={{ worktree_path }}
282	tmux new-session -d -s "$S" -c "$W" -n dev
283	tmux split-window -h -t "$S:dev" -c "$W"
284	tmux split-window -v -t "$S:dev.0" -c "$W"
285	tmux split-window -v -t "$S:dev.2" -c "$W"
286	tmux send-keys -t "$S:dev.1" 'npm run backend' Enter
287	tmux send-keys -t "$S:dev.2" 'claude' Enter
288	tmux send-keys -t "$S:dev.3" 'npm run frontend' Enter
289	tmux select-pane -t "$S:dev.0"
290	"""
291	
292	[pre-remove]
293	tmux = "tmux kill-session -t {{ branch | sanitize }} 2>/dev/null || true"
294	```
295	
296	Then `wt switch --create feature -x 'tmux attach -t {{ branch | sanitize }}'`
297	creates the worktree, runs the layout, and attaches you to the new session.
298	
299	✅ **Best for**: 3+ parallel agents, dashboard-style overview,
300	worktree-specific services (backend/frontend/db each in their own pane).
301	❌ **Limitation**: tmux session list grows fast — pair with `sesh` to
302	filter (sesh picks up tmux sessions automatically). Also: heavier
303	cold-start.
304	
305	### How they interact
306	
307	The two models are **not mutually exclusive**:
308	
309	- Use `scode` to enter the project (one persistent session for the editor
310	  + git overview).
311	- Use Model B's `pre-start` hook to spawn a **separate** session per
312	  worktree containing only the agent + dev servers.
313	- Switch between them via `Alt+S` (sesh picker shows both
314	  `coding-agent/dotfiles` AND `dotfiles.feat-x`, `dotfiles.feat-y`...).
315	- Detach the agent session, leave it running. Re-attach later with sesh.
316	
317	### Sesh + wt session naming convention
318	
319	If you adopt Model B, recommend prefixing tmux session names so sesh's
320	picker groups them sensibly:
321	
322	```toml
323	[pre-start]
324	tmux = "tmux new-session -d -s 'wt/{{ repo }}/{{ branch | sanitize }}' ..."
325	```
326	
327	Now `Alt+S` shows:
328	
329	```
330	coding-agent/dotfiles      ← scode session (editor)
331	wt/dotfiles/feat-x         ← wt session (agent A)
332	wt/dotfiles/feat-y         ← wt session (agent B)
333	wt/dotfiles/fix-z          ← wt session (agent C)
334	```
335	
336	…all greppable by typing `wt/dotfiles/` in fzf.
337	
338	---
339	
340	## Cold-start elimination
341	
342	A new worktree is a fresh checkout — no `node_modules/`, no `target/`,
343	no `.env`, no build cache. For a Rust or pnpm project, that's a 60-180s
344	penalty per `wt switch --create`. Two complementary mitigations:
345	
346	### `wt step copy-ignored`
347	
348	Copies all gitignored files from the source worktree into the new one.
349	Add to project's `.config/wt.toml`:
350	
351	```toml
352	[post-start]
353	copy = "wt step copy-ignored"
354	```
355	
356	For projects with huge ignored directories you don't want to copy (e.g.
357	`coverage/`, `dist/`, OS junk), create `.worktreeinclude` listing what
358	**should** be copied — files must be both gitignored AND listed.
359	
360	### Sequenced pipelines
361	
362	When `pnpm install` needs to see the copied `node_modules/` first,
363	sequence with the `[[hook]]` array form (`[[…]]` = ordered pipeline,
364	`[…]` = parallel):
365	
366	```toml
367	[[post-start]]
368	copy = "wt step copy-ignored"
369	
370	[[post-start]]
371	install = "pnpm install"   # reuses cached packages from copied node_modules
372	```
373	
374	### When the agent needs files immediately
375	
376	If `--execute claude` needs `.env` to exist before launch, use `pre-start`
377	instead of `post-start`:
378	
379	```toml
380	[pre-start]
381	copy = "wt step copy-ignored"
382	```
383	
384	---
385	
386	## Merge & cleanup flow
387	
388	Worktrunk replaces the multi-step "commit → push → merge → switch back →
389	remove worktree → delete branch" dance with one command:
390	
391	```bash
392	wt merge main
393	# 1. (optional) generates LLM commit message from staged diff
394	# 2. commits, rebases onto main, fast-forwards merge
395	# 3. switches you back to main worktree
396	# 4. background-removes the feature worktree + branch
397	```
398	
399	What this means in practice with parallel agents:
400	
401	```bash
402	# Three agents finished. Review their diffs in the picker first:
403	wt switch              # interactive picker shows live diff/log preview, tab between worktrees
404	
405	# Pick winner #1, merge it
406	wt merge main
407	
408	# Pick winner #2, but want manual commit message for this one (override):
409	wt mc                  # if you set up the editor-override alias from `Manual commit messages`
410	                       # in https://worktrunk.dev/tips-patterns/
411	
412	# Reject #3 — close without merging
413	wt switch reject-this-one
414	wt remove              # discards branch + worktree (will warn if unmerged commits)
415	```
416	
417	### Per-merge cleanup hooks
418	
419	Add per-project `pre-merge` (run validation before letting bad code in)
420	and `post-merge` (deploy, notify):
421	
422	```toml
423	[[pre-merge]]
424	test = "npm test"
425	build = "npm run build"
426	
427	[post-merge]
428	deploy = """
429	if [ {{ target }} = main ]; then npm run deploy:production; fi
430	"""
431	```
432	
433	`pre-merge` runs **once per merge** (after rebase). `pre-commit` runs
434	**per squashed commit** during the merge — put fast checks (lint,
435	typecheck) there and slow ones (full test suite) in `pre-merge`.
436	
437	---
438	
439	## LLM commit messages — when to bother
440	
441	`wt merge` can pipe the staged diff to a command that returns a commit
442	message on stdout. Three configurations, pick at most one in
443	`~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml`:
444	
445	| Strategy | When | Config |
446	|----------|------|--------|
447	| **Manual editor** | Solo work, you're the one with context | `command = '''f=$(mktemp); printf '\n\n' > "$f"; sed 's/^/# /' >> "$f"; ${EDITOR:-vi} "$f" < /dev/tty > /dev/tty; grep -v '^#' "$f"'''` |
448	| **Claude headless** | Agent-driven workflow, want the agent to also write the message | `command = "claude -p"` |
449	| **OpenCode** | Same as Claude but with OpenCode | `command = "opencode run"` |
450	
451	All three currently sit **commented out** in this repo's
452	[`dot_config/worktrunk/config.toml`](../../dot_config/worktrunk/config.toml).
453	Reasoning: I haven't decided yet whether the LLM-generated messages are
454	better than what a coding agent already produced before staging. Plan is
455	to enable `claude -p` once I've used `wt merge` enough to feel the friction.
456	
457	### Editor override per-merge
458	
459	Keep LLM as default but use editor for one specific merge:
460	
461	```toml
462	[aliases]
463	mc = '''WORKTRUNK_COMMIT__GENERATION__COMMAND='f=$(mktemp); printf "\n\n" > "$f"; sed "s/^/# /" >> "$f"; ${EDITOR:-vi} "$f" < /dev/tty > /dev/tty; grep -v "^#" "$f"' wt merge'''
464	```
465	
466	Then `wt merge` uses Claude, `wt mc` opens `$EDITOR`.
467	
468	### Branch summaries
469	
470	With LLM commits enabled, also turn on `summary = true` to get one-line
471	LLM-generated branch summaries in `wt list --full` and the picker (tab 5):
472	
473	```toml
474	[list]
475	summary = true
476	```
477	
478	---
479	
480	## Recipes I haven't enabled yet
481	
482	Documented for "future me" — copy-paste targets when the need arises.
483	All from [worktrunk.dev/tips-patterns](https://worktrunk.dev/tips-patterns/).
484	
485	| Recipe | Trigger to enable |
486	|--------|-------------------|
487	| **Database per worktree** (Postgres container, `hash_port` for the DB port, `vars` to coordinate names) | First time I want to test schema migrations on a feature branch without trashing the main DB |
488	| **Caddy subdomain routing** (`feat-x.dotfiles.localhost` instead of `:14823`) | First time cookies / CORS bites me on a port-based dev URL |
489	| **Bare repo layout** (`<project>/.git` + `<project>/<branch>/`) | New project where I want symmetric branch dirs from day one |
490	| **Stacked branches** (`wt switch --create part2 --base=@`) | First time I want to break a big PR into a stack |
491	| **Agent handoff** (one agent spawns another in a detached tmux session) | First time I'm running an agent long enough to want it to delegate |
492	| **CI status in `wt list`** (`wt list --full --branches`) | First time I'm juggling enough open PRs to lose track of which CI is green |
493

```text
1	# SSH Agent
2	
3	Automatic SSH agent management with Bitwarden-first fallback to `ssh-agent`.
4	
5	**Config file**: `~/.config/zsh/tools/94_ssh_agent.zsh`
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Concepts
10	
11	### What is an SSH key pair?
12	
13	SSH uses asymmetric cryptography — a **private key** (kept secret) and a **public key** (shared freely).
14	
15	```
16	~/.ssh/id_ed25519      ← private key  (never share this)
17	~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub  ← public key   (paste into servers / GitHub)
18	```
19	
20	When you connect to a server, SSH proves your identity by doing a cryptographic challenge using your private key. The server verifies it with your public key in `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`.
21	
22	**Key types** (prefer ed25519 for new keys):
23	
24	| Type | Strength | Notes |
25	|------|----------|-------|
26	| `ed25519` | Modern, recommended | Small key, fast, secure |
27	| `rsa` (4096-bit) | Widely compatible | Older; still fine if already in use |
28	| `ecdsa` | Good | Less common |
29	
30	Generate a new key:
31	```bash
32	ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your@email.com"
33	# Saves to ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 and ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
34	```
35	
36	### What is a passphrase?
37	
38	A passphrase encrypts your private key file on disk. Without it, anyone who gets the file can use it.
39	
40	**Trade-off:**
41	- No passphrase: convenient, but risky if your machine is compromised
42	- With passphrase: secure, but SSH asks for it every time you use the key — unless you use an **SSH agent**
43	
44	### What is an SSH agent?
45	
46	An SSH agent is a background process that holds your **decrypted private keys in memory**. When SSH needs to sign a challenge, it asks the agent — so you only enter the passphrase **once per login session**, not every connection.
47	
48	```
49	┌───────────┐  challenge  ┌───────────────┐  sign  ┌─────────────┐
50	│  ssh/git  │ ──────────▶ │   ssh-agent   │ ──────▶ │  decrypted  │
51	│  client   │ ◀────────── │  (in memory)  │         │   key copy  │
52	└───────────┘  signature  └───────────────┘         └─────────────┘
53	        ↑
54	        └── "Connected!"
55	```
56	
57	Communication happens through a **Unix socket** pointed to by `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`:
58	
59	```bash
60	echo $SSH_AUTH_SOCK    # e.g. /run/user/1000/ssh-agent/agent.sock
61	ssh-add -l             # list keys currently held by the agent
62	ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa  # manually add a key (will ask for passphrase once)
63	```
64	
65	### How auto-loading keys works (and the passphrase prompt)
66	
67	When the fallback `ssh-agent` starts and has no keys, `_maybe_add_keys` in
68	`94_ssh_agent.zsh` tries to add common key files automatically:
69	
70	```zsh
71	# key_names list: id_ed25519, id_rsa, id_ecdsa, jingle
72	SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never ssh-add -q "$kf" 2>/dev/null
73	```
74	
75	**`SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never`** tells ssh-add: "don't prompt for a passphrase at
76	all — if you need one, just fail silently." This means:
77	
78	- Keys **without** a passphrase → auto-loaded into the agent silently
79	- Keys **with** a passphrase → skipped (no prompt at login)
80	
81	> **Why not `</dev/null`?** `ssh-add` bypasses stdin and opens `/dev/tty` directly
82	> for passphrase input, so redirecting stdin has no effect. `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE`
83	> is the correct mechanism (available since OpenSSH 8.4, 2020).
84	
85	**To manually load a key with a passphrase** (once per session):
86	```bash
87	ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa
88	# Enter passphrase: ••••••
89	# The key is now in the agent for the rest of this login session
90	```
91	
92	---
93	
94	## How It Works
95	
96	Every new interactive shell runs the following fallback chain:
97	
98	```
99	1. Bitwarden SSH agent socket?  ──yes──▶  Use it (export SSH_AUTH_SOCK)
100	         │ no
101	         ▼
102	2. Existing SSH_AUTH_SOCK works? ──yes──▶  Keep it (forwarded agent, systemd, gnome-keyring, etc.)
103	         │ no
104	         ▼
105	3. Persistent ssh-agent         ──────▶  Spawn once, reuse across shells
106	         │                                Auto-load passphrase-free keys from ~/.ssh/
107	         ▼
108	   SSH_AUTH_SOCK is set and ready
109	```
110	
111	### Step 1: Bitwarden SSH Agent
112	
113	Iterates known Bitwarden socket paths (see [bitwarden_ssh_agent.md](../tutorials/bitwarden_ssh_agent.md#2-configure-ssh_auth_sock) for the full table).
114	Each candidate is probed with a **2-second timeout** on `ssh-add -l`:
115	
116	- Socket doesn't exist (`-S` test fails) → skip immediately
117	- Socket exists but `ssh-add -l` **times out** (agent hung) → skip
118	- Socket responds with "agent refused operation" (Bitwarden locked/disabled) → skip
119	- Socket responds with keys or "no identities" → **use it**
120	
121	This means a locked/crashed Bitwarden won't block shell startup.
122	
123	### Step 2: Existing Agent
124	
125	Respects any `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` already set by the environment:
126	- SSH agent forwarding (`ssh -A`)
127	- systemd `ssh-agent.service`
128	- GNOME Keyring
129	- GPG agent with SSH support
130	
131	If the current socket is valid and responding, it is kept as-is.
132	
133	### Step 3: Persistent ssh-agent
134	
135	When neither Bitwarden nor an existing agent is available, a standard `ssh-agent` is spawned with a **fixed socket path**:
136	
137	```
138	$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ssh-agent/agent.sock   (Linux, typical: /run/user/1000/ssh-agent/)
139	$HOME/.cache/ssh-agent/agent.sock        (fallback when XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unset)
140	```
141	
142	Key properties:
143	- **One agent per user**: all shells share the same socket, no orphan agents.
144	- **Survives shell restarts**: opening a new terminal reuses the existing agent.
145	- **Auto-loads keys**: on first use (when agent has no identities), automatically runs `ssh-add` for common key names: `id_ed25519`, `id_rsa`, `id_ecdsa`, `jingle`. Keys with passphrases are skipped silently.
146	
147	---
148	
149	## SSH Config Basics
150	
151	`~/.ssh/config` lets you define aliases and per-host settings so you don't have to
152	type long options every time.
153	
154	### Structure
155	
156	```ssh-config
157	Host <alias>
158	    HostName <real hostname or IP>
159	    User <username>
160	    Port <port>          # default: 22
161	    IdentityFile <path>  # which key to use
162	```
163	
164	### Common patterns
165	
166	#### Simple alias
167	
168	```ssh-config
169	Host rpi
170	    HostName 100.64.157.9   # Tailscale IP or domain
171	    User keithkslee
172	```
173	
174	Now `ssh rpi` works instead of `ssh keithkslee@100.64.157.9`.
175	
176	#### Specify which key to use
177	
178	```ssh-config
179	Host github.com
180	    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
181	    IdentitiesOnly yes   # don't try other agent keys
182	```
183	
184	`IdentitiesOnly yes` prevents SSH from offering every key in the agent. Useful when
185	a server rejects too many auth attempts.
186	
187	#### Agent forwarding
188	
189	```ssh-config
190	Host rpi
191	    HostName 100.64.157.9
192	    User keithkslee
193	    ForwardAgent yes   # your local agent keys work on the remote host
194	```
195	
196	With `ForwardAgent yes`, once you're on the remote machine, you can `git pull`,
197	`ssh` to other servers, etc. using your local keys — **without copying private
198	keys to the remote machine**.
199	
200	> **Security note**: only forward your agent to hosts you trust. Anyone with root
201	> on the remote machine can use your forwarded agent socket.
202	
203	#### Jump host (ProxyJump)
204	
205	If a server is only reachable through a bastion/jump host:
206	
207	```ssh-config
208	Host bastion
209	    HostName bastion.example.com
210	    User admin
211	
212	Host internal-server
213	    HostName 10.0.0.5
214	    User app
215	    ProxyJump bastion   # SSH through bastion automatically
216	```
217	
218	`ssh internal-server` will transparently connect through `bastion`.
219	
220	#### Common options reference
221	
222	| Option | What it does |
223	|--------|-------------|
224	| `HostName` | Real hostname/IP (alias goes in `Host`) |
225	| `User` | Remote username |
226	| `Port` | SSH port (default 22) |
227	| `IdentityFile` | Path to private key (`~/.ssh/id_ed25519`) |
228	| `IdentitiesOnly yes` | Only use specified keys, not all agent keys |
229	| `ForwardAgent yes` | Forward local SSH agent to remote |
230	| `ProxyJump <host>` | Connect through a jump host |
231	| `ServerAliveInterval 60` | Send keepalive every 60s (prevents timeout) |
232	| `StrictHostKeyChecking no` | Skip host key verification (use for known-safe internal hosts only) |
233	
234	---
235	
236	## Debugging
237	
238	```bash
239	# Which agent is active?
240	echo $SSH_AUTH_SOCK
241	
242	# Is the agent responding?
243	ssh-add -l
244	
245	# Which strategy was selected?
246	# Re-source with verbose output:
247	zsh -x -c 'source ~/.config/zsh/tools/94_ssh_agent.zsh' 2>&1 | grep SSH_AUTH_SOCK
248	
249	# Force fallback (skip Bitwarden) for testing:
250	unset SSH_AUTH_SOCK
251	source ~/.config/zsh/tools/94_ssh_agent.zsh
252	echo $SSH_AUTH_SOCK
253	
254	# Verbose SSH connection (shows which key is being tried)
255	ssh -v user@host
256	ssh -vvv user@host  # more verbose
257	```
258	
259	## Troubleshooting
260	
261	| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
262	|---|---|---|
263	| `ssh-add -l` → "Could not open connection" | No agent running, script didn't execute | Check `source ~/.config/zsh/tools/94_ssh_agent.zsh` runs without error |
264	| Bitwarden socket exists but fallback is used | Bitwarden locked or agent disabled | Unlock Bitwarden, enable SSH agent in **Settings** |
265	| Multiple ssh-agent processes | Old agents from before this script | `pkill ssh-agent` then open a new shell |
266	| Keys not auto-loaded | Key filename not in the list | Add the filename to `key_names` array in `94_ssh_agent.zsh` |
267	| Agent dies after reboot | XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is tmpfs (expected) | Normal — agent respawns on next shell |
268	| Passphrase prompt appears at login | Key with passphrase in `~/.ssh/`, OpenSSH < 8.4 | `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never` requires OpenSSH 8.4+; upgrade or remove the key from `key_names` |
269	| `Permission denied (publickey)` | Public key not in server's `authorized_keys` | Run `ssh-copy-id user@host` or append `~/.ssh/id_*.pub` to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` on server |
270	| SSH asks for password despite having a key | Wrong key / key not in agent | `ssh-add -l` to check; `ssh -v user@host` to trace |
271	
272	## Customization
273	
274	### Adding more key files to auto-load
275	
276	Edit the `key_names` array in `94_ssh_agent.zsh`:
277	
278	```zsh
279	local -a key_names=(id_ed25519 id_rsa id_ecdsa jingle my_work_key)
280	```
281	
282	### Disabling auto-load entirely
283	
284	Comment out the `_maybe_add_keys` call inside `_fallback_ssh_agent`.
285	
286	### Using systemd ssh-agent instead of the built-in fallback
287	
288	If you prefer systemd to manage the agent:
289	
290	```bash
291	# Create the service
292	systemctl --user enable --now ssh-agent
293	
294	# Set SSH_AUTH_SOCK in environment
295	echo 'export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ssh-agent.socket"' >> ~/.zshrc.adhoc
296	```
297	
298	The fallback script's step 2 will detect this and skip step 3.
299	
300	## Related
301	
302	- [Bitwarden SSH Agent tutorial](../tutorials/bitwarden_ssh_agent.md) — full setup guide for Bitwarden as agent
303	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/94_ssh_agent.zsh` — SSH agent auto-detection and fallback
304	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` — Bitwarden CLI zsh completion
305
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Starship Prompt
2	
3	[Starship](https://starship.rs/) is a cross-shell prompt written in Rust, replacing the default oh-my-zsh `robbyrussell` theme.
4	
5	- **Config file**: `~/.config/starship.toml` (chezmoi source: `dot_config/starship.toml`)
6	- **ZSH init**: `~/.config/zsh/tools/01_starship.zsh`
7	- **Ansible role**: `starship` (brew on macOS, official installer on Linux, user-level fallback for noRoot)
8	- **Dependencies**: Nerd Fonts (Hack Nerd Font installed by `nerdfonts` role)
9	
10	## Quick Start
11	
12	```bash
13	chezmoi apply     # deploys config + installs starship via ansible
14	exec zsh          # reload shell to see the new prompt
15	```
16	
17	## Presets
18	
19	Starship ships with built-in presets that change the entire look:
20	
21	```bash
22	# List all available presets
23	starship preset --list
24	
25	# Apply a preset (overwrites starship.toml)
26	starship preset nerd-font-symbols -o ~/.config/starship.toml    # full Nerd Font icons
27	starship preset pastel-powerline -o ~/.config/starship.toml      # Powerline-style segments
28	starship preset tokyo-night -o ~/.config/starship.toml           # dark color scheme
29	starship preset plain-text-symbols -o ~/.config/starship.toml    # ASCII fallback (no Nerd Fonts)
30	```
31	
32	After trying a preset, run `chezmoi apply` to restore the chezmoi-managed version.
33	
34	Preview all presets: <https://starship.rs/presets/>
35	
36	## Module Configuration
37	
38	Modules control what information appears in the prompt. Edit `dot_config/starship.toml` (or `chezmoi edit ~/.config/starship.toml`).
39	
40	### Commonly Useful Modules
41	
42	| Module | Description | Default |
43	|--------|-------------|---------|
44	| `[directory]` | Current path | enabled, truncated to 3 levels |
45	| `[git_branch]` | Git branch name | enabled |
46	| `[git_status]` | Dirty/staged/ahead/behind | enabled |
47	| `[python]` | Python version + virtualenv | enabled (auto-detected) |
48	| `[nodejs]` | Node.js version | enabled (auto-detected) |
49	| `[rust]` | Rust version | enabled (auto-detected) |
50	| `[conda]` | Conda environment name | enabled (works with `CONDA_CHANGEPS1=false`) |
51	| `[docker_context]` | Docker context | enabled |
52	| `[cmd_duration]` | Command execution time | enabled, shows when > 2s |
53	| `[character]` | Prompt character (`❯`) | green on success, red on error |
54	
55	### Disabled by Default (Worth Enabling)
56	
57	```toml
58	# Show clock on the right
59	[time]
60	disabled = false
61	format = "[$time]($style) "
62	time_format = "%H:%M"
63	
64	# Show username/hostname (auto-shows over SSH)
65	[username]
66	show_always = false    # only show over SSH
67	
68	[hostname]
69	ssh_only = true
70	
71	# Kubernetes context
72	[kubernetes]
73	disabled = false
74	
75	# Memory usage
76	[memory_usage]
77	disabled = false
78	threshold = 75         # only show when usage > 75%
79	
80	# Battery (laptop)
81	[battery]
82	disabled = false
83	
84	# AWS / GCP / Azure profile
85	[aws]
86	[gcloud]
87	[azure]
88	```
89	
90	### Command Duration
91	
92	```toml
93	[cmd_duration]
94	min_time = 2_000           # show when command takes > 2 seconds
95	format = "took [$duration]($style) "
96	show_milliseconds = false
97	```
98	
99	## Prompt Layout
100	
101	### Two-Line Prompt
102	
103	The default config uses `add_newline = true` which adds a blank line between prompts. The `[line_break]` module separates info from the input line:
104	
105	```toml
106	# Info on line 1, input cursor on line 2
107	format = """
108	$username\
109	$hostname\
110	$directory\
111	$git_branch\
112	$git_status\
113	$python\
114	$nodejs\
115	$rust\
116	$conda\
117	$line_break\
118	$character"""
119	```
120	
121	### Right-Side Prompt
122	
123	Display less critical info on the right edge of the terminal:
124	
125	```toml
126	right_format = "$time$cmd_duration"
127	```
128	
129	## Custom Modules
130	
131	Create custom modules for project-specific or workflow-specific info:
132	
133	```toml
134	# Show current tmux session name
135	[custom.tmux]
136	command = "tmux display-message -p '#S' 2>/dev/null"
137	when = "test -n \"$TMUX\""
138	format = "[$output]($style) "
139	style = "bold cyan"
140	
141	# Show active pueue task count
142	[custom.pueue]
143	command = "pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq '[.tasks[] | select(.status == \"Running\")] | length'"
144	when = "command -v pueue"
145	format = "[$output tasks]($style) "
146	style = "yellow"
147	```
148	
149	## Integration Notes
150	
151	- **oh-my-zsh**: Still loaded for plugins (git aliases, autosuggestions, syntax-highlighting). Only the theme is disabled (`ZSH_THEME=""`).
152	- **Conda**: `CONDA_CHANGEPS1=false` is set in `04_conda_mamba.zsh`, so starship's `[conda]` module handles env display.
153	- **tmux2k**: tmux status bar is independent of starship; no conflicts.
154	- **Nerd Fonts**: Hack Nerd Font Mono is configured in Alacritty. If using a terminal without Nerd Fonts (e.g., SSH to ubuntu_server), apply the `plain-text-symbols` preset.
155	
156	## Suggested Experience Order
157	
158	1. **Apply and verify** — `chezmoi apply && exec zsh` (5 min)
159	2. **Try presets** — find a visual base you like (10 min)
160	3. **Tune modules** — add `cmd_duration`, `time`, etc. (15 min)
161	4. **Adjust layout** — two-line prompt, right_format (as needed)
162	5. **Custom modules** — extend for your workflow (advanced)
163	
164	Steps 1-2 are enough for daily use. Steps 3-5 can be done incrementally.
165	
166	## References
167	
168	- Configuration: <https://starship.rs/config/>
169	- All presets: <https://starship.rs/presets/>
170	- All modules: <https://starship.rs/config/#prompt>
171
```
</details></tool-use>
